items.title: Starting A^el expression
items.description: States the previous result $A^{el} = -\frac{k_B T V}{12\pi}\kappa^3$ or equivalently $\frac{V\beta^{1/2}}{12\pi}\left(\sum_j \frac{q_j^2 C_j}{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r}\right)^{3/2}$ as the starting free energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) requires using the result for A^el from the previous problem as the starting point for differentiation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps straight to the final formula without showing where the derivation begins.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Entry point for the entire derivation; without it the partial derivative cannot be formed.

items.title: Partial derivative links A^el to mu
items.description: Computes the partial derivative $\left(\frac{\partial A^{el}}{\partial N_j}\right)_{T,V}$ as the link between the electrostatic free energy and $\mu_j^{el}$.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) asks to use the per-particle relation $\mu_j^{el} = (\partial A^{el}/\partial N_j)_{T,V} = k_B T \ln \gamma_j^{el}$.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the target equation without performing the derivative step.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate step connecting thermodynamic potential to activity coefficient.

items.title: Kappa depends on N_j
items.description: Uses $\kappa^2 = \frac{1}{\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r k_B T}\frac{\sum_i N_i q_i^2}{V}$ or an equivalent expression showing that $\kappa$ depends on $N_j$.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'κ treated as constant' identifies that forgetting the N_j dependence of κ through the ionic strength sum is a high-severity error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats κ as a constant when differentiating, causing the derivative to vanish or be incorrect.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Pitfall-mined: responses that treat $\kappa$ as constant when differentiating produce wrong results.

items.title: Derivative of kappa squared
items.description: States $\partial \kappa^2 / \partial N_j = q_j^2/(\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r k_B T V)$ obtained by differentiating the $\sum_i N_i q_i^2$ term with respect to $N_j$.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer shows the differentiation of the sum $\sum_j q_j^2 C_j$ with respect to $N_j$, yielding the $q_j^2/(\varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r V)$ factor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that produces the wrong derivative by mishandling the V or charge factors in the ionic strength.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate; incorrect derivative propagates errors to the final expression.

items.title: Chain rule 3/2 factor
items.description: Applies the chain rule through $\kappa^3 = (\kappa^2)^{3/2}$ yielding a factor of $\frac{3}{2}\kappa$ when differentiating with respect to $N_j$.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Chain rule factor lost' warns that differentiating κ³ as $3κ^2$ instead of via $(κ^2)^{3/2}$ gives the wrong numerical coefficient.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses $3\kappa^2$ instead of $\frac{3}{2}\kappa$, yielding $1/(12\pi)$ or $1/(4\pi)$ instead of $1/(8\pi)$.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Pitfall-mined: omitting the chain rule factor is a common differentiation error in this step.

items.title: Volume cancellation
items.description: Shows that the prefactor $V$ in $A^{el}$ cancels the $1/V$ from $\partial \kappa^2/\partial N_j$, leaving a volume-independent $\mu_j^{el}$ with no spurious $V$ or $1/V$ factors.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'V cancellation dropped' identifies that losing track of the three V factors leads to spurious volume dependence.
provenance.discriminates: A response with leftover $V$ or $1/V$ factors in the final expression for $\mu_j^{el}$.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Pitfall-mined: leftover volume factors are a discriminative error; correct cancellation is required.

items.title: Part (a) final result
items.description: Obtains $k_B T \ln \gamma_j^{el} = -\frac{\kappa q_j^2}{8\pi \varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r}$ as the final result of the first derivation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) target equation specifies this exact result.
provenance.discriminates: A response with a wrong sign, wrong numerical factor, or wrong charge dependence in the single-ion activity coefficient.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly requested quantity; correctness of subsequent steps depends on it.

items.title: Logarithm of gamma_pm formula
items.description: Takes the logarithm of the formula $\gamma_{\pm}^z = \gamma_+^{v_+}\gamma_-^{v_-}$ with $z = v_+ + v_-$ to obtain $\ln\gamma_{\pm} = \frac{v_+\ln\gamma_+ + v_-\ln\gamma_-}{v_+ + v_-}$.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Mean γ exponent wrong' warns that failing to recognize $z = v_+ + v_-$ leads to a missing or incorrect divisor.
provenance.discriminates: A response using $z = 1$, $z = v_+ v_-$, or omitting the root entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Pitfall-mined: wrong $z$ exponent corrupts the divisor; this step is gateway to part (b).

items.title: Substitute part (a) result
items.description: Substitutes $\ln\gamma_j = -\frac{\kappa q_j^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r k_BT}$ for $j = +$ and $j = -$ into the expression for $\ln\gamma_{\pm}$.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly substitutes the individual-ion result into $v_+ \ln \gamma_+ + v_- \ln \gamma_-$ to obtain the mean coefficient expression.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the final $\ln \gamma_{\pm}$ without connecting it to the individual-ion coefficients from part (a).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects part (a) to part (b); without substitution the intermediate result is unused.

items.title: Part (b) final result
items.description: Arrives at $\ln\gamma_{\pm} = -\left(\frac{v_+q_+^2 + v_-q_-^2}{v_+ + v_-}\right)\frac{\kappa}{8\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r k_BT}$ as the result of the second derivation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (b) target equation specifies this exact intermediate result.
provenance.discriminates: A response missing the $(v_+ + v_-)$ divisor or with incorrect charge/stoichiometry grouping.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly requested quantity; essential checkpoint before the electroneutrality rewrite.

items.title: Electroneutrality condition
items.description: Applies the electroneutrality condition $v_+q_+ + v_-q_- = 0$ (equivalently $v_+q_+ = -v_-q_-$ with $q_- < 0$) to simplify the numerator $v_+q_+^2 + v_-q_-^2$.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Electroneutrality sign flip' warns that writing $v_+ q_+ = v_- q_-$ instead of $v_+ q_+ = -v_- q_-$ corrupts the simplification.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses $v_+ q_+ = v_- q_-$, producing the wrong sign or failing to simplify to $|q_+ q_-|$.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Pitfall-mined: sign errors in electroneutrality corrupt the final simplification.

items.title: Numerator simplification
items.description: Shows that $v_+q_+^2 + v_-q_-^2 = (v_+ + v_-)|q_+q_-|$ using the electroneutrality condition.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts arrived at this simplification via different algebraic paths; the reference uses factoring through $q_+$, but the key checkable result is the same.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose algebra fails to produce the $|q_+ q_-|$ factor or leaves the numerator unsimplified.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key algebraic step; divergent responses that fail here cannot reach the final form.

items.title: Part (c) final result
items.description: Arrives at $\ln\gamma_{\pm} = -|q_+q_-|\frac{\kappa}{8\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r k_BT}$ in agreement with Equation 25.49.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (c) target equation specifies this exact final result, and the question states it should agree with Equation 25.49.
provenance.discriminates: A response with a sign error, missing absolute value, or incorrect prefactor in the final mean activity coefficient.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly requested final quantity; the target result of the entire derivation.

items.title: Avoids dropped negative sign
items.description: Avoids dropping the overall negative sign from $A^{el}$ when differentiating, which would incorrectly produce $k_BT\ln\gamma_j = +\frac{\kappa q_j^2}{8\pi\varepsilon_0\varepsilon_r}$ instead of the negative result.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Sign from A^el' (severity: high) identifies that the leading minus sign is easily lost in the chain-rule algebra.
provenance.discriminates: A response with a positive electrostatic chemical potential, implying activity coefficients greater than 1.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed pitfall; sign error destroys agreement with Equation 25.49.

items.title: Avoids per-mole per-particle mix
items.description: Avoids mixing per-mole quantities ($R$, $n_j$) with per-particle quantities ($k_BT$, $N_j$) when computing the partial derivative $\partial A^{el}/\partial N_j$.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Per-mole vs per-particle' (severity: medium) warns that the question gives both forms and $R$ may be carried over from habit.
provenance.discriminates: A response with an $N_A$ factor discrepancy between the left and right sides of the target equation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed pitfall; unit inconsistency produces wrong prefactors throughout.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Prefactor N/π
items.description: The final expression for n(E) contains the prefactor N/π after the lattice constant a, which is real, cancels via dk=dx/a in the substitution x=ka.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires the correct closed-form n(E); the reference answer has prefactor N/π with no extra a.
provenance.discriminates: A response that leaves Na/π or any incorrect prefactor in the final n(E).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result anchor; a must cancel. No validation data but structurally essential.

items.title: Square-root denominator
items.description: The final expression for n(E) contains √(4J²−(E−E_s)²) in the denominator or the equivalent form J√(1−((E−E_s)/(2J))²).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer has 1/[J√(1−((E−E_s)/(2J))²)], algebraically equivalent to 1/√(4J²−(E−E_s)²).
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes a linear denominator, drops the square root, or places E−E_s outside the sqrt.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Defines the density-of-states shape; central to the requested expression.

items.title: Factor of two roots
items.description: The final expression for n(E) contains a factor of 2 in the numerator, giving 2N/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)), reflecting the two symmetric roots ±k₀.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agree that two roots ±k₀ each contribute 1/|g'(k_i)|, doubling the result.
provenance.discriminates: A response that produces half the correct value by counting only one root.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Two-root multiplicity is load-bearing for the correct prefactor magnitude.

items.title: Heaviside theta factor
items.description: The final expression for n(E) contains a Heaviside step function factor in the form θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) or an equivalent form such as θ(2|J|−|E−E_s|).

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts diverge on the exact form: θ(4J²−(E−E_s)²), θ(2|J|−|E−E_s|), or θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t); all are equivalent for J>0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes a single θ with the wrong argument or a difference with reversed ordering.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key requested quantity; encodes band support condition.

items.title: Change of variable
items.description: The derivation explicitly performs the substitution x=ka with dk=dx/a, transforming the integral to ∫_{−π}^{π} δ(E−E_s+2J cos x) dx.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts show x=ka, dk=dx/a, and the integral transformed to limits [−π, π].
provenance.discriminates: A response that keeps k as the integration variable and mishandles the limits or the Jacobian dk=dx/a.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate step that eliminates a and sets up the delta integral.

items.title: Root condition
items.description: The root condition cos(ka₀) = −(E−E_s)/(2J) is explicitly stated for the argument of the delta function.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts state cos x₀ = −(E−E_s)/(2J) as the equation g(x)=0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that solves for the root incorrectly or does not state the condition on cos(ka₀).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Defines where δ fires; prerequisite for the Jacobian evaluation.

items.title: Delta identity
items.description: The identity δ(g(k)) = Σ_i δ(k−k_i)/|g'(k_i)| is stated in the form for handling the delta function of a composite argument.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts use this standard identity to decompose the delta function at its roots.
provenance.discriminates: A response that evaluates δ(g(k)) without identifying the roots or applying the Jacobian factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Standard identity that powers the entire transformation from integral to algebraic form.

items.title: Jacobian value
items.description: The Jacobian |g'(k_i)| = √(4J²−(E−E_s)²) is derived at each root of the delta function argument.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts compute |g'(x_i)| = 2|J|√(1−cos²x₀) = √(4J²−(E−E_s)²).
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes the Jacobian as 2J sin(ka₀) without the absolute value or the simplification to the sqrt form.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Produces the square-root denominator in the final expression.

items.title: Delta-derivative explanation
items.description: The relationship δ(y) = dθ(y)/dy is stated and used to explain how the integral of the delta function is transformed into terms involving the Heaviside theta function by integrating θ over k-space and then differentiating with respect to E.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts cite δ(y) = dθ(y)/dy to connect the delta function integral to Heaviside step functions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses θ in the final answer without explaining its connection to the delta function.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the 'explain how δ is transformed into terms involving θ' sub-question.

items.title: Band edges defined
items.description: The band-edge energies E_b and E_t corresponding to E−E_s = ±2J are defined in the derivation of the expression involving the Heaviside function.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses E_b and E_t in the step function arguments; rollouts express this as |E−E_s| ≤ 2|J| instead.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) without defining E_b and E_t.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Bounds the theta support; needed for the θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) form.

items.title: Derivative g'(k)
items.description: The derivative g'(k) = −2Ja sin(ka) is explicitly computed for the argument g(k) = E−E_s + 2J cos(ka) of the delta function.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts compute g'(x) = −2J sin x as the derivative needed for the Jacobian.
provenance.discriminates: A response that skips computing g'(k) and cannot justify the Jacobian factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate quantity for evaluating the Jacobian at each root.

items.title: Avoids spurious a
items.description: Avoids retaining a spurious factor of the lattice constant a in the final expression for n(E) by failing to apply dk = dx/a when substituting x = ka.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Failing to cancel lattice constant a' (severity medium): Na/π retains an extra a if dk=dx/a is overlooked.
provenance.discriminates: A response whose final expression has 2Na/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)) instead of 2N/(π√(4J²−(E−E_s)²)).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common algebraic slip; removes correctness of the prefactor.

items.title: Avoids bare J
items.description: Avoids writing the prefactor with bare J in the denominator of the final expression for n(E) as N/(πJ√(1−((E−E_s)/(2J))²)) without using |J| or J², which yields a negative density of states for J < 0.

provenance.evidence_detail: Collective error: the reference answer itself uses bare J; all rollouts correctly use |J| or J² in the denominator, which is manifestly positive for either sign of J.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes N/(πJ√(...)) and produces a negative n(E) when J < 0.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Collective error observed; sign-correctness depends on |J| or J².

items.title: Avoids wrong ordering
items.description: Avoids the wrong band-edge ordering in the theta function expression θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) where E_b > E_t for J > 0, which evaluates to −1 inside the band and gives a negative density of states.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong band-edge ordering' (severity medium): the reference uses E_b, E_t without defining them, and the bottom/top assignment depends on the sign of J.
provenance.discriminates: A response that defines E_b = E_s + 2J and E_t = E_s − 2J for J > 0, reversing the step-function difference and giving a negative DOS.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed pitfall; wrong ordering negates the entire density of states.

items.title: Theta difference form
items.description: The Heaviside step function factor is written as θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t) or an equivalent form such as θ(2|J|−|E−E_s|).

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts diverge on the exact form: θ(4J²−(E−E_s)²), θ(2|J|−|E−E_s|), or θ(E−E_b)−θ(E−E_t); all are equivalent for J>0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes a single θ with the wrong argument or a difference with reversed ordering.

items.title: Overall impact stated
items.description: The response states that knowledge of Mendelian genetics would have significantly impacted Darwin's theories of evolution.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question a asks for a detailed analysis of the overall impact of genetic principles on Darwin's evolutionary framework; the reference affirms significant impact.
provenance.discriminates: A response that merely describes Mendel and Darwin separately without connecting them as a significant impact on Darwin's theories.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core thesis; no valid answer omits the central claim that genetics would have changed Darwin's work.

items.title: Blending inheritance gap
items.description: The response states that Darwin's mechanisms of inheritance relied on blending inheritance rather than Mendelian particulate inheritance, and recognizes this as a major gap in his work.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agree Darwin's model was blending inheritance, to be replaced by Mendelian particulate inheritance; this is the core contrast the question demands.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims Darwin already had a workable inheritance model or treats blending and particulate inheritance as equivalent.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Identifies the specific inheritance defect Darwin held; central to the counterfactual analysis.

items.title: Particulate inheritance contrast
items.description: The response states that Mendelian genetics provides particulate inheritance in which discrete alleles persist intact in heterozygotes rather than being blended away, directly contrasting with Darwin's blending inheritance model.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agree Mendelian alleles persist intact in heterozygotes rather than being halved each generation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions particulate inheritance but does not explain the mechanism of allele persistence that resolves the swamping problem.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The mechanistic crux: alleles persisting in heterozygotes is what makes selection workable.

items.title: Swamping problem resolved
items.description: The response addresses the swamping problem (Fleeming Jenkin's objection) that blending inheritance dilutes favorable variants and explains how Mendelian inheritance resolves it.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts identify Jenkin's swamping problem and agree Mendelian alleles persist intact; the implicit constraints require addressing this objection.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses inheritance mechanisms but never mentions the swamping problem that was a major historical challenge to Darwin's theory.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Jenkin's objection was a historically specific challenge that genetics directly answers.

items.title: Pangenesis replaced
items.description: The response identifies Darwin's pangenesis theory (gemmules) as his specific proposed mechanism of inheritance that Mendelian genetics would replace, including leading Darwin to reject the inheritance of acquired characters.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agree Darwin's model included pangenesis/gemmules; the implicit constraints require distinguishing what Darwin actually proposed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that vaguely attributes a 'wrong inheritance model' to Darwin without naming pangenesis or gemmules.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Names Darwin's actual inheritance theory; connects genetics to a concrete change in his work.

items.title: Genotype-phenotype distinction
items.description: The response distinguishes that natural selection acts on phenotypes while heritable evolutionary change depends on genotypic or allele-frequency change in Darwin's work.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts make the genotype-phenotype distinction; the implicit constraints require it.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts natural selection acts directly on genes or that 'fittest' means best genotype.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundation for reframing fitness; without this distinction genetics adds nothing to Darwin's theories.

items.title: Fitness redefined
items.description: The response explains that 'survival of the fittest' would be refined into differential reproductive success tied to heritable allele or genotype transmission, providing a detailed analysis of how genetic principles including heritable variation and allele frequencies would affect this concept in Darwin's theories.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question c targets re-examination of 'survival of the fittest' in light of genetic variation; all rollouts agree on this redefinition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses fitness only as physical strength or survival without connecting it to heritable reproductive success.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the sub-question on survival of the fittest; redefines fitness in genetic terms.

items.title: Natural selection preserved
items.description: The response states that Mendelian genetics would strengthen and refine natural selection as a core principle rather than overturn or replace it.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Overturning natural selection' (high severity); all three rollouts state the core theory would be preserved.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims Darwin would have abandoned 'survival of the fittest' or replaced natural selection with a purely genetic model.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Critical corrective: genetics complements Darwin's theories, it does not supplant natural selection.

items.title: Changes enumerated
items.description: The response enumerates at least two changes to Darwin's theories that would have resulted from understanding genetic principles, such as rejecting pangenesis, adopting particulate inheritance, or reframing fitness as differential allele transmission.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Sub-question d left unanswered' (medium severity); sub-question d requires concrete enumeration of theoretical modifications.
provenance.discriminates: A response that provides general analysis but never lists specific changes or modifications to Darwin's theories.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly asks for resulting changes; enumeration directly satisfies that requirement.

items.title: Avoids anachronistic synthesis
items.description: Avoids attributing the full Modern Synthesis (e.g., Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, Fisher/Wright/Haldane population genetics) to what Mendelian genetics alone would have given Darwin in the 1860s.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Anachronistic Modern Synthesis' (medium severity) warns against conflating 1930s-40s population genetics with 1860s Mendelian genetics.
provenance.discriminates: A response that credits Darwin's hypothetical revision with Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium or neutral theory, which postdated Mendel by decades.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common conflation of Mendel's peas with 20th-century population genetics; discounted pitfall.

items.title: Avoids pure Lamarckian framing
items.description: Avoids conflating Darwin's pangenesis with Lamarckian inheritance of acquired characters as if Darwin's theories were purely Lamarckian and would be wholly overturned.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Acquired characters misattribution' (low severity) warns against treating pangenesis and Lamarckism as identical.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims Darwin's theory was purely Lamarckian and that Mendelian genetics would reject the entire Darwinian framework.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Overstates the Lamarckian element; Darwin's natural selection was distinct from Lamarck's mechanism.

items.title: Avoids wrong dilution rate
items.description: Avoids stating the swamping dilution rate under blending inheritance as quartered or eliminated in one generation; the correct rate is that a favorable trait is halved (50% dilution) per outcrossing generation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Jenkin swamping dilution rate' (medium severity) warns against misstating the dilution factor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that quantifies the dilution rate incorrectly as 25% or zero per generation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific numeric error if quantified; discounted because flaws were built from mined pitfalls.

items.title: Mendel contemporary noted
items.description: The response notes that Mendel's 1866 work was contemporary with Darwin but unknown to him, framing the analysis as counterfactual rather than a historical chronology of influence.

provenance.evidence_detail: The implicit constraints require historical accuracy and recognition that the question is counterfactual.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats Mendelian genetics as if Darwin had access to it or that misdates the timeline of discovery.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds historical depth; contextualizes the counterfactual but not load-bearing for correctness.

items.title: Allele frequency framing
items.description: The response discusses that evolution could be understood in terms of changes in allele frequencies across generations, a refinement that genetic principles would have added to Darwin's theories.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 2 lists reinterpreting evolution as allele frequency change; rollout 3 discusses reconciling continuous and discrete variation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that frames evolution only as morphological change without connecting it to allele-frequency change in populations.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Allele-frequency framing is the key conceptual bridge between Mendel and Darwin's evolution.

items.title: Continuous-discrete reconciliation
items.description: The response addresses how Mendelian genetics would help reconcile the observation of continuous phenotypic variation with discrete genetic factors, a tension in Darwin's work regarding inheritance, connecting specific genetic principles to specific weaknesses in Darwin's original formulation of evolution.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 3 lists reconciling continuous and discrete variation as a specific change; this was a genuine historical tension.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats continuous variation and discrete Mendelian factors as contradictory without addressing how they are reconciled.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real but secondary insight; continuous-vs-discrete tension was a genuine issue for Darwin.

items.title: Integral formula stated
items.description: States the expectation value formula as ⟨A⟩ = ∫ dV ψ*(Âψ), with the operator Â applied to the wave function ψ and ψ* forming the bra.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires the standard expectation value expression; the reference answer gives exactly ⟨A⟩ = ∫ dV ψ*(Âψ).
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that write a wrong integrand or omit the operator acting on ψ.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core formula the entire question revolves around; without it correctness collapses.

items.title: Dirac notation form
items.description: States the equivalent Dirac notation form ⟨ψ|Â|ψ⟩ for the expectation value of observable A.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts included ⟨A⟩ = ⟨ψ|Â|ψ⟩ as the compact form alongside the integral expression.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that give only one notation and cannot connect the integral to the inner-product structure.

items.title: Avoid scalar on |ψ|²
items.description: Avoids writing the formula as ∫ |ψ|² A dV with A treated as a classical scalar function rather than as an operator acting on the wave function ψ.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Operator on probability density' (high severity): treating Â as a c-number multiplier of |ψ|².

items.title: Conjugate present
items.description: Avoids writing the expectation formula as ∫ ψ(Âψ) dV without the complex conjugate ψ* on the bra factor, where the operator is applied to the wave function ψ but not its modulus.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing complex conjugate' (high severity): omitting ψ* yields an expression not guaranteed real for Hermitian Â.

items.title: Avoid operator on modulus
items.description: Avoids writing ⟨A⟩ = ∫ ψ*(Â|ψ|) dV, which applies the operator Â to the modulus |ψ| rather than to the wave function ψ itself.

items.title: Eigenbasis expansion
items.description: Derives the expectation value by expanding ψ in the eigenbasis of Â as ψ = Σ c_n φ_n, where φ_n are the eigenfunctions of Â.

items.title: Born rule in derivation
items.description: Uses the Born rule P(a_n) = |c_n|² to obtain ⟨A⟩ = Σ a_n |c_n|² in the derivation of the expectation value formula.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts use P(a_n) = |c_n|² and compute Σ a_n |c_n|² before converting to operator form.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that skip the probabilistic foundation and write the operator form without justification.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate result linking measurement probabilities to expectation.

items.title: Completeness to integral
items.description: Applies the completeness relation to convert the spectral sum Σ a_n |c_n|² into the standard integral form ∫ ψ*(Âψ) dV.

provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that present the sum and the integral as unrelated facts rather than connected by completeness.

items.title: Linearity property stated
items.description: States that the linearity of Â means Â(αψ + βφ) = αÂψ + βÂφ, preserving quantum superposition.

items.title: Modulus causes nonlinearity

items.title: Postulate: operators
items.description: Maps the formulation to the quantum mechanics postulates by stating that observables correspond to linear Hermitian operators.

items.title: Postulate: state vectors
items.description: Maps the formulation to the quantum mechanics postulates by stating that the wave function ψ represents a state vector in Hilbert space.

provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that discuss operators but never connect ψ to the Hilbert-space state-vector postulate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Links the wave function to Hilbert space formalism; supports the postulate discussion.

items.title: Cross-terms preserved

items.title: Hermiticity and reality

provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that claim reality of ⟨A⟩ without showing the conjugation-and-Hermiticity derivation step.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Underlying reasoning for why Na2HPO3 is a normal salt; common student error point.

items.title: H3PO4 is tribasic

items.title: NH2 ortho/para director
items.description: The response states that the NH2 group in C6H5NH2 directs electrophilic substitution to the ortho and para positions through delocalization of the nitrogen lone pair into the aromatic ring, increasing electron density at those positions.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question b asks to classify directing effects of NH2; reference confirms NH2 is ortho/para director.
provenance.discriminates: A response that classifies NH2 as a meta director or fails to state its directing orientation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer requirement; no valid response can omit NH2 directing to ortho and para positions.

items.title: OH ortho/para director
items.description: The response states that OH directs electrophilic substitution to the ortho and para positions.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question b asks to compare directing effects of OH; reference confirms OH is ortho/para director.
provenance.discriminates: A response that classifies OH as a meta director or omits its directing orientation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly requested comparison; OH directing behavior is central to the asked contrast.

items.title: NO2 meta director
items.description: The response states that NO2 directs electrophilic substitution to the meta position as a deactivating group rather than as an ortho/para-directing activator.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'NO2 direction reversed' identifies the high-severity error of misclassifying NO2 as ortho/para director.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states NO2 is an ortho/para-directing activator.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core contrast requested; NO2 meta direction is essential to the directing-effects discussion.

items.title: NH2 +M mechanism
items.description: The response explains that NH2 activates the aromatic ring through +M mesomeric lone-pair resonance donation into the ring rather than primarily through a +I inductive effect.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall '+I attribution error' notes the mistake of claiming NH2 activates by inductive donation; nitrogen is actually electronegative (-I).
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes 'NH2 activates by inductive donation (+I)' as the mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Mechanistic explanation is a requested sub-question; +M attribution discriminates correct reasoning.

items.title: Iminium resonance contributor
items.description: The response invokes the sigma complex intermediate and describes a resonance contributor of the ortho or para sigma complex in which positive charge resides on the carbon bearing NH2 and nitrogen donates its lone pair, forming an iminium-like structure.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Resonance forms omitted' requires describing the specific iminium-type contributor for o/p attack.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only a verbal 'NH2 donates electrons to o/p' with no resonance-form description.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key mechanistic intermediate explaining why ortho and para attack is favored; distinctive correct detail.

items.title: Meta sigma complex limits
items.description: The response states that the meta sigma complex cannot generate the iminium-type resonance contributor that places positive charge on the NH2-bearing carbon, while still acknowledging that the meta pathway possesses ordinary resonance contributors.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Meta complex unstabilized' and consensus both state meta lacks the extra iminium stabilization.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not explain why meta is disfavored relative to o/p at the sigma-complex level.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the meta disfavour without overclaiming; corrects a common structural misconception.

items.title: NH2 stronger than OH
items.description: The response states that NH2 is a stronger activator than OH in electrophilic aromatic substitution, giving the relative activation order -NH2 > -OH >> benzene > -NO2.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus includes the full relative activation order; this synthesizes the comparison across all three substituents demanded by sub-question b.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses each substituent individually but never places them in a single comparative ranking.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Requested comparison of substituent directing effects; the activation order is a disputed point.

items.title: Electronegativity rationale
items.description: The response attributes the greater activating strength of NH2 over OH to nitrogen's lower electronegativity (~3.0 vs ~3.5 Pauling), which holds the lone pair more loosely for resonance donation into the aromatic ring.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'NH2 weaker than OH' correct_result specifies the electronegativity argument for why NH2 > OH.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the correct NH2 > OH order but with no rationale, or gives a wrong rationale.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds depth to the NH2-versus-OH comparison; not essential but demonstrates deeper reasoning.

items.title: NO2 deactivation mechanism
items.description: The response states that NO2 deactivates the aromatic ring through -M mesomeric and -I inductive electron withdrawal from the ring.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'NO2 direction reversed' correct_result specifies NO2 is a strong meta-directing deactivator via -M and -I.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes NO2 as electron-donating or omits its withdrawal mechanisms.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Mechanism for NO2 deactivation is part of the directing-effects explanation requested.

items.title: NO2 meta rationale
items.description: Avoids the claim that NO2 actively donates electron density to the meta position, instead explaining that meta is favored because the ortho and para sigma complexes are destabilized by placing positive charge adjacent to the electron-withdrawing NO2 group.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'NO2 direction reversed' identifies the mistake of asserting NO2 pushes electrons to meta.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says 'NO2 directs to meta because it donates electrons to the meta position.'
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common conceptual trap; observed flawed responses misattribute meta direction to active donation.

items.title: Tribromoaniline example
items.description: The response identifies bromination of aniline as giving 2,4,6-tribromoaniline as the product of direct electrophilic substitution, illustrating strong NH2 ortho and para activation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Bromination product wrong' notes the error of reporting mono-brominated aniline; consensus gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states bromination of aniline gives p-bromoaniline or another monosubstituted product.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Concrete example of NH2 directing effects as requested; product specificity discriminates correct answers.

items.title: m-Dinitrobenzene example
items.description: The response identifies nitration of nitrobenzene as giving m-dinitrobenzene (1,3-dinitrobenzene), illustrating NO2 meta directing effects.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question c asks for examples illustrating directing effects; consensus provides nitration of nitrobenzene → m-dinitrobenzene as a NO2 meta-directing example.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims nitration of nitrobenzene gives o- or p-dinitrobenzene, or gives no NO2-directed example.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Concrete example of NO2 meta direction as requested; positional isomer specification is load-bearing.

items.title: Acidic protonation caveat
items.description: Avoids claiming that direct nitration of aniline under strongly acidic HNO3/H2SO4 conditions cleanly gives ortho/para-nitroaniline, instead noting that the NH2 group is protonated to -NH3+ under these conditions.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Acidic protonation ignored' identifies the error of reporting o/p-nitroaniline as direct nitration products of aniline in mixed acid.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states direct nitration of aniline in mixed acid gives o- and p-nitroaniline without addressing protonation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common trap where NH2 protonation reverses directing behavior; observed in flawed responses.

items.title: Acetanilide protection
items.description: The response mentions that aniline is protected as acetanilide before nitration to preserve ortho and para directing behavior and obtain the para-nitro product.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Acidic protonation ignored' correct_result specifies acetanilide protection; consensus includes this as important practical context.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses aniline nitration but does not address how to avoid the protonation problem.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Practical resolution to the protonation problem; demonstrates mastery of directing effects under real conditions.

items.title: Phenol nitration example
items.description: The response provides nitration of phenol giving o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol as an example illustrating OH ortho and para directing effects.

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergent claim on choice of OH example; rollouts 1 and 2 used nitration of phenol → o/p-nitrophenol, which is a valid illustration.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives no specific OH-directed example or gives one without positional outcomes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Supplementary example for OH directing effects; adds coverage but is not essential to the core answer.

items.title: Recursion relation formula
items.description: The response states the decimation recursion relation for the 1D Ising model coupling constant as K' = (1/2) ln cosh(2K) or equivalently tanh K' = tanh² K, avoiding omission of the factor 1/2.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Missing 1/2 factor': dropping the 1/2 yields spurious fixed points.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes K' = ln cosh(2K) instead of K' = (1/2) ln cosh(2K).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core derivation result; pitfall item confirms high discrimination for missing 1/2.

items.title: Step-by-step derivation
items.description: The response shows the derivation of the recursion relation by summing over every other site in the 1D Ising model, arriving at e^{2K'} = cosh(2K).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks to derive the recursion relations; the step-by-step summation is the expected derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the final recursion relation without any derivation from the Ising partition function.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly asks to derive; intermediate steps are load-bearing.

items.title: Partition function preservation
items.description: The response shows that the RG procedure preserves the partition function as Z_N(K) = C^{N/2} Z_{N/2}(K') with C = 2√cosh(2K), reflecting that the system renormalizes by decreasing the number of sites.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim: partition function preservation with site reduction N → N/2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives K' without connecting it to the partition function and the halving of the system size.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Intermediate quantity linking decimation to the recursion; moderate importance.

items.title: Fixed point K*=0
items.description: The response states that K*=0 is a fixed point of the renormalization group flow for the 1D Ising model coupling constant and that iterating the flow at nearby values converges to K=0.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Stability of fixed points reversed': correct is K*=0 stable, K*=∞ unstable.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reverses the stability of the two fixed points.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct stability assignment is essential; pitfall confirms reversed-stability errors are common.

items.title: Fixed point K*=∞
items.description: The response states that K*=∞ (T=0) is a fixed point of the coupling constant flow and that iterating the flow at nearby finite values diverges from K=∞.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Stability of fixed points reversed': correct is K*=0 stable, K*=∞ unstable.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reverses the stability of the two fixed points.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Essential for identifying the only critical point; pitfall confirms common reversed-stability error.

items.title: Flow toward K=0
items.description: The response states that for all finite K>0 the recursion relation gives K' < K, so the coupling constant flows toward K=0, and that the correct flow is determined by iterating the relation K'(K).

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Flow direction reversed': correct is K' < K for all finite K>0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the flow drives K to infinity for any initial K>0.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the reference; pitfall confirms reversed-flow-direction errors are common.

items.title: Low-temperature variable analysis
items.description: The response analyzes the flow near K=∞ using u = e^{-2K}, deriving u' ≈ 2u or u' = 2u/(1+u²), to show that the coupling constant flow moves away from K=∞.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: low-temperature stability analysis with u = e^{-2K} yields u' ≈ 2u.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims K=∞ is stable without performing the near-critical linearized analysis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate result proving repulsion from K=∞; strong reasoning step.

items.title: High-temperature behavior
items.description: The response states that near K=0 the recursion relation gives K' ≈ K², indicating flow of the coupling constant to zero at high temperature.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: K' ≈ K² near K=0, rapid flow to zero.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not quantify the high-temperature behavior of the flow.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Intermediate result confirming attraction to K=0; moderate discrimination.

items.title: Semi-group nature of RG
items.description: The response describes the renormalization group as a semi-group, where the transformation renormalizes the system by decreasing the number of sites and has no inverse.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer: 'reflecting the semi-group nature of the RG'; no rollout used the term semi-group.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the RG as a full group with an inverse, or omits the semi-group characterization.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly in reference answer; conceptually central to RG structure.

items.title: K = βJ dimensionless coupling
items.description: The response uses the dimensionless coupling K = βJ as the variable in the recursion relation, correctly absorbing temperature into the coupling constant.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Variable K vs J conflated': the natural RG variable is K = βJ, not J alone.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the recursion in terms of J without tracking temperature dependence.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Pitfall-anchored; using wrong variable would derail the entire derivation.

items.title: Correlation length scaling
items.description: The response states that the correlation length transforms under the renormalization group rescaling as ξ' = ξ/b with b=2 for decimation, so ξ(K') = ξ(K)/2.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: ξ(K') = ξ(K)/2, confirming b=2 rescaling.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ξ' = b·ξ or ξ' = ξ, which is inconsistent with the flow toward K=0.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects RG flow to physical observables; supports phase-transition discussion.

items.title: Finite correlation length T>0
items.description: The response states that the correlation length ξ is finite for all T>0 and diverges only as T→0 (K→∞), the fixed point from which the renormalization group flow diverges.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: ξ is finite for all T>0 and diverges only as T→0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims ξ diverges at a finite temperature.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Physical justification for no finite-T transition; links fixed points to observables.

items.title: Physical meaning of coarse-graining
items.description: The response states the physical meaning of the renormalization group procedure as coarse-graining by decimation with scale factor b=2, summing over short-distance spin degrees of freedom to yield a coupling at longer length scales.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks for physical meaning; consensus: coarse-graining by summing short-distance spins.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives K'(K) and fixed points but never describes what coarse-graining means physically.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly requests physical meaning; central conceptual content.

items.title: No finite-T phase transition
items.description: The response concludes that the 1D Ising model has no phase transition at finite temperature and that the only critical point is at T=0 (K=∞).

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Finite-T phase transition claimed': correct is no finite-T transition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports a finite-T phase transition based on a spurious fixed point.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key conclusion for phase transitions; pitfall confirms common false-claim errors.

items.title: RG flow justifies no transition
items.description: The response uses the renormalization group flow analysis — whether fixed points attract or repel the coupling constant flow — to justify the absence of a finite-temperature phase transition.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) requires RG reasoning supporting the phase-transition conclusion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts no transition without connecting it to the fixed-point and flow analysis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Ties derivation to the phase-transition conclusion; question asks for implications.

items.title: Hamiltonian with inverse inertia
items.description: States the quantum mechanical treatment Hamiltonian as Ĥ = (1/2) Σ_{ij} L̂_i I^{-1}_{ij} L̂_j, explicitly using the inverse of the inertia tensor rather than the inertia tensor itself.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer gives exactly this formula; sub-question (b) asks for the explicit Hamiltonian.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes a different Hamiltonian form or omits the sum over ij.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core formula; reference answer requires it. Highest importance to correctness.

items.title: Principal-axis diagonal form
items.description: Writes the Hamiltonian in principal axes as H = Σ_k L̂_k²/(2I_k), showing this diagonal special case of the general quantum treatment.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed on this diagonal form; it clarifies how the general formula reduces when the inertia tensor is diagonal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the abstract tensor formula without showing the physically transparent diagonal reduction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate result; connects general form to solvable cases.

items.title: Hermiticity and symmetrization
items.description: Addresses operator ordering in the Hamiltonian by noting that in a non-principal-axis frame H must be symmetrized as (1/4) Σ_{ij} (I^{-1})_{ij}(L̂_i L̂_j + L̂_j L̂_i) to remain Hermitian, or that principal axes avoid the issue.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts disagreed on symmetrization: rollout 1 symmetrized explicitly, rollout 3 did not, rollout 2 only used principal axes. The reference gives the unsymmetrized form, which is correct only in principal axes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the unsymmetrized tensor form for a general frame without acknowledging the operator-ordering issue.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Subtle correctness requirement; distinct from simply stating the formula.

items.title: Inertia tensor is c-number
items.description: States that the inertia tensor (or its inverse) is a classical c-number parameter determined by the mass distribution, not a quantum operator acting on angular momentum states.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts correctly identify the inertia tensor as a c-number; the reference and implicit constraints confirm only angular momentum components are operators.
provenance.discriminates: A response that promotes I^{-1}_{ij} to an operator and introduces commutation relations for it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Clarifies role of inertia tensor; prevents a category error in the treatment.

items.title: Space-fixed commutativity
items.description: States that space-fixed angular momentum components commute with the Hamiltonian, [J_i^S, H] = 0, so angular momentum is conserved in the torque-free context.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed that [J_i^(S), H] = 0 and [J², H] = 0, reflecting torque-free conservation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims space-fixed angular momentum is not conserved or fails to distinguish it from body-fixed components.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the commutativity sub-question with a specific relation.

items.title: Total J² conservation
items.description: States that [J², H] = 0, so the total angular momentum magnitude is conserved as the quantum expression of the torque-free condition.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts noted [J², H] = 0 as a consequence of the torque-free condition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not identify total angular momentum as a conserved quantity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinct from component-wise conservation; a required intermediate result.

items.title: Body-fixed anomalous sign
items.description: States that body-fixed angular momentum components satisfy [J_i^B, J_j^B] = −iℏ ε_{ijk} J_k^B, the anomalous negative-sign commutation relation distinct from the space-fixed case.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts correctly contrasted [J_i^B, J_j^B] = −iℏ ε_{ijk} J_k^B with the standard space-fixed [J_i^S, J_j^S] = +iℏ ε_{ijk} J_k^S.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns the standard positive-sign commutator to body-fixed components.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific disputed point; wrong sign leads to incorrect precession analysis.

items.title: Body-fixed non-commutation with H
items.description: States that body-fixed angular momentum components generally do not commute with the Hamiltonian for an asymmetric top, [J_i^B, H] ≠ 0.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed that [J_i^(B), H] ≠ 0 for the asymmetric top, which produces the quantum analogue of Euler precession.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims all body-fixed components commute with H, which would eliminate precession.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core contrast with space-fixed case; explains why precession occurs.

items.title: Commutativity drives precession
items.description: Explains that the commutativity of space-fixed angular momentum with the Hamiltonian means conservation, while non-commutativity of body-fixed components with H drives the time evolution constituting quantum precession.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) asks how commutativity of angular momentum with the Hamiltonian affects precession; the consensus shows space-fixed commutes (conservation) and body-fixed does not (precession).
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not connect the commutation structure to the precession dynamics.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers how commutativity affects precession; synthesizes items 5 and 8.

items.title: Inertia tensor determines spectrum
items.description: Explains that the eigenvalues of the inertia tensor (the principal moments I_1, I_2, I_3) determine the energy spectrum and the character of the precession through their role in the Hamiltonian.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks for the role of the inertia tensor; the consensus confirms principal moments shape the dynamics.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions the inertia tensor formula without explaining how its eigenvalues determine the spectrum and precession type.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects inertia tensor to physical consequences; addresses the role sub-question.

items.title: Torque-free conservation basis
items.description: States that the torque-free condition means no external torque acts on the rigid rotor, so total angular momentum is conserved, which underlies the commutativity of space-fixed angular momentum with the Hamiltonian.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for the framework including the torque-free condition; the implicit constraints confirm no external torque implies total angular momentum conservation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents the Hamiltonian and commutators without linking them to the physical torque-free condition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Provides physical grounding for the mathematical commutativity results.

items.title: Euler and Ehrenfest correspondence
items.description: States that [J_i^B, H] ≠ 0 produces time evolution of body-fixed angular momentum expectation values that is the quantum analogue of Euler's precession equations, connected to the classical torque-free limit via the Ehrenfest theorem.

provenance.evidence_detail: The implicit constraints list the Ehrenfest theorem as a link between quantum operators and classical precession; sub-question (a) asks for the overall quantum mechanical treatment.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents only operator algebra without connecting to the classical precession limit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds depth linking quantum and classical treatments; not strictly required for correctness.

items.title: Symmetric top extra quantum number
items.description: States that for a symmetric top, the body-fixed projection along the symmetry axis commutes with the Hamiltonian, [J_3^B, H] = 0, enabling regular precession and providing an additional quantum number.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts noted that for the symmetric top [J_3^(B), H] = 0, giving regular precession.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the general asymmetric-top case without addressing how symmetric-top symmetry changes the commutation structure.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Important special case but supplementary to the general treatment.

items.title: Spherical top isotropy
items.description: States that for a spherical top the Hamiltonian reduces to H = J²/(2I), all components commute with H, and no precession occurs.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts noted that for the spherical top H ∝ J² and all components commute, giving no precession.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to mention the spherical-top limit where precession vanishes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Boundary case illustrating when precession vanishes; supplementary depth.

items.title: Angular momentum notation
items.description: Uses the L̂ notation for the angular momentum operator in the Hamiltonian as in the reference, or explicitly states that J_i is used equivalently for the rigid-rotor angular momentum.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses L̂_i; all three rollouts used J notation without noting the equivalence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses J_i throughout without any statement of equivalence to the reference's L̂ notation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Notational consistency with reference; minor but verifiable.

items.title: Original resonance condition
items.description: States that the resonant frequency condition for the two original series RLC circuits is ω₀² = 1/(L₁C₁) = 1/(L₂C₂).

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference agree on this starting condition; it is the load-bearing premise for the entire proof.
provenance.discriminates: A response that never states the relationship between ω₀ and the original L,C values, making the subsequent proof unverifiable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational equality; without it the entire proof collapses. Collective-error evidence.

items.title: Series inductance addition
items.description: States that when the inductors are connected together in series, the combined inductance is L = L₁ + L₂, not the parallel formula L₁L₂/(L₁ + L₂).

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among all rollouts and the reference; a required intermediate value for the combined circuit.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a parallel inductor formula or otherwise fails to add the inductances for the series chain.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core combined-circuit fact; absorbed the parallel-inductor pitfall. Collective-error discrimination.

items.title: Series capacitance formula
items.description: States that the two capacitors connected in series yield a combined capacitance C = C₁C₂/(C₁ + C₂), not C₁ + C₂.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree; the reference explicitly notes the capacitors are in series.
provenance.discriminates: A response that adds C₁ + C₂ as if the capacitors were in parallel, which would break the proof.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key combined-circuit fact; absorbed parallel-capacitor pitfall and series identification. Collective-error discrimination.

items.title: General resonance formula
items.description: States that for a series RLC circuit, resonance occurs at ω = 1/√(LC).

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts use this standard formula as the basis for computing the combined resonant frequency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not invoke the LC resonance relation and therefore cannot connect the LC product to the frequency.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required formula applied later; reference groundwork without high standalone discrimination.

items.title: Resonance formula applied
items.description: Uses the resonant condition ω² = 1/(LC) with the combined L and C values to derive the combined circuit's frequency.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference apply the resonance formula to the equivalent combined L and C rather than to individual elements.
provenance.discriminates: A response that finds equivalent L and C but never plugs them into the resonance formula to compute the frequency.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects combined elements to frequency; collective-error evidence, load-bearing step.

items.title: Combined LC product
items.description: Shows that the combined LC product (L₁ + L₂) · C₁C₂/(C₁ + C₂) equals 1/ω₀².

provenance.evidence_detail: This is the core target of the question — demonstrating that the combined LC product yields the same resonant frequency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the equivalent L and C values but never verifies that their product reproduces 1/ω₀².
provenance.calibration_rationale: The pivotal intermediate result proving frequency is again ω₀. Sub-question evidence.

items.title: Conclusion ω equals ω₀
items.description: Concludes that the resonant frequency of the combined circuit equals ω₀.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question explicitly asks to show that the resonant frequency will again be ω₀.
provenance.discriminates: A response that performs algebra but never states the final conclusion that the combined frequency is again ω₀.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The final requested result; without it the proof is incomplete. Sub-question evidence.

items.title: Distributive expansion
items.description: Expands (L₁ + L₂)C₁C₂ as L₁C₁·C₂ + L₂C₂·C₁ when simplifying the combined resonant frequency expression.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference performs this specific distributive step to regroup terms by the original LC products.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts the product equals 1/ω₀² without showing the key distributive expansion that makes the substitution possible.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing algebra step enabling the substitution; reference-only evidence.

items.title: Substitution of LᵢCᵢ
items.description: Substitutes L₁C₁ = 1/ω₀² and L₂C₂ = 1/ω₀² into the combined expression, yielding a numerator of (C₁ + C₂)/ω₀².

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference substitutes these values into the grouped terms C₂(L₁C₁) and C₁(L₂C₂) in the denominator.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the product but never applies the given resonance condition to simplify it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects original conditions to combined circuit; reference-only but mechanistically essential.

items.title: Final division step
items.description: Divides (C₁ + C₂)/ω₀² by (C₁ + C₂) to obtain 1/ω₀² as the combined LC product.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference's final algebraic step cancels the (C₁ + C₂) factor between numerator and denominator.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the result 1/ω₀² without showing the cancellation of the (C₁ + C₂) term.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Completes the algebraic simplification; reference-only, lower standalone importance.

items.title: Resistance irrelevance
items.description: States that the resistances R₁ and R₂ do not affect the resonant frequency of the series RLC circuit, avoiding use of a damped-resonance formula that includes R.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference note that resistances affect only damping, not the frequency where reactance vanishes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that includes R₁ or R₂ in the resonance formula, leading to an incorrect combined frequency.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common misconception; absorbed damped-resonance pitfall. Collective-error evidence.

items.title: Avoids identical-components
items.description: Avoids assuming L₁ = L₂ and C₁ = C₂ as a special case in the proof that the combined resonant frequency is again ω₀.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Assuming identical components' is medium severity; equal products L₁C₁ = L₂C₂ do not imply equal individual values.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only proves the result for the special case L₁ = L₂, C₁ = C₂ rather than for the general case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific trap where proof only works for equal elements; pitfall evidence, moderate impact.

items.title: Fulcrum near object
items.description: States that the fulcrum is placed closer to the object than to the point where effort is applied on the lever.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question b asks where the fulcrum must be placed; reference answer states 'Place fulcrum closer to the object.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the fulcrum goes in the middle or near the effort end.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer element; directly specifies fulcrum placement relative to object.

items.title: 3:1 arm ratio
items.description: States a 3:1 ratio of effort arm to load arm as the required lever configuration, avoiding a reversed 1:3 ratio that would make the object harder to lift.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Ratio direction reversed' (severity high): inverting MA so load arm / effort arm = 3 instead of effort arm / load arm = 3.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says 'place fulcrum 3 times farther from the object' or otherwise inverts the ratio direction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core quantitative answer; absorbs the reversed-ratio pitfall observed in flawed responses.

items.title: Fulcrum at quarter length
items.description: States the fulcrum is placed at one-quarter of the total lever length from the object, consistent with a 3:1 arm ratio.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct includes 'Fulcrum positioned 1/4 of lever length from the object'; the reference scope is bare and omits this, so it is genuine extra depth.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the 3:1 ratio but does not translate it into a fractional position along the lever.
provenance.calibration_rationale: More specific restatement of the 3:1 ratio; adds concrete placement detail without being essential.

items.title: Lever setup described
items.description: Describes a lever setup with the object on one side of the fulcrum and effort applied on the opposite side.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question a asks how the lever is used; implicit_constraints specify the load is placed on the side opposite the applied effort relative to the fulcrum.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a ratio but never describes the physical arrangement of object, fulcrum, and effort.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Establishes the physical Class 1 lever configuration needed to lift the object.

items.title: Load is threefold effort
items.description: States that the object is three times as heavy as the maximum lifting force, so the required mechanical advantage is 3 and F_load = 3 × F_effort.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct includes 'Mechanical advantage of 3 required' and 'Load is 3 times maximum lifting force'; these link the problem's given to the required physics.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states a 3:1 ratio without connecting it to the fact that the object is three times as heavy.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Links the problem's given weight ratio to the required lever mechanical advantage.

items.title: Torque equilibrium
items.description: States or applies the torque equilibrium condition that effort force times effort arm equals load force times load arm about the fulcrum.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct includes 'Torque equilibrium: F_effort × L_effort = F_load × L_load'; this is the load-bearing derivation step.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the ratio without showing or implying the torque balance that produces it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Underlying physics principle that justifies the 3:1 arm ratio for lifting the object.

items.title: Effort at far end
items.description: States that the effort is applied at the end of the lever farthest from the fulcrum to maximize the effort arm.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question a asks how the lever is used; the physical setup requires pushing down on the long arm opposite the object.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions a lever and ratio but does not specify where along the lever the effort is applied.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Practical detail that maximizes mechanical advantage; adds depth beyond the core ratio.

items.title: Both sub-questions answered
items.description: Addresses both how the lever is used to lift the object and where the fulcrum must be placed.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sub-question left unanswered' (severity low) notes respondents may answer only one of the two parts.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the ratio or only the qualitative description, but not both.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Ensures completeness; flawed responses were observed to omit one sub-question.

items.title: Avoids fulcrum at 1/3
items.description: Avoids placing the fulcrum at one-third of the lever length from the object, which yields only a 2:1 arm ratio insufficient to lift an object three times as heavy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Fulcrum at 1/3 not 1/4' (severity high): reasoning that '3× heavier' maps to 1/3 of the way rather than 1/4.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the fulcrum goes one-third of the way from the object.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific wrong placement observed in flawed responses; yields inadequate mechanical advantage.

items.title: Avoids Class 3 lever
items.description: Avoids using a Class 3 lever configuration where the effort point lies between the fulcrum and the object, which always has mechanical advantage less than 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong lever class assumed' (severity medium): placing effort between fulcrum and load gives MA < 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that places effort and object on the same side of the fulcrum with effort in between.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed conceptual error; a Class 3 lever cannot provide the needed advantage to lift the object.
