items.title: Correct verdict: No
items.description: States that no interference pattern will be observed at D2 without coincidence counting, even if 100% of the signal photons are detected at D1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (a) asks for a yes/no verdict on whether interference appears at D2 without coincidence counting; the reference answer and all three rollouts agree the answer is No.
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers 'Yes' or claims interference appears unconditionally at D2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core verdict of the question; without it the answer is simply wrong.

items.title: Entanglement yields mixed state
items.description: Identifies that entanglement between the signal and idler photons causes the reduced state of the idler photon to be a mixed state rather than a pure state.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agree that signal-idler entanglement destroys idler path coherence, yielding a mixed reduced state; this is the central explanatory claim for part (b).
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the idler as remaining in a pure state after the signal is detected at D1.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key quantum mechanical principle explaining why coherence is lost; central to the argument.

items.title: Reduced density matrix
items.description: States the reduced density matrix of the idler photon as ρᵢ = ½(|1⟩⟨1| + |2⟩⟨2|) with zero off-diagonal coherence terms when the signal photon states are orthogonal.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts write ρᵢ = ½(|1⟩⟨1| + |2⟩⟨2|) with ⟨s₁|s₂⟩ ≈ 0 and zero off-diagonal terms; this intermediate formalism is load-bearing for the conclusion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the off-diagonal terms of ρᵢ are nonzero or does not address the reduced density matrix structure.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Precise mathematical demonstration of how entanglement destroys interference; load-bearing intermediate result.

items.title: Unconditioned D2 probability
items.description: Gives the unconditioned D2 detection probability as P(x) = ½(|ψ₁(x)|² + |ψ₂(x)|²) with no interference cross-term 2Re[ψ₁*ψ₂].

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts give P_D2(x) = ½(|ψ₁(x)|² + |ψ₂(x)|²) with no interference cross-term, which is the key quantitative result showing no fringes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the D2 probability with a nonzero cross-term, implying interference fringes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct calculation showing no interference cross-term survives in the marginal D2 distribution.

items.title: 100% detection ≠ coherence
items.description: States that 100% detection of signal photons at D1 ensures every idler photon has a correlated signal record but does not restore off-diagonal density matrix terms or collapse the idler photon into a pure-state superposition.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts state that perfect detection efficiency ensures every idler has a correlated signal record but does not select a coherent subensemble or restore path coherence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims 100% D1 detection alone is sufficient to produce interference at D2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly addresses the question's core misconception; absorbed pitfall of claiming D1 collapse restores coherence.

items.title: Coincidence as postselection
items.description: Explains that coincidence counting corresponds to conditioning the idler counts at D2 on specific D1 measurement outcomes, which is postselection of conditional subensembles.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts explain that coincidence sorting selects conditional subensembles (quantum eraser) that can show fringes or anti-fringes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats coincidence counting as merely detecting pairs without sorting by D1 outcome.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Clarifies why coincidence counting is essential and distinct from mere detection efficiency.

items.title: Interference requires coherence
items.description: States that observing an interference pattern at D2 requires coherence between the quantum amplitudes for the idler photon traversing slit 1 and slit 2 of the double slit.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure's implicit constraints state that interference at D2 requires coherence between the two path amplitudes; all rollouts invoke this condition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims interference can appear without coherence between the two slit amplitudes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Establishes the physical condition for interference that is defeated by entanglement.

items.title: Entangled state as superposition
items.description: Writes the entangled signal-idler state as a superposition |Ψ⟩ = (1/√2)(|1⟩ᵢ|s₁⟩ₛ + |2⟩ᵢ|s₂⟩ₛ) with ⟨s₁|s₂⟩ ≈ 0, identifying that the idler photon passes through the double slit in a superposition of path states that becomes entangled with the signal photon.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts write the joint state as |Ψ⟩ = (1/√2)(|1⟩ᵢ|s₁⟩ₛ + |2⟩ᵢ|s₂⟩ₛ) with ⟨s₁|s₂⟩ ≈ 0 as the starting point for the derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes an unentangled idler state or omits the correlation between idler paths and signal states.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merged two near-duplicates; provides the starting state from which all downstream results follow.

items.title: Fringe cancellation at D2
items.description: Explains that coincidence-selected conditional subensembles at D2 can show fringes and anti-fringes that are π out of phase and cancel exactly when summed over all D1 outcomes without coincidence counting.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts explain that quantum eraser subensembles show fringes/anti-fringes which cancel when summed over all D1 outcomes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that argues since some coincidence channels show interference, the total D2 pattern must also show residual fringes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merged two near-duplicates; explains why the marginal shows no pattern despite conditional fringes existing.

items.title: Zero unconditioned visibility
items.description: States that the unconditioned fringe visibility at D2 is zero, so no interference pattern is observed at D2 without coincidence counting.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts 2 and 3 explicitly state visibility = 0; rollout 1 implies it via the vanishing interference term.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims nonzero residual visibility in the unconditioned D2 distribution.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Quantitative restatement of the verdict; adds the visibility concept as real depth.

items.title: No-signaling constrains D2
items.description: Invokes the quantum mechanical no-signaling principle to explain that signal photon operations at D1 cannot change the marginal D2 distribution of idler photons.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 2 explicitly invokes no-signaling; rollouts 1 and 3 mention it only implicitly. The reference is silent, so this is a supplementary argument.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims operating D1 with 100% efficiency changes the local D2 interference pattern without addressing the no-signaling constraint.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Additional principled argument; no-flaw data available but conceptually sound supporting reasoning.

items.title: Avoids detection = erasure
items.description: Avoids conflating 100% detection at D1 with quantum erasure of which-path information for the idler photons passing through the double slit.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined high-severity pitfall 'Detection conflated with erasure': equating 100% D1 detection with which-path erasure and concluding coherence is restored.
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes interference will be observed because detecting all signal photons at D1 erases which-path information.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Targets a specific conceptual trap observed in flawed responses about the Dopfer experiment.

items.title: Avoids marginal as conditional
items.description: Avoids treating the unconditioned marginal D2 distribution of idler photons as though it were the coincidence-selected conditional D2 distribution, and avoids treating 100% D1 detection efficiency as functionally equivalent to performing coincidence counting.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined high-severity pitfall 'Marginal vs. conditional confusion': answering as though the question asks about the conditional D2 distribution rather than the unconditioned marginal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims interference appears at D2 by implicitly sorting idler counts on D1 outcomes while the question asks about the pattern without coincidence counting.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merged two near-duplicate pitfalls; targets the central confusion between marginal and conditional distributions.

items.title: Avoids dropping entanglement
items.description: Avoids computing the D2 probability by dropping the signal-idler entanglement and treating the idler as if it were in the pure state (1/√2)(|1⟩ + |2⟩), which would yield a nonzero interference cross-term.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Which-path label dropped': writing the entangled state but then treating the idler alone as a pure superposition, obtaining a nonzero cross-term.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the entangled state but then computes P_D2(x) = ¼|ψ₁(x) + ψ₂(x)|² with a cross-term, supporting a yes answer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Targets the specific mathematical error of ignoring entanglement; would produce the wrong answer.

items.title: Which-path info in signal
items.description: States that the entanglement between signal and idler photons encodes which-path information about the idler photon's traversal of the double slit in the signal photon state detected at D1.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts describe the joint state as correlating idler path |1⟩ or |2⟩ with distinct signal states |s₁⟩ or |s₂⟩, encoding which-path information in the signal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not explain how the signal photon at D1 carries which-path information about the idler's slit choice.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects entanglement to the loss of interference via which-path information; key reasoning step.

items.title: Final molarity 0.1 M
items.description: The response states the molarity of the MnO4- solution as 0.1 M (or 0.100 M).

items.title: Final normality 0.5 N
items.description: The response states the normality of the MnO4- solution as 0.5 N (or 0.500 N).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Only one answer reported': the solver computes one quantity and leaves the other sub-question unanswered.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states only M = 0.1 M or only N = 0.5 N, leaving the other blank.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the second requested quantity; essential to the question.

items.title: Moles of Fe2+
items.description: The response calculates moles of Fe2+ as 0.400 M times 0.04000 L = 0.01600 mol (or an equivalent expression yielding 0.01600 mol).

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed moles of Fe2+ = 0.01600 mol; this is the load-bearing intermediate for both final values.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 0.0400 L, 40.00 L, or skips this step entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate; errors here propagate to both final answers.

items.title: n-factor MnO4- is 5
items.description: The response identifies the valence factor (n-factor) of MnO4- as 5, citing the Mn(+7) to Mn(+2) change, and avoids using an n-factor of 1 or 3.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree n-factor of MnO4- = 5 because Mn goes from +7 to +2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses n-factor = 1, 3, or any other value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Central to both M and N; wrong n-factor invalidates both answers.

items.title: Milliequivalent equation
items.description: The response sets up the equivalence N_MnO4 times 32 = 40 times 0.400, stating that Meq. of MnO4- equals Meq. of Fe2+.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference uses the milliequivalent method Meq. of MnO4- = Meq. of Fe2+ with N times 32 = 40 times 0.400.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inverts the volume ratio or misplaces the unknown.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core equation from reference answer; alternate valid path to N = 0.5.

items.title: M equals N divided by 5
items.description: The response applies the relationship M_MnO4 = N_MnO4 divided by the valence factor 5, yielding 0.1 = 0.5 divided by 5.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states M_KMnO4 = N_KMnO4 / valence factor and computes 0.5/5 = 0.1 M.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes M = N times 5, or M = N without dividing.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects the two requested quantities; missing it breaks the M answer.

items.title: Normality of Fe2+
items.description: The response computes or states the normality of Fe2+ as 0.400 N, using n-factor 1 times 0.400 M.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts compute N_Fe2 = 0.400 M times 1 = 0.400 N before applying N1V1 = N2V2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats Fe2+ normality as 2.00 N or 0.0800 N.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate in the normality approach; directly feeds N times V equation.

items.title: Units M and N included
items.description: The response includes units of M for the molarity value (0.1 M) and units of N for the normality value (0.5 N).

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks for molarity (M) and normality (N); the reference states both values with their respective units.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 0.1 and 0.5 without any units or with mismatched units.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real but minor correctness detail; units distinguish the two quantities.

items.title: Molarity uses liters
items.description: The response converts 32.00 mL to 0.03200 L when computing molarity as moles divided by volume in liters.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Volume in mL without conversion' warns against using 32.00 mL directly in n = M times V.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes M = 0.003200 / 32.00 = 0.000100 M by failing to convert mL to L.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct unit handling; failure would shift the molarity by 1000-fold.

items.title: Avoid M1V1=M2V2
items.description: Avoids applying M1V1 = M2V2 directly with molarities (0.400 times 40.00 = M times 32.00) and labeling the resulting 0.500 as the molarity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'M1V1=M2V2 ignoring stoichiometry': this yields 0.500 reported as molarity instead of normality.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports M = 0.500 M from applying the molarity dilution formula without stoichiometry.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common trap that conflates molarity with normality; gives swapped answer.

items.title: Avoid swapping M and N
items.description: Avoids reporting M = 0.5 and N = 0.1, swapping the values so that molarity is the larger number and normality is the smaller.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Swapping M and N labels': the solver computes both values but assigns 0.500 to molarity and 0.100 to normality.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports M = 0.500 M and N = 0.100 N with the values reversed.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific confusion between the two quantities; both values appear correct individually.

items.title: Avoid inverted volume ratio
items.description: Avoids writing N_MnO4 = N_Fe2 times (32/40) = 0.400 times (32/40) = 0.320 N by placing the unknown MnO4- volume in the numerator instead of the Fe2+ volume.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Inverted volume ratio': computing N = 0.400 times (32/40) gives 0.320 N instead of 0.5 N.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports N = 0.320 N and M = 0.0640 M from the inverted volume ratio.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific algebraic error in the normality equation; yields 0.320 N.

items.title: n-factor MnO4- is 5
items.description: The response identifies the valence factor (n-factor) of MnO4- as 5, citing the Mn(+7) rightarrow Mn(+2) change.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree n-factor of MnO4- = 5 because Mn goes from +7 to +2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses n-factor = 1, 3, or any other value.

items.title: H-H equation setup
items.description: Writes the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation as pH = pKa + log([A⁻]/[HA]) using 3.9 for pH and 4.8 for pKa.

provenance.evidence_detail: Both sub-questions require a correct H-H setup to reach the target volumes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the wrong equation form or wrong pKa/pH assignment.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core equation; without it the entire calculation cannot proceed.

items.title: Exponent sign correct
items.description: Computes the exponent as pH − pKa = 3.9 − 4.8 = −0.9.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Reversed H-H ratio sign' (high severity): the reversed exponent yields V_NaOH ≈ 939 mL, V_acid ≈ 1061 mL.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a positive exponent and assigns more volume to NaOH than acid.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate; sign error here inverts the entire ratio and final volumes.

items.title: Buffer ratio computed
items.description: Calculates the buffer [A⁻]/[HA] ratio as 10^(3.9 − 4.8) ≈ 0.126.

provenance.evidence_detail: The divergent rounding discussion confirms all correct responses recognized the acid must dominate since pH < pKa.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns more volume to NaOH than to acetic acid.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct ratio drives all downstream volume calculations.

items.title: Neutralization equation
items.description: Writes the buffer ratio as V_NaOH/(V_acid − V_NaOH) = 0.126, subtracting the volume of NaOH that reacts with acetic acid from the HA term.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Skipping neutralization stoichiometry' (high severity) identifies the direct-ratio error as the most common mistake.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes V_NaOH / V_acid = 0.126, ignoring the consumed acid in the denominator.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Central stoichiometric insight; omitting consumed acid term produces incorrect volumes.

items.title: HA consumed by NaOH
items.description: States that remaining HA = initial HA − moles NaOH added, recognizing each mole of NaOH destroys one mole of HA.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Treating NaOH as conjugate base directly' (high severity) concerns the denominator of the H-H ratio.
provenance.discriminates: A response that leaves the HA amount unchanged after neutralization.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Chemical reasoning behind denominator subtraction; essential for correct stoichiometric accounting.

items.title: Equal concentrations simplify
items.description: Notes that both stock solutions are 0.2 M, so the mole ratio reduces to a volume ratio in the expression V_NaOH/(V_acid − V_NaOH).

provenance.evidence_detail: The implicit constraint that both stocks share 0.2 M is load-bearing for reducing the system to two volume equations.
provenance.discriminates: A response that carries mismatched concentrations or does not exploit the equal-molarity simplification.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Justifies using volumes directly instead of moles; key simplification step.

items.title: 1:1 stoichiometry stated
items.description: States that NaOH reacts 1:1 stoichiometrically with acetic acid to convert HA into A⁻.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Treating NaOH as conjugate base directly' (high severity) concerns failure to couple the HA decrease to the NaOH addition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats [A⁻] as simply the NaOH concentration without coupling the HA decrease.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required stoichiometric fact underpinning the neutralization equation.

items.title: Volume constraint enforced
items.description: Enforces the constraint V_acid + V_NaOH = 2000 mL.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Dropping volume constraint' (medium severity) flags responses that report only a ratio without scaling to 2000 mL.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports proportions or volumes that do not sum to 2000 mL.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required constraint; without it the volumes are unconstrained.

items.title: Final acetic acid volume
items.description: Reports the volume of acetic acid as approximately 1.8 L (or equivalently ~1799 mL).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for the volume of 0.2 M acetic acid; consensus correct attempts and the reference agree on ~1.8 L.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives ~1776 mL (from the direct-ratio error) or ~1061 mL (from the reversed-ratio error).
provenance.calibration_rationale: One of two requested quantities; essential output.

items.title: Final NaOH volume
items.description: Reports the volume of NaOH as approximately 0.2 L (or equivalently ~201 mL).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks for the volume of 0.2 M NaOH; consensus correct attempts and the reference agree on ~0.2 L.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives ~224 mL (from the direct-ratio error) or ~939 mL (from the reversed-ratio error).
provenance.calibration_rationale: One of two requested quantities; essential output.

items.title: Simultaneous equations solved
items.description: Solves the simultaneous equations — V_NaOH/(V_acid − V_NaOH) = 0.126 and V_acid + V_NaOH = 2000 mL — to obtain absolute volumes.

provenance.evidence_detail: The answer format demands the solution of the two simultaneous equations (ratio constraint + volume constraint).
provenance.discriminates: A response that sets up the equations but does not solve them to produce numerical volumes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects ratio and volume equations to produce the final answer.

items.title: Avoids unscaled ratio
items.description: Avoids reporting only a mixing ratio such as 9:1 without solving for absolute volumes that sum to 2000 mL.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Dropping volume constraint' (medium severity): the problem asks for volumes, not proportions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the ratio correctly but never translates it into mL volumes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Catches shortcut that skips the required absolute volume calculation.

items.title: Avoids extra dilution
items.description: Avoids stating that additional water must be added to bring the stock volumes to 2000 mL, since both stocks are already 0.2 M.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Adding water to reach volume' (low severity): reflexive dilution step is unnecessary because the stocks are at the target concentration.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses smaller stock volumes and tops up with water, or states 'dilute to 2000 mL with water' after adding the correct stock volumes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Catches error of adding water when stocks already sum to target.

items.title: Both stock concentrations used
items.description: Uses the value 0.2 M for both the acetic acid stock and the NaOH stock in its calculations.

provenance.evidence_detail: Both stock concentrations are given values used throughout every correct attempt's derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a different concentration for one of the stocks.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Verifies the setup uses correct given stock data.

items.title: Acid volume exceeds base
items.description: Assigns a larger volume to acetic acid than to NaOH, consistent with pH 3.9 being below pKa 4.8.

provenance.evidence_detail: The divergent analysis confirms all correct responses recognized acid must dominate when pH < pKa.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns more NaOH than acetic acid.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Sanity check catching volume reversal given pH below pKa.

items.title: HOMO-LUMO interaction
items.description: The response identifies the HOMO of the diene and the LUMO of the dienophile as the key interacting molecular orbitals, with electron flow directed from the diene HOMO to the dienophile LUMO.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Reversed electron flow direction' (high severity) identifies reversing the FMO pair as the most common conceptual trap.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that reverse the electron flow direction in the normal electron-demand case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; absorbs the reversed-flow pitfall.

items.title: LUMO population rationale
items.description: The response explains that the dienophile's LUMO must be populated to form new bonds because it is the lowest-energy empty orbital that accepts electron density from the diene HOMO.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer supplies the specific causal framing that the dienophile's LUMO 'must be populated to form new bonds'; all rollouts missed this exact rationale.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that correctly name the HOMO-LUMO pair but never explain why the LUMO specifically must be populated.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly from reference answer; explains why LUMO matters.

items.title: Concerted mechanism
items.description: The response describes the Diels-Alder reaction as a concerted mechanism in which two new sigma bonds form simultaneously without a discrete intermediate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Stepwise mechanism asserted' (high severity) identifies claiming a non-concerted pathway as a critical error.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that assert a discrete intermediate rather than concerted bond formation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Fundamental mechanism fact; absorbs stepwise pitfall.

items.title: Six-membered transition state
items.description: The response states that the Diels-Alder reaction proceeds through a six-membered cyclic transition state.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) target specifies 'cyclic transition state' as part of the mechanism description.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that describe the mechanism without mentioning the cyclic six-membered transition state geometry.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key mechanistic detail anchoring the concerted pathway.

items.title: [4+2] cycloaddition label
items.description: The response characterizes the Diels-Alder reaction as a [4+2] cycloaddition involving four pi electrons from the diene and two pi electrons from the dienophile.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) target references the concerted [4+2] cycloaddition; the implicit constraints specify the reaction is the [4+2] cycloaddition.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that fail to specify the 4-electron diene and 2-electron dienophile partition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Classifies the reaction type; central to orbital counting.

items.title: Bond reorganization
items.description: The response includes the bond reorganization of two diene pi bonds and one dienophile pi bond into two new C-C sigma bonds and one new pi bond, yielding cyclohexene.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) asks for a detailed mechanistic account; consensus_correct includes the 3π → 2σ + 1π reorganization.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that omit the specific bond-forming and bond-breaking pattern of the cycloaddition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific mechanistic outcome; distinguises from flawed accounts.

items.title: Orbital symmetry allowed
items.description: The response explains that orbital symmetry conservation makes the thermal Diels-Alder reaction symmetry-allowed, lowering the activation energy, and avoids claiming the suprafacial-suprafacial pathway is forbidden.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Suprafacial/antarafacial confusion' (medium severity) identifies overgeneralizing the [2+2] forbidden rule to [4+2].
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that apply [2+2] thermal rules incorrectly to the [4+2] cycloaddition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains importance of orbital interactions; absorbs forbidden-pathway pitfall.

items.title: Phase matching at termini
items.description: The response states that constructive orbital overlap occurs because the diene HOMO and dienophile LUMO have matching phases at the reacting termini.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) target specifies phase matching; consensus_correct includes the phase-matching argument for constructive overlap.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that claim orbital overlap is important without explaining the phase-matching requirement for constructive overlap.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains why HOMO-LUMO interaction is productive; specific and checkable.

items.title: Suprafacial-suprafacial pathway
items.description: The response states that the thermal [4+2] Diels-Alder proceeds via a suprafacial-suprafacial pathway on both the diene and dienophile.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct includes suprafacial-suprafacial stereochemistry; the mined pitfall 'Suprafacial/antarafacial confusion' identifies the wrong pathway as a medium-severity trap.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that incorrectly claim the thermal pathway is suprafacial-antarafacial.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific stereochemical pathway; complements symmetry criterion.

items.title: Diene HOMO is psi-2
items.description: The response identifies the diene HOMO as the second molecular orbital (psi-2) with one node between C2 and C3, giving opposite phases at C1 and C4, and avoids identifying it as psi-1 or psi-3.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong diene MO assignment' (high severity) identifies incorrect HOMO assignment as breaking the phase-matching argument.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that assign the wrong molecular orbital as the diene HOMO.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Deep orbital detail; absorbs wrong-HOMO pitfall.

items.title: s-cis conformation required
items.description: The response includes that the diene must adopt the s-cis conformation so that the C1 and C4 termini can simultaneously overlap with the dienophile.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct notes the s-cis conformation requirement; the mined pitfall 's-cis requirement missed' catalogs its omission as a failure mode.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that describe the mechanism without noting the s-cis geometric prerequisite.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real geometric prerequisite for orbital overlap.

items.title: Inverse electron demand
items.description: The response includes that in inverse electron-demand Diels-Alder reactions the dominant interaction switches to HOMO(dienophile) to LUMO(diene), reversing the electron flow direction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct includes the inverse electron-demand case; the mined pitfall 'Inverse electron demand omitted' flags its absence as a medium-severity failure.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that present normal electron-demand as universal without acknowledging the inverse case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Contrast case that clarifies the normal-demand direction.

items.title: FMO energy gap
items.description: The response states that the dominant FMO interaction is the one with the smallest HOMO-LUMO energy gap between the diene and dienophile.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) asks to explain the importance of orbital interactions; the implicit constraints reference orbital energy matching as a factor in reactivity.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that identify the HOMO-LUMO pair without explaining the energy-gap rationale for why that pair dominates.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains why HOMO-LUMO pair is selected; added depth.

items.title: Stereospecificity
items.description: The response states that the Diels-Alder reaction is stereospecific, with cis substituents on the dienophile remaining cis in the product and trans substituents remaining trans.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct includes suprafacial-suprafacial stereospecificity; this supports sub-question (d) on the importance of orbital interactions for stereoselectivity.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that omit the stereospecific outcome dictated by the suprafacial-suprafacial mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Consequence of concerted suprafacial mechanism.

items.title: Endo selectivity
items.description: The response mentions that endo selectivity in the Diels-Alder reaction arises from secondary orbital interactions between the diene HOMO and the dienophile substituent pi-star system.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct includes endo selectivity from secondary orbital interactions as a supporting detail for orbital interaction importance.
provenance.discriminates: Catches responses that never connect secondary orbital interactions to endo selectivity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Advanced detail on orbital interactions; minor scope.

items.title: NPT Boltzmann weight
items.description: The response gives the isothermal-isobaric distribution as proportional to exp[−β(E + PV)] with the pressure-volume term inside the exponential adding to the energy rather than subtracted or omitted.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sign of PV term' (severity: high): the wrong sign causes the partition function to diverge.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses exp[-β(H - PV)] by misidentifying the reservoir entropy sign.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Central result; sign error and missing-term pitfalls load-bearing.

items.title: NPT partition function
items.description: The response writes the isothermal-isobaric partition function as Δ(N, P, T) = ∫₀^∞ dV e^{−βPV} Z(N, V, T), a Laplace transform of the canonical partition function over volume.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three consensus rollouts stated this relation; it is the standard integrated form of the NPT distribution.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the volume integral or writes a Fourier kernel e^{+iβPV} instead of the real decaying Laplace kernel.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate object; distinguishes NPT from canonical ensemble.

items.title: Extended phase space
items.description: The response introduces an extended phase space Γ_ext = Γ_{6N} × ℝ⁺ that supplements the classical 6N-dimensional phase space with volume as an additional coordinate conjugate to pressure.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three consensus rollouts constructed this extended phase space; it is the core of sub-question (b).
provenance.discriminates: A response that insists volume is strictly an external parameter that cannot appear as a coordinate on phase space.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational construct enabling thermodynamic Volume function; no flaws passed.

items.title: Volume as dynamical function
items.description: The response states that the Volume function is defined on the extended phase space as V(q, p, V) = V, treating volume as a legitimate dynamical variable rather than merely a fixed external parameter.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts defined this projection function on the extended phase space.
provenance.discriminates: A response that denies a Volume function can be defined on phase space at all.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core conceptual point of sub-question (b); inverse of parameter-only pitfall.

items.title: Reservoir entropy derivation
items.description: The response derives the isothermal-isobaric distribution by expanding the reservoir entropy using ∂S/∂E = 1/T and ∂S/∂V = +P/T, yielding ΔS_r = −(E + PV)/T.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts used this reservoir-entropy expansion as the derivation method.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses ∂S/∂V = -P/T, which flips the sign of the PV term.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key derivation step; sign of volume derivative directly fixes PV sign.

items.title: Hamiltonian depends on volume
items.description: The response states that the system Hamiltonian depends parametrically on volume, written as H_N(q, p; V) or E_i(V_j), so that changing volume changes the energy levels.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts used H_N(q,p;V) notation; the reference uses E_i(V_j).
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the Hamiltonian as independent of the volume variable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate; explains why Z depends on V in the integral.

items.title: Quantum V as parameter
items.description: The response states that in standard quantum mechanics volume enters the Hamiltonian H(V) as a c-number parameter, not as an operator acting on the particle Hilbert space.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three consensus rollouts stated V is a parameter in H(V); this is the essential point of sub-question (c).
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims V̂ is already a standard operator on the particle Hilbert space without any extension.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly defines quantum treatment of volume; corrects common misconception.

items.title: Extended Hilbert space for V̂
items.description: The response explains that a true quantum volume-operator requires quantizing an added boundary degree of freedom on an extended Hilbert space, such as a direct integral over V or a tensor product with L²(ℝ⁺).

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts disagreed on whether the extended space is a direct integral or a tensor product, but all agreed some extension is needed for V̂.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims V̂ maps directly from the classical volume function to an operator on the unextended particle Hilbert space.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Second half of quantum volume-operator discussion; non-trivial construction.

items.title: Volume function discussion
items.description: The response provides an explicit discussion of the implications of treating volume as a variable for defining a Volume function on phase space in thermodynamics.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) explicitly asks for this conceptual discussion of the Volume function on phase space.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the derivation and the quantum discussion but skips the thermodynamic phase-space analysis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Entire sub-question (b); gold-standard coverage anchor.

items.title: Volume-operator discussion
items.description: The response provides an explicit discussion of the volume-operator concept in quantum mechanics, relating the classical volume variable to its quantum mechanical treatment.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sub-question (c) left blank' (severity: medium): the quantum discussion is conceptually distinct and easy to skip.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives the distribution and discusses the classical Volume function but says nothing about quantum mechanics.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Entire sub-question (c); required by question structure.

items.title: Piston Hamiltonian form
items.description: The response writes an extended piston Hamiltonian of the form H_ext = H_N(V̂) + p̂_V²/(2M) + P V̂ that includes a kinetic term for the volume degree of freedom and the pressure coupling.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three consensus rollouts wrote this extended Hamiltonian structure with [V̂, p̂_V] = iℏ.
provenance.discriminates: A response that introduces V̂ but never specifies the extended Hamiltonian in which it appears.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds concrete depth on quantum volume-operator mechanics.

items.title: Gibbs free energy relation
items.description: The response states the relation G = −k_B T ln Δ connecting the isothermal-isobaric partition function to the Gibbs free energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Only rollout 3 explicitly stated G = -k_B T ln Δ; the reference is silent on thermodynamic potentials.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives the distribution but never connects it to a named thermodynamic potential.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct thermodynamic bridge; real but secondary depth.

items.title: Canonical phase-space measure
items.description: The response includes the canonical phase-space measure factor 1/(N! h^{3N}) in the isothermal-isobaric partition function.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts included this standard Gibbs measure factor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes only the Boltzmann factor without any measure prefactor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Technically correct normalization; minor against conceptual points.

items.title: Avoids Fourier volume kernel
items.description: Avoids writing the volume integral of the isothermal-isobaric partition function as ∫ dV e^{+iβPV} Z(V) or any oscillatory Fourier-type kernel in the volume variable.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Fourier instead of Laplace' (severity: medium): an imaginary kernel gives a complex, non-convergent partition function.
provenance.discriminates: A response that misidentifies the NPT partition function as a Fourier transform rather than a Laplace transform.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed sign-error variant; Laplace transform not Fourier.

items.title: Avoids overstated quantum correspondence
items.description: Avoids claiming that the classical volume function on phase space automatically corresponds to a standard quantum operator V̂ acting on the particle Hilbert space without any boundary extension.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Overstated quantum correspondence' (severity: medium): V is not a function of q,p alone, so the naive correspondence principle does not apply.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts V̂ exists on H_particles with volume eigenvalues, adding no new degree of freedom.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed misconception; conflation of classical variable with native operator.

items.title: Beta definition
items.description: The response defines β = 1/(k_B T) when introducing the isothermal-isobaric distribution.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts included this definition; it anchors the meaning of β in the NPT weight.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses β without defining it or defines it with the wrong sign or wrong constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Standard notation anchor; minimal discriminative value.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Qualified well-definedness
items.description: States that molecular structures are well-defined according to quantum mechanics, but with limitations due to the Born-Oppenheimer approximation and the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for a qualified claim about the well-definedness of molecular structures; all rollouts agree on a qualified yes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a simple unqualified yes or no without acknowledging quantum limitations.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core thesis of the question; no correct answer exists without it.

items.title: BO separates via mass
items.description: States that the Born-Oppenheimer approximation separates nuclear and electronic motion because the nuclear mass is larger than the electron mass.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among all rollouts that BO exploits M_nuc >> m_e; this is the load-bearing justification for treating nuclei as nearly fixed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that invokes the Born-Oppenheimer approximation without explaining the mass-ratio basis for the separation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational mechanism for the entire discussion; without it the BO explanation is unsupported.

items.title: Large mass allows localization
items.description: States that the large nuclear mass relative to the electron mass allows nuclei to be localized with a small kinetic energy cost.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: KE scale ~ ħ²/(M(Δx)²) is small because M is large, enabling localization of nuclei.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the uncertainty principle prevents exact localization without explaining why nuclei can still be localized to high precision.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate reasoning connecting mass ratio to the feasibility of well-defined structures.

items.title: PES minima define geometry
items.description: States that the Born-Oppenheimer approximation produces a potential energy surface whose minima define equilibrium molecular geometries.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts: PES U(R) = E_el(R) + V_NN(R), with minima at R_0 giving the molecular structure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions the Born-Oppenheimer approximation but never connects it to a potential energy surface and equilibrium geometry.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly explains how molecular structures arise from the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.

items.title: Heisenberg limits localization
items.description: States that the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, via Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2, prevents exact localization of nuclei.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires analysis of how the uncertainty principle constrains nuclear localization; all rollouts identify Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2 as the relevant relation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses the Born-Oppenheimer approximation but never invokes the Heisenberg uncertainty principle as a constraint on nuclear positions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly requested sub-question; formula anchor makes it checkable and high-value.

items.title: Zero-point motion limits precision
items.description: States that nuclei possess zero-point motion and are therefore not pinned to exact fixed points, limiting molecular structures to the precision of the vibrational zero-point amplitude.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: structure is well-defined to excellent approximation but not absolutely exact; zero-point amplitude sets the precision.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims molecular structure is exactly well-defined once the Born-Oppenheimer approximation is applied.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects Heisenberg to practical structural limits; absorbs the pitfall of treating nuclei as classical points.

items.title: Splitting sets timescale
items.description: States that the energy splitting between different superpositions sets an oscillation or beating timescale on the order of ħ/ΔE.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) requires discussion of how energy splitting affects structural definiteness; consensus identifies τ ~ ħ/ΔE as the characteristic timescale.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions energy splitting between superpositions but never connects it to a timescale for interconversion or oscillation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly requested energy-splitting sub-question with a concrete formula; high discriminative value.

items.title: Superposition of configurations
items.description: States that different nuclear configurations correspond to different molecular structures existing in quantum superposition, and that a small energy splitting allows such a superposition to persist rather than resolving to one geometry.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: small ΔE → persistent localization/superposition, ill-defined single structure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses energy splitting without explaining that small splitting permits coexistence of multiple structures.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Bridges superposition concept to molecular structure; needed for the splitting discussion.

items.title: Large splitting drives oscillation
items.description: States that for an isolated molecule, a large energy splitting between different superpositions leads to oscillation or interconversion between configurations.

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergent: Rollouts 1 and 2 state large ΔE → rapid mixing, while Rollout 3 focuses on decoherence; the isolated-system coherent dynamics result is the physically correct primary effect.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims large energy splitting unambiguously stabilizes structure without acknowledging rapid coherent interconversion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Complements the small-splitting case; both directions needed for a complete explanation.

items.title: Decoherence suppresses interference
items.description: States that environmental decoherence suppresses interference between superposed molecular geometries.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: coupling to environment suppresses interference between superposed geometries, contributing to effective localization.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses superpositions of structures but never addresses how environmental interaction suppresses their interference.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key mechanism explaining why superposed structures appear well-defined in practice.

items.title: Decoherence without collapse
items.description: States that decoherence makes superposed molecular structures behave classically for practical purposes without selecting a unique outcome as a projective measurement would.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Decoherence conflated with measurement': decoherence suppresses interference but does not select a unique outcome as projective measurement does.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses decoherence but does not distinguish it from wavefunction collapse or measurement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added depth distinguishing decoherence from collapse; absorbs the collapse-pitfall avoidance.

items.title: Large splitting accelerates decoherence
items.description: States that in an open system, a large energy splitting between different superpositions accelerates decoherence between them.

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergent: Rollout 3 notes large ΔE makes components energetically distinguishable and susceptible to rapid decoherence; this open-system effect coexists with the coherent dynamics of criterion 10.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses decoherence but never connects the rate of decoherence to the magnitude of the energy splitting.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Nuanced extension linking splitting magnitude to decoherence rate in open systems.

items.title: BO breakdown at crossings
items.description: States that the Born-Oppenheimer approximation breaks down when electronic energy surfaces approach or cross, such as at conical intersections.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'BO applied at conical intersection': BO requires electronic surfaces to be well-separated in energy; near conical intersections a single well-defined PES-minimum structure may not exist.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents the Born-Oppenheimer approximation as universally valid without noting its domain of validity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Names the specific failure mode of BO; a mined pitfall that distinguishes correct from flawed answers.

items.title: Mass ratio numeric value
items.description: States the approximate nuclear-to-electron mass ratio of about 1836 for a proton relative to an electron as quantitative justification for the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: M_nuc >> m_e, e.g. proton/electron ~1836, cited by rollouts as the mass-ratio basis for BO.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts the mass ratio is large without providing any quantitative estimate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Concrete numeric anchor; adds quantitative depth but not essential to the argument.

items.title: Avoids splitting-as-stabilizing
items.description: Avoids claiming that a large energy splitting between different superpositions promotes well-defined molecular structures solely through decoherence while omitting the interconversion dynamics of an isolated system.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Energy splitting sub-question dropped': discussing BO and uncertainty but omitting the connection between ΔE and structural localization leaves sub-question (d) unanswered.
provenance.discriminates: A response that covers three of the four sub-questions but entirely omits the role of energy splitting between superpositions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific observed pitfall of incomplete reasoning about splitting effects; low weight as avoidance item.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Differential rate equation
items.description: Part (i) writes the differential rate equation as rate = k[A]^1[B]^2 (or dx/dt = k[A][B]^2), with [A] to the first power and [B] squared, consistent with the reaction being first order in A and second order in B.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Swapped exponents in rate law' (severity high).
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns second order to A and first order to B.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer for part (i); wrong exponents or structure breaks correctness entirely.

items.title: Rate constant present
items.description: The differential rate equation in part (i) includes a rate constant k or K multiplying the concentration terms.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Omitting rate constant k' foresees writing Rate = [A][B]^2 without k.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the rate law without any proportionality constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Omitting k is a common error; its presence is a required element of the equation.

items.title: Part ii result 9 times
items.description: Part (ii) states that when the concentration of B is tripled, the rate becomes 9 times the original rate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Linear not exponential for B' (severity high).
provenance.discriminates: A response that applies the concentration change linearly because B is second order.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Final numeric answer for part (ii); directly tests squaring of the tripled concentration.

items.title: Part ii shows 3B squared
items.description: Part (ii) shows the new rate expression substituting [3B] and evaluating 3^2 = 9 to obtain the rate multiplier.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference shows r1 = k[A]^1[3B]^2 then r1 = 9 × r0; rollouts stated only the final factor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts 9× without any substitution or derivation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate step for the part (ii) answer; distinguishes reasoning from guessing.

items.title: Part ii keeps A fixed
items.description: Part (ii) keeps the concentration of A unchanged and only varies [B] when computing how the rate is affected.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (ii) specifies only [B] is tripled; reference keeps [A]^1 fixed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that also changes [A] in part (ii).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct reasoning step; changing A would corrupt the part (ii) comparison.

items.title: Part ii baseline rate
items.description: Part (ii) writes an original rate expression r0 = k[A][B]^2 as the baseline before applying the tripling of B.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly writes r0 = K[A]^1[B]^2 before r1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to the final factor without stating the baseline rate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Baseline expression anchors the comparison; demonstrates correct method.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: Part (iii) writes an original rate expression r0 = k[A][B]^2 as the baseline before applying the doubling of A and B.

items.title: Part iii result 8 times
items.description: Part (iii) states that when the concentration of both A and B is doubled, the rate becomes 8 times the original rate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (iii) target: multiplicative factor; reference gives r2 = 8 × r0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 4×, 6×, or any factor other than 8.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Final numeric answer for part (iii); correctness collapses without the right multiplier.

items.title: Part iii substitution
items.description: Part (iii) shows the new rate expression substituting [2A]^1 and [2B]^2 to derive the rate factor of 8.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference shows r2 = k[2A]^1[2B]^2 then r2 = 8 × r0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts 8× without showing the substitution into the rate law.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate derivation; shows the doubled concentrations are raised to correct orders.

items.title: Part iii multiply factors
items.description: Part (iii) computes the rate-change factor as 2^1 × 2^2 = 8, multiplying the per-reactant contributions rather than adding them.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Adding instead of multiplying factors' foresees 2 + 4 = 6.
provenance.discriminates: A response that adds the individual factors to get 6×.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes correct multiplication from the common addition error; central to the answer.

items.title: Part iii A factor 2
items.description: Part (iii) raises the doubled concentration ratio for A to the first power, contributing a factor of 2 to the overall rate change.

provenance.evidence_detail: A is first order; doubling gives 2^1 = 2, part of the 2^1 × 2^2 = 8 derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that raises A's factor to the wrong power.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Intermediate factor for A; verifies the first-order dependence is applied correctly.

items.title: Part iii B factor 4
items.description: Part (iii) raises the doubled concentration ratio for B to the second power, contributing a factor of 4 to the overall rate change.

provenance.evidence_detail: B is second order; doubling gives 2^2 = 4, part of the 2^1 × 2^2 = 8 derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that raises B's factor to the wrong power.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Intermediate factor for B; verifies the second-order dependence is applied correctly.

items.title: Avoid adding factors
items.description: Avoids computing the part (iii) rate change as 2^1 + 2^2 = 6 instead of 2^1 × 2^2 = 8.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Adding instead of multiplying factors' (severity high).
provenance.discriminates: A response that sums the individual order contributions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed specific trap; adding per-reactant factors yields a plausible but wrong answer.

items.title: Avoid ignoring orders
items.description: Avoids computing the part (iii) rate change as 2 × 2 = 4 by ignoring the reaction orders of A and B.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Linear scaling for both reactants' (severity medium).
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats both reactants as first order and multiplies 2 by 2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed trap where both concentrations are doubled but orders are neglected.

items.title: dx/dt notation
items.description: Part (i) expresses the differential rate using dx/dt or an equivalent time-derivative notation for the rate of reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses dx/dt notation; rollouts used 'rate' or -d[A]/dt instead.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only an expression like k[A][B]^2 with no indication it is a rate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Optional notation detail; correct in either form but dx/dt is the textbook convention.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Linear dispersion
items.description: The response states that the energy-momentum relationship in graphene is linear, i.e., energy E is directly proportional to momentum, analogous to E = pc for massless particles.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks why electrons are relativistic; the linear E ∝ p dispersion is the load-bearing fact.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains relativity qualitatively without naming the linear energy-momentum relationship.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core of the question; linear E∝p is the foundational fact everything else follows from.

items.title: Velocity independent of energy
items.description: The response states that the characteristic velocity of electrons in graphene is independent of energy level, as a direct consequence of the linear dispersion relation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Velocity depends on energy' (medium severity): the default non-relativistic intuition that v increases with E.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims higher-energy electrons move faster through graphene with an energy-dependent velocity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers why linear dispersion implies relativistic-like behavior; load-bearing consequence.

items.title: Dirac analogy not speed
items.description: The response states that 'relativistic' refers to the Dirac-like mathematical form of the dynamics arising from linear dispersion, rather than the electrons' speed being close to the speed of light.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Relativistic = fast' (high severity): the defining mistake is conflating relativistic with large Lorentz factor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that invokes γ ≈ 1.0000045 or claims 0.003c is 'fast enough' for relativistic effects.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Resolves the central paradox in the question; without this the explanation misses the point.

items.title: Despite low speed
items.description: The response explicitly reconciles the relativistic label with the fact that the characteristic velocity of electrons in graphene is much less than the speed of light, stating the analogy holds despite this low speed.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Relativistic = fast' (high severity) and the question's explicit 'despite their speed being much less' framing.
provenance.discriminates: A response that never addresses the tension between the low velocity and the relativistic description.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly demands this reconciliation; addresses the 'despite' framing directly.

items.title: v_F replaces c
items.description: The response states that the Fermi velocity v_F replaces c in the effective Dirac theory for graphene, giving energy E = v_F p instead of E = pc, and avoids substituting the speed of light c into the effective Dirac equation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All consensus rollouts agree v_F replaces c in the effective Dirac equation; the reference frames the constant velocity as the key insight.
provenance.discriminates: A response that substitutes the literal speed of light c into the graphene dispersion relation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate identifying the structural replacement that makes graphene effectively relativistic.

items.title: v_F numerical value
items.description: The response gives the Fermi velocity as approximately 0.003c or about 10^6 m/s for electrons in graphene.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus rollouts agree on v_F ≈ 0.003c ≈ 10^6 m/s; the question supplies the 0.3% figure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the numerical value of the characteristic velocity entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Concrete anchor tying the 0.3% figure to the correct physical quantity; adds precision.

items.title: Dirac Hamiltonian
items.description: The response identifies a Dirac-like Hamiltonian H = v_F σ·p describing electrons in graphene near the K/K' points.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus rollouts identify the 2D massless Dirac Hamiltonian H = v_F σ·p as the formal basis for calling the quasiparticles relativistic.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains the linear dispersion but never connects it to a Dirac equation or Dirac-like Hamiltonian.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific mathematical structure underpinning the relativistic analogy; strong intermediate result.

items.title: Quasiparticle effective mass
items.description: The response states that the charge carriers in graphene are quasiparticles with zero effective mass described by the Dirac equation rather than the Schrödinger equation, and avoids stating they have zero rest mass m_e = 0.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Literal zero rest mass' (medium severity): conflating quasiparticle effective mass with bare electron mass.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims actual electrons in graphene are massless particles with zero rest mass.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Clarifies massless means effective mass, not literal rest mass; prevents a common misconception.

items.title: Conductivity addressed
items.description: The response addresses the implications of relativistic behavior on the conductivity of graphene, going beyond the explanation of why electrons are relativistic.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) explicitly asks for conductivity implications; the reference answer is silent on part (b), creating a reference-contrast pitfall.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fully explains the Dirac analogy but omits the conductivity part entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly requested sub-question; an answer omitting conductivity implications is incomplete.

items.title: High mobility
items.description: The response states that the Dirac-like massless behavior of electrons in graphene leads to high carrier mobility and conductivity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus rollouts identify high mobility and conductivity as an overall implication of the relativistic behavior.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses Klein tunneling and minimum conductivity but never generally characterizes graphene as high-mobility.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct physical consequence connecting relativistic behavior to the observed high conductivity.

items.title: Backscattering suppression
items.description: The response states that pseudospin-momentum locking or chirality of electrons in graphene suppresses backscattering, as a mechanism connecting the linear dispersion to enhanced conductivity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus rollouts identify pseudospin/chirality as the mechanism for backscattering suppression; depth beyond the reference answer.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts suppressed backscattering without any link to pseudospin or chirality.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific mechanism linking relativistic structure to conductivity; stronger than a generic claim.

items.title: Klein tunneling
items.description: The response mentions Klein tunneling or perfect transmission of normally incident electrons through barriers in graphene as a consequence of relativistic behavior.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus rollouts identify Klein tunneling as a hallmark conductivity implication of the Dirac-like description.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists mobility effects but never identifies the Klein-tunneling-like barrier transmission.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Hallmark phenomenon of massless Dirac fermions; adds real depth to the conductivity discussion.

items.title: Finite minimum conductivity
items.description: The response states that graphene retains a finite minimum conductivity at the charge-neutrality (Dirac) point, and avoids stating that conductivity is zero there due to vanishing density of states.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Zero conductivity at Dirac point' (medium severity): foreseen mistake of treating graphene like a gapped semiconductor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that applies conventional-semiconductor intuition and concludes σ = 0 at the Dirac point.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Non-intuitive consequence of the Dirac spectrum; directly addresses conductivity implications.

items.title: Avoids Lorentz factor
items.description: Avoids computing or invoking a Lorentz factor γ near unity (e.g., γ ≈ 1.0000045) as the reason electrons in graphene are considered relativistic.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Relativistic = fast' (high severity): a foreseen wrong path is invoking γ as justification.
provenance.discriminates: A response that quantifies γ for v = 0.003c and uses that as the basis for the relativistic label.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common trap from applying special relativity literally; observed pitfall worth guarding against.

validation_summary.pitfall_weight_convention: stored on the RaR -1/-2 scale by schema.Criterion; graded by magnitude with polarity=positive

items.title: Subjective collapse
items.description: States that wavefunction collapse is a subjective process dependent on the observer's knowledge and measurement, rather than an objective physical process.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for implications for the concept of wavefunction collapse; the reference answer states collapse 'is a subjective process that depends on the observer's knowledge and measurement,' and all three rollouts agreed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims collapse is a real physical event happening for all observers simultaneously.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core thesis of reference answer; collapse being observer-dependent is central.

items.title: Wavefunction as information
items.description: States that the wavefunction represents the information about the system known by the observer and is not unique to the observer.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly states the wavefunction 'is not unique to the observer' and 'is a tool that represents the information about the system known by the observer'; rollouts conveyed the idea but did not use this framing of non-uniqueness.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the wavefunction as a single objective physical entity shared by all observers.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core thesis of reference answer; wavefunction-as-information is the key conceptual claim.

items.title: O1 density matrix
items.description: Provides Observer 1's density matrix as ρ = |↑↓⟩⟨↑↓| after the spin measurement in the z-direction.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed that the conditioned density matrix for Observer 1 is ρ_O1 = |↑↓⟩⟨↑↓|; this is also a required deliverable of sub-question (c) for the density matrices target.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives Observer 1 a mixed or unconditioned state instead of the pure collapsed state.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key technical result; question explicitly asks for density matrices.

items.title: O2 coherence terms
items.description: Provides Observer 2's density matrix ρ = |ψ⟩⟨ψ| = (1/2)(|↑↓⟩⟨↑↓| + |↑↓⟩⟨↓↑| + |↓↑⟩⟨↑↓| + |↓↑⟩⟨↓↑|) with nonzero off-diagonal coherence terms.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Dropped coherence terms' pitfall (severity high) identifies the error of writing Observer 2's density matrix as a diagonal mixed state; all three rollouts correctly included off-diagonal terms.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ρ_O2 as (1/2)|↑↓⟩⟨↑↓| + (1/2)|↓↑⟩⟨↓↑| without coherence terms, falsely implying Observer 2 describes a classical mixture.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes O2's state from a classical mixture; central to the technical discussion.

items.title: Copenhagen interpretation
items.description: Applies the Copenhagen interpretation to explain that collapse occurs upon measurement while different observers with different measurement histories can assign different valid state descriptions.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) explicitly requests an explanation including the Copenhagen interpretation; the question structure lists 'Copenhagen interpretation analysis' as a target.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses observer-dependent states without referencing the Copenhagen interpretation's measurement postulate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly requested in question; links interpretive framework to the scenario.

items.title: Triplet not singlet
items.description: Notes that the given state (1/√2)(|↑↓⟩ + |↓↑⟩) is the S=1, m=0 triplet state, not the singlet state.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Singlet vs triplet mislabel' pitfall (severity medium) identifies the prompt's conflation of the symmetric plus-sign state with a singlet; all three rollouts noted the discrepancy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that accepts the prompt's label and treats the plus-sign state as a singlet throughout.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Important factual correction; the plus-sign state is a triplet, not a singlet.

items.title: Consistent predictions
items.description: States that both observers make consistent empirical predictions and that no observer can detect a contradiction from the divergence in state descriptions.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Observables disagree claim' pitfall (severity medium) identifies the error of asserting the two observers predict different probabilities as a contradiction; the correct result is that predictions are consistent when conditioning is accounted for.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims Observer 1 and Observer 2 make contradictory empirical predictions for the same measurement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Resolves the apparent paradox; essential for explaining why the scenario is consistent.

items.title: O1 collapsed state
items.description: States that Observer 1 assigns the collapsed state |↑↓⟩ after measuring spin of one electron in the z-direction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) targets explaining how the state is collapsed for one observer; the question gives the collapsed state as |ψ⟩ = |↑↓⟩.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not explicitly identify the post-measurement state |↑↓⟩ assigned by the measuring observer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Prerequisite for density matrix discussion; response should state it explicitly.

items.title: O2 original wavefunction
items.description: States that Observer 2 describes the system with the original wavefunction (1/√2)(|↑↓⟩ + |↓↑⟩) because no measurement information has been acquired.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) targets how differing knowledge leads to different valid state descriptions; the question specifies that Observer 2 still describes the system with the original wavefunction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims Observer 2 must also use a collapsed or mixed state.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Prerequisite for density matrix discussion; sets up the comparison with O1.

items.title: O1 reduced state electron 2
items.description: States that for Observer 1 conditioned on measuring ↑, the reduced density matrix of electron 2 is |↓⟩⟨↓|.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Reduced state of electron 2' pitfall (severity medium) identifies the error of claiming the reduced state remains I/2 after conditioning on a specific outcome.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims Observer 1 assigns ρ_2 = I/2 to electron 2 after measuring ↑ on electron 1.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds technical depth on the partial trace for O1; not strictly required.

items.title: O2 reduced state electron 2
items.description: States that the reduced density matrix of electron 2 for Observer 2 is I/2, the maximally mixed state.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed that the reduced density matrix of electron 2 for the non-measuring observer is I/2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims Observer 2 assigns a definite spin state to electron 2 before any measurement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds technical depth on the partial trace for O2; contrasts with O1's result.

items.title: Unconditioned post-measurement
items.description: Provides the unconditioned post-measurement density matrix (1/2)|↑↓⟩⟨↑↓| + (1/2)|↓↑⟩⟨↓↑| for an observer who knows a measurement occurred but not the outcome.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed on this intermediate density matrix for the case of knowing a measurement happened without knowing the result.
provenance.discriminates: A response that conflates Observer 2's pure state with the unconditioned mixed state that arises when only the measurement occurrence is known.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds depth on intermediate knowledge states; distinguishes from both O1 and O2.

items.title: Measurement probabilities
items.description: States that measuring spin in the z-direction of one electron yields outcomes ↑ and ↓ each with probability 1/2.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed that p(↑) = 1/2 and p(↓) = 1/2 for the z-basis measurement on the given state.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the measurement has a determined outcome or different probabilities.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Basic prerequisite; lower weight as it is a simple Born-rule application.

items.title: Observer role and definition
items.description: States that the role of the observer in quantum mechanics is acquiring information, not causing a physical change to the system, and that the observer is an agent or apparatus rather than a conscious entity.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts stated the observer need not be conscious and can be any agent or apparatus that stores information; the reference answer is silent on this point but consistent.
provenance.discriminates: A response that requires the observer to be a conscious human mind for collapse to occur.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Clarifies observer concept; merges agent-not-conscious with information-acquisition role.

items.title: Avoids minus-sign over-correction
items.description: Avoids switching to a minus-sign singlet state in density matrix calculations after noting the triplet/singlet label discrepancy, instead using the plus-sign state as given throughout.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Minus-sign density matrix' pitfall (severity low) identifies the error of over-correcting by writing all subsequent density matrices with minus signs after identifying the label error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that notes the state is a triplet but then writes Observer 2's density matrix with minus signs on off-diagonal terms.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Plausible error; the question's state must be used as given despite the label issue.
