items.title: Correct formula
items.description: The response states or uses the formula ΔS = nR ln(V₂/V₁) for the reversible isothermal expansion of one mole of an ideal gas.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires calculating ΔS; the consensus correct approach uses this formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a wrong or absent formula, such as computing nR×(V₂/V₁) without a logarithm.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core formula; without it the answer cannot be derived. High importance.

items.title: Volume ratio 2.00
items.description: The response forms the volume ratio V₂/V₁ = 20.0/10.0 = 2.00, and avoids computing the inverted ratio ln(10.0/20.0).

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct value from all rollouts and the reference; the ratio 2.00 is load-bearing.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inverts the ratio to 10.0/20.0 or uses a different ratio.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct ratio is load-bearing; inverted ratio was a tested pitfall producing wrong sign.

items.title: Natural logarithm applied
items.description: The response applies the natural logarithm ln to the ratio 2.00, yielding ln(2.00) ≈ 0.6931, and avoids using log₁₀ or skipping the logarithm entirely.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'log10 instead of ln' (high severity); also 'ln omitted entirely'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses log₁₀(2.00) or skips the logarithm entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Using ln is essential; log₁₀ and omitting ln were both observed pitfall failures.

items.title: Correct R value
items.description: The response uses R = 8.314 J·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹ in the calculation of ΔS for one mole of ideal gas expanded isothermally, and avoids using R = 0.08206 dm³·atm·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹ without unit conversion.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong R units' (medium severity); consensus correct uses 8.314 J·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses R = 0.08206 dm³·atm·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹ without converting to joules.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Wrong R gives incorrect magnitude; energy-units R is required for entropy.

items.title: n equals one mole
items.description: The response uses n = 1 mole in the calculation of ΔS for the isothermal expansion.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question specifies one mole of ideal gas; consensus correct uses n = 1.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a different value of n or drops n from the formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: n = 1 is stated in the problem; omitting it or using another value changes the result.

items.title: Final ΔS value
items.description: The response reports the final numerical value ΔS = 5.76 J·K⁻¹ (or equivalently 5.76 J·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) target; consensus correct final value from all rollouts and the reference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives a different numerical value such as 2.50, 16.63, or −5.76.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The requested computed quantity; the answer is incomplete without it.

items.title: Units stated
items.description: The response states the units of ΔS as J·K⁻¹ (or J·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹) alongside the value 5.76.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks to calculate ΔS; the reference and all rollouts report units of J·K⁻¹.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 5.76 with no units or with wrong units such as dm³·atm·K⁻¹.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Units are required for a complete numerical answer in thermodynamics.

items.title: Positive sign stated
items.description: The response states that the sign of ΔS is positive.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) requires explaining the sign; consensus correct sign is positive.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states ΔS is negative or gives no sign.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the sign sub-question; the question explicitly asks for it.

items.title: Sign linked to expanding
items.description: The response explains that ΔS is positive because the gas is expanding, with volume increasing from 10.0 dm³ to 20.0 dm³.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) target; the reference states 'The value of ΔS is positive because the gas is expanding.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the correct sign but provides no physical reason, or a wrong reason.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the origin of the positive sign; key reasoning linking expansion to entropy.

items.title: Microstates explanation
items.description: The response states that the sign of ΔS is positive because the gas is expanding, which increases the number of accessible microstates.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct explanation references increased accessible volume/microstates and heat absorption; the reference uses the 'expanding' phrasing.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the sign is positive but gives no microstate or volume-based justification.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds statistical-mechanics depth beyond the minimum; real but non-essential insight.

items.title: Derivation from PdV
items.description: The response derives ΔS starting from δq = PdV for the isothermal process, writing ΔS = ∫(δq_rev/T) = ∫(P/T)dV and substituting the ideal gas equation P = nRT/V to obtain ΔS = ∫(nR/V)dV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference-only content: the reference shows the step-by-step derivation from first principles; all rollouts jump straight to the formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only writes the final formula without any thermodynamic derivation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Derivation steps add rigor but are not required for the final numeric answer.

items.title: Reversible heat absorbed
items.description: The response mentions that the system absorbs heat reversibly at constant temperature as part of the sign explanation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct explanation mentions heat absorption; reference derives q_rev via PdV.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only mentions volume increase without acknowledging heat flow during the isothermal process.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Supplementary thermodynamic context; minor added depth.

items.title: Avoids temperature claim
items.description: Avoids asserting that the problem is unsolvable because temperature is not given, since T cancels in ΔS = nR ln(2.00) for the isothermal reversible expansion.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Claiming T needed' (medium severity).
provenance.discriminates: A response that refuses to compute a numerical ΔS on the grounds that T is missing.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed trap: claiming missing T makes problem unsolvable when it cancels.

items.title: Avoids unit conversion
items.description: Avoids converting 10.0 dm³ and 20.0 dm³ to other volume units before forming the dimensionless ratio 2.00, since dm³ units cancel in the ratio.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Unnecessary unit conversion' (low severity).
provenance.discriminates: A response that converts dm³ to m³ and introduces an arithmetic error in the conversion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Minor pitfall; unnecessary conversion adds error opportunity but does not change result.

items.title: Qualified bilocation
items.description: States that the electron's quantum state can be a superposition with nonzero probability amplitude in two spatially separated regions, but that a measurement yields one definite position rather than the electron being literally located at two distinct points simultaneously.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Literal bilocation claim' (severity high): responses may answer a flat 'yes' equating superposition with classical simultaneous presence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explicitly states the electron is physically present at two coordinates at the same time.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core thesis of the question; discriminates correct from literal-bilocation responses.

items.title: Superposition formalism
items.description: Presents the superposition as α|ψ_A⟩ + β|ψ_B⟩ or equivalent notation with the normalization condition |α|² + |β|² = 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) and consensus_correct: all three rollouts wrote this formalism with normalization.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses superposition only qualitatively without ever writing the state vector or normalization condition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Precise mathematical anchor; separates rigorous answers from hand-waving.

items.title: Operational wave-particle duality
items.description: Describes wave-particle duality as wave-like delocalized wavefunction propagation under Schrödinger evolution and particle-like discrete localized detection events arising from the same quantum formalism.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) target and consensus_correct: all rollouts stated electron propagates as delocalized wavefunction and is detected as single localized event.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the electron 'is sometimes a wave and sometimes a particle' without connecting both behaviors to one formalism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly addresses question's wave-particle duality sub-topic with technical specificity.

items.title: Avoids ontological switching
items.description: Avoids stating that the electron physically switches ontological type between a spread-out wave and a point particle depending on experimental context.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wave-particle duality duality' (severity high): responses may imply the electron physically changes its nature.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the electron literally becomes a wave or literally becomes a particle at different stages.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common misconception; pitfalls are kept low-weight since silence satisfies them.

items.title: QFT field excitation
items.description: States that in quantum field theory the electron is an excitation of the Dirac field, which is an operator-valued distribution rather than a classical field configuration carrying the electron's charge and mass at every point.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'QFT field ≠ classical field' (severity high) and implicit constraint: must not conflate particle and field pictures; the correct QFT description requires the operator-valued distribution characterization.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes the field as a classical object with electron properties smeared across space.
provenance.calibration_rationale: QFT sub-question requires this; absorbs classical-field pitfall into positive statement.

items.title: QFT localization via interaction
items.description: States that the quantum field exists everywhere but the electron excitation can be delocalized, and that detection corresponds to a local interaction yielding a single quantum event.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) target and consensus_correct: all rollouts connected field delocalization to local detection yielding one event.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes the field but never explains how a delocalized excitation produces a single localized detection.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Bridges QFT formalism to measurement; key intermediate reasoning.

items.title: Position eigenstates vs wavepackets
items.description: States that position eigenstates satisfy ⟨x|x'⟩ = δ(x−x') and are non-normalizable distributions rather than physical quantum states, so physical localized states of the electron are finite-width wavepackets ψ_A(x), ψ_B(x) rather than point-localized states.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Position eigenstate as physical' (severity medium): responses may use non-normalizable position kets as realizable states.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes |x₁⟩ + |x₂⟩ as the electron's state without acknowledging these are not physical states.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Absorbs point-eigenstate pitfall; technical correctness anchor with high discriminative value.

items.title: Born rule probability
items.description: States the Born rule gives the probability of finding the electron in region R as P(R) = ∫_R |ψ(x)|² dx.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) and consensus_correct: all rollouts included Born rule probability density.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses measurement without specifying the |ψ|² probability density.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects formalism to operational prediction; required intermediate result.

items.title: Unitary evolution vs measurement
items.description: Distinguishes the unitary evolution of the quantum superposition according to the Schrödinger equation from the definite outcome obtained upon measurement.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (d) and implicit constraint: must distinguish unitary evolution from measurement collapse.
provenance.discriminates: A response that conflates superposition evolution with the single outcome observed at detection.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merges Schrödinger evolution with measurement distinction; central to the topic.

items.title: Double-slit single-electron detection
items.description: Describes the double-slit experiment with electrons where each individual electron is detected as a single localized dot.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (e) and consensus_correct: all rollouts described single-electron detection as individual dots.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes the double-slit experiment without mentioning single-electron detection events.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly required by question's experimental-setup sub-question; highly discriminative.

items.title: Statistical pattern buildup
items.description: States that the interference pattern in the double-slit experiment emerges statistically over many single-electron detection events, one dot at a time.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (e) and consensus_correct: all rollouts stated the pattern builds up over many events.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies the interference pattern appears in a single detection event.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key implication of single-electron detection; separates correct from classical explanations.

items.title: Avoids multi-electron interference
items.description: Avoids claiming that the double-slit interference pattern requires multiple electrons to pass through simultaneously and interfere with each other.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Multi-electron interference' (severity medium): responses may attribute fringes to electron-electron interactions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the fringe pattern requires many electrons in the apparatus at once.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common observable mistake; pitfall weight kept low as silence satisfies it.

items.title: Interference cross term
items.description: Includes the interference cross term 2Re[ψ*_A ψ_B] in the probability expression |ψ_A + ψ_B|² for the double-slit experiment.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (e) and consensus_correct: all rollouts wrote |ψ_A + ψ_B|² with the cross term.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes |ψ_A|² + |ψ_B|² and drops the cross term, losing the interference fringes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Mathematical heart of interference; strong discriminator against flawed responses.

items.title: Which-path and decoherence
items.description: States that recording which-path information in the double-slit experiment eliminates the interference pattern due to decoherence suppressing off-diagonal interference terms.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (e) and consensus_correct: all rollouts stated which-path measurement destroys interference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims interference persists even when which-path information is available.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merges which-path loss with decoherence mechanism; tests deeper understanding.

items.title: Relativistic localization subtlety
items.description: Mentions at least one relativistic localization subtlety in quantum field theory, such as Hegerfeldt's theorem, the Newton–Wigner position operator, or the Compton wavelength as a localization limit.

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergent finding: rollouts cited different supplementary QFT localization results (Hegerfeldt, Newton–Wigner, Compton wavelength); all are technically correct additions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that addresses QFT but never touches the difficulties of defining localization relativistically.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added depth in QFT localization; not essential but rewards technical nuance.

items.title: Acid dissolution of solid
items.description: Describes dissolving the solid sample in mineral acid (HNO3 or HCl) with warming to convert insoluble phosphate salts to soluble orthophosphate, including a representative dissolution reaction such as M3(PO4)2 + 6H+ → 3M2+ + 2H3PO4, and specifies filtration of insoluble residue before the analytical determination.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires sample preparation; consensus_correct confirms acid digestion as the standard approach.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only says 'prepare the sample' without specifying acid digestion of insoluble phosphate salts.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational preparation step; without dissolution no quantification is possible.

items.title: Oxidation to orthophosphate
items.description: Includes an oxidizing step using persulfate (K2S2O8) or H2O2/HNO3 to convert all phosphorus species to PO43-, and states that the dissolved phosphorus must be present as PO43- (orthophosphate) before the analytical determination step.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Incomplete oxidation step' (high severity): non-oxidizing acid alone misses phosphite, hypophosphite, pyrophosphate, or organic P.
provenance.discriminates: A response that dissolves in HCl only, never converting lower oxidation states or condensed phosphates to PO43-.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core prerequisite for either gravimetric or colorimetric phosphate approach.

items.title: Molybdophosphate formation
items.description: Includes the formation of ammonium molybdophosphate (12-molybdophosphoric acid) from the reaction of PO43- with ammonium molybdate ((NH4)6Mo7O24) in acidic medium.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) requires chemical reactions; consensus_correct confirms heteropoly acid formation as central reaction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the method but never describes the molybdophosphate formation reaction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key chemical reaction linking phosphate to detectable species.

items.title: Heteropoly acid equation
items.description: Includes the heteropoly acid formation reaction as PO43- + 12MoO42- + 24H+ → [PMo12O40]3- + 12H2O or an equation showing 12:1 Mo:P stoichiometry.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Unbalanced heteropoly equation': errors in MoO4 unit count, proton count, or water omission misrepresent the 12:1 Mo:P ratio.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes PO43- + MoO42- + H+ → [PMo12O40]3- without the correct 12:1 stoichiometry.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific stoichiometry is load-bearing for quantitative accuracy.

items.title: Molybdenum blue reduction
items.description: Describes reduction of the phosphomolybdate complex to molybdenum blue using ascorbic acid for the colorimetric assay.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts correctly include ascorbic acid reduction to molybdenum blue as the colorimetric step.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions molybdenum blue but never identifies ascorbic acid or another reducing agent.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Without reduction step the colorimetric quantification method does not function.

items.title: Spectrophotometric detection
items.description: Specifies UV-Vis spectrophotometric detection of the molybdenum blue complex at approximately 880 nm for quantification.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts: measurement at ~880 nm using UV-Vis spectrophotometry.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says 'measure absorbance' without specifying the 880 nm wavelength.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Concrete detection wavelength anchors the quantification method.

items.title: Calibration standards
items.description: Describes preparation of KH2PO4 calibration standards and construction of an absorbance-versus-concentration calibration curve, noting that absorbance is linearly proportional to phosphate concentration within a defined range requiring dilution.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Omitting calibration': relying on absolute molar absorptivity rather than empirical KH2PO4 calibration is not standard practice.
provenance.discriminates: A response that applies Beer-Lambert law directly without mentioning KH2PO4 standards or a calibration curve.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Calibration is essential for converting absorbance to concentration.

items.title: Beer-Lambert law
items.description: States that Beer-Lambert law (A = ε·b·C) relates absorbance to phosphate concentration for the colorimetric quantification.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts: Beer-Lambert law used to relate absorbance to concentration.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes absorbance measurement without connecting it to concentration via Beer-Lambert law.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Named law underpins the quantitative relationship used for detection.

items.title: PO4-to-P conversion factor
items.description: States or applies the PO4-to-P conversion using molar masses 94.97 g/mol (PO4) and 30.97 g/mol (P), giving a factor of 3.066.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'P/PO4 conversion direction' (high severity): applying the factor in the wrong direction gives a ~3-fold error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports PO4 = P concentration without applying the 94.97/30.97 ratio, or applies it in the wrong direction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific numeric conversion is load-bearing for reporting phosphorus content.

items.title: Content calculation
items.description: Describes the calculation of phosphorus or PO4 content in the solid sample from the measured concentration, solution volume, and original sample mass.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) target requires how P or PO4 content is obtained from the measured signal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes the measurement technique but never explains how the final mass fraction of phosphate in the solid is computed.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Final quantification step links measured signal back to solid sample.

items.title: Mg2P2O7 gravimetric form
items.description: If gravimetric determination of phosphate via magnesium is mentioned, identifies Mg2P2O7 (222.6 g/mol) as the final weighing form obtained by igniting MgNH4PO4·6H2O.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong gravimetric weighing form' (high severity): mixing up ammonium molybdophosphate and Mg2P2O7 weighing forms produces massive stoichiometric errors.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names MgNH4PO4·6H2O as the final weighing form instead of the ignited Mg2P2O7 product.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct weighing form is essential for gravimetric phosphate approach.

items.title: Molybdophosphate gravimetric form
items.description: If gravimetric ammonium molybdophosphate determination is described, specifies the weighing form as (NH4)3[PMo12O40] or its exact derivative with correct phosphate stoichiometry.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong gravimetric weighing form' (high severity): using wrong molar mass for the molybdophosphate precipitate produces massive errors.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims ammonium molybdophosphate gravimetry but names Mg2P2O7 as the weighing form, conflating two gravimetric methods.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct gravimetric form prevents quantification error in molybdophosphate method.

items.title: Two distinct alternatives
items.description: Lists determining phosphate as ammonium molybdophosphate and using a colorimetric assay as two separate analytical approaches rather than a single merged workflow.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer joins the two methods with 'or'; all rollouts merged them into one pipeline, missing the distinction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats ammonium molybdophosphate formation only as an intermediate step in molybdenum-blue spectrophotometry, never as a standalone gravimetric method.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Reference answer explicitly names both as distinct approaches.

items.title: Alkaline fusion alternative
items.description: Mentions alkaline fusion with Na2CO3 or NaOH at approximately 900 °C as an alternative method for dissolving refractory or acid-insoluble phosphate minerals.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing refractory dissolution' (medium severity): acid digestion alone fails for acid-resistant phosphate minerals like some apatites.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assumes acid digestion always suffices without acknowledging refractory matrices.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added depth for refractory sample preparation.

items.title: Interference and remediation
items.description: Notes that arsenate (AsO43-) or silicate (SiO32-) interferes with the colorimetric molybdenum blue method by forming analogous heteropoly acids, and mentions thiosulfate reduction of arsenate or acidity and reaction-time control as remediation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Arsenate/silicate interference' (medium severity): AsO43- and SiO32- also form heteropoly molybdate blues, giving positive bias.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents the molybdenum blue reaction as phosphate-specific without noting matrix interferents.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Practical interference awareness adds analytical depth.

items.title: Avoids mixing schemes
items.description: Avoids mixing steps from incompatible analytical schemes for phosphate, such as describing acid digestion intended for ICP-OES while quoting a molybdenum-blue colorimetric reaction as part of the same single method.

provenance.evidence_detail: Difficulty notes warn that responses mix incompatible method steps; implicit constraint requires mutual consistency of preparation, reactions, and detection.
provenance.discriminates: A response that pairs ICP-OES sample preparation with molybdenum-blue reactions in one incoherent protocol.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific trap where incompatible scheme steps are conflated.

items.title: Final answer 0.49%
items.description: The response gives 0.49% as the expected percentage of females who are color blind.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer is $\boxed{0.49\%}$; this is the target final deliverable of sub-question (a).
provenance.discriminates: Responses with any other final percentage for color-blind females.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core requested quantity; no valid answer without it.

items.title: Allele frequency q = 0.07
items.description: The response states that the allele frequency q equals 0.07, explaining that males are hemizygous for the X chromosome so the male color-blind rate directly equals the allele frequency.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts set q = 0.07 because males are hemizygous for X-linked genes, so male prevalence equals allele frequency.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that use a different allele frequency or never convert the 7% male prevalence into q.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate; every flawed path errors here or downstream.

items.title: Squares allele frequency
items.description: The response computes (0.07)² = 0.0049 and explicitly converts this decimal to 0.49% as the expected percentage of color-blind females.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts compute (0.07)² = 0.0049 for the homozygous female genotype frequency.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that use 2pq, 2q, or some other formula instead of q².
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key calculation step linking q to the final female percentage.

items.title: Homozygous requirement
items.description: The response states that females require two non-functional genes (homozygous) to be color blind, so only q² females are affected.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Heterozygous female count' warns of conflating carriers with affected females, so the homozygous-only claim must appear.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that treat heterozygous females (2pq) as color blind.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Justifies squaring rather than using dominant-allele formula.

items.title: Dominance contradiction
items.description: The response explicitly notes that the 'dominant' label conflicts with the requirement that females need two non-functional genes, and treats the allele as recessive for the female calculation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts acknowledge the contradiction between 'dominant' and 'two non-functional genes required' and follow the two-copy requirement.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that take 'dominant' at face value and compute female prevalence as 2pq+q² or 1-(1-q)².
provenance.calibration_rationale: Addresses an implicit constraint; prevents wrong-formula pitfall.

items.title: Hardy-Weinberg assumption
items.description: The response invokes Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium or random mating to justify using the allele frequency q in calculating the expected percentage of color blindness in females.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts assume Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium applies to obtain q² for females.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that derive the female frequency without acknowledging the population-genetics assumption.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Legitimate modelling assumption; adds depth but not strictly required.

items.title: Reasoning visible
items.description: The response includes visible reasoning and calculations showing the step from 7% male prevalence to 0.49% female prevalence, not just a bare final number.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) explicitly asks to 'Show your reasoning and calculations'; the reference_answer alone is bare, but the question demands derivation.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that give only '0.49%' with no intermediate steps or explanation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly requests reasoning and calculations.

items.title: Boxed final answer
items.description: The response includes a boxed expression containing the answer 0.49%.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer uses the $\boxed{0.49\%}$ format.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that give the correct number but without matching the reference's boxed presentation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Matches reference format; cosmetic, minimal weight.

items.title: Avoids dominant formula
items.description: Avoids computing female color-blind prevalence as 1-(1-q)² or 2pq+q² (approximately 13.51%) by treating the gene as dominant in females.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Dominant allele misread' (high severity): taking 'dominant' at face value yields ~13.51% instead of 0.49%.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that apply the dominant phenotype formula and report ~13.51% of females as color blind.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Most common observed error; directly produces wrong percentage.

items.title: Avoids 0.0049% answer
items.description: Avoids reporting 0.0049% or the bare decimal 0.0049 without units as the final percentage of color-blind females.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Percentage-as-decimal dropped' (medium severity): leaving the squared decimal unlabeled or mislabeled as a percentage.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that write 0.0049 and treat it as the percentage rather than converting to 0.49%.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed decimal-conversion error; doubles the percentage mistake.

items.title: Color sex-linked
items.description: The response states that canary color is sex-linked.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference opens with 'Color is sex-linked' as the core mechanism to explain the cross results.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes the pattern to autosomal inheritance or polygenic effects.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core conclusion; without it the explanation is wrong.

items.title: Male homogametic ZZ
items.description: The response states that the male is the homogametic sex, with males being ZZ and females ZW.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly concludes 'the male is the homogametic sex' after rejecting the female-homogametic hypothesis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assumes the female is homogametic, as in the mammalian system.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing assumption distinguishing this from mammalian X/Y inheritance.

items.title: Green dominant
items.description: The response identifies green as the dominant color allele.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed green (G) is dominant over yellow (y).
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats yellow as dominant, which would predict all offspring yellow.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Determines which allele is expressed in heterozygous F1 males.

items.title: Yellow recessive
items.description: The response identifies yellow as the recessive color allele.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed yellow (y) is recessive to green (G).
provenance.discriminates: A response that reverses the dominance relationship.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Complements green dominance; anchors the Z^y notation.

items.title: Yellow male genotype
items.description: The response gives the yellow male canary parental genotype as Z^y Z^y or equivalent homozygous recessive notation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed the yellow male is Z^y Z^y.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the yellow male as heterozygous or as a ZW individual.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific parental genotype required for the cross to work.

items.title: Green female genotype
items.description: The response gives the green female canary parental genotype as Z^G W or equivalent hemizygous notation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed the green female is Z^G W.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the green female as ZZ or as lacking a W chromosome.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific parental genotype required for the cross to work.

items.title: F1 males Z^G Z^y green
items.description: The response states the F1 males are Z^G Z^y and therefore green.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed F1 males are Z^G Z^y = green.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives F1 males as Z^y Z^y or as yellow.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct prediction matching the observed green males.

items.title: F1 females Z^y W yellow
items.description: The response states the F1 females are Z^y W and therefore yellow.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed F1 females are Z^y W = yellow.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives F1 females as Z^G W or as green.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct prediction matching the observed yellow females.

items.title: Sons inherit mother's Z
items.description: The response explains that F1 males inherit the green Z^G chromosome from the green female parent, making them green.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts noted sons get the mother's Z^G chromosome.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says sons inherit their color-bearing Z from the father.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Mechanistic reasoning behind the F1 male genotype.

items.title: Daughters inherit father's Z
items.description: The response explains that F1 females inherit the yellow Z^y chromosome from the yellow male parent, making them yellow.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts noted daughters get the father's Z^y chromosome and W from the mother.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says daughters inherit their color-bearing Z from the mother.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Mechanistic reasoning behind the F1 female genotype.

items.title: Female-homogametic rejected
items.description: The response sets up the assumption that the female is homogametic (e.g., X^G X^* × X^y Y), shows this predicts both males and females green, and states this prediction is inconsistent with the observations.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference first assumes female homogametic, derives both sexes green, and notes inconsistency with observations before switching to male-homogametic.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps directly to the ZW answer without testing and rejecting the alternative.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Critical reasoning step explaining why the initial assumption fails.

items.title: Parents not heterozygous
items.description: The response states that since all members of a given sex are identical, the parents are not heterozygous.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference notes 'all members of a given sex are identical, we are not dealing with heterozygous parents.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that proposes heterozygous parents, which would produce phenotypic splitting within each sex.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Justifies using homozygous parental genotypes.

items.title: Criss-cross pattern
items.description: The response identifies the criss-cross pattern where males resemble the green female and females resemble the yellow male.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts noted the criss-cross inheritance pattern is diagnostic of Z-linkage in birds.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not connect the reciprocal parent-offspring resemblance to sex-linkage.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Recognizes the diagnostic signature of sex-linked inheritance.

items.title: Full cross derivation
items.description: The response sets up the cross as Z^G W green female × Z^y Z^y yellow male with the Punnett-square downarrow to offspring genotypes and phenotypes.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference gives the full cross notation Z^G W × Z^9 Z^9 downarrow Z^9 W and Z^G Z^9.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the inheritance mode but omits the explicit genotypes of parents and offspring.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Ties parental genotypes to offspring predictions in one unified step.

items.title: W lacks color locus
items.description: The response states that the W chromosome lacks the color locus so females express only their single Z-linked allele.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts noted W lacks the expressed locus, making females hemizygous for Z-linked traits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the W chromosome as carrying a color equivalent to the Z.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds depth on hemizygosity; not strictly required.

items.title: General acoustic formulas
items.description: The response uses the general acoustic relations v = (K/ρ)^{1/2} and Z = (Kρ)^{1/2} (equivalently Z = ρv), connecting wave speed and impedance to the bulk modulus and volumic mass density.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts and the reference agree on this starting formula; it is the load-bearing intermediate for both limits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to final answers without relating them to K and ρ, making the derivation uncheckable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational intermediate relation; no direct discrimination data but required for correct derivation.

items.title: Isothermal bulk modulus
items.description: The response uses the ideal-gas equation of state P = NT/V under isothermal conditions to derive the isothermal bulk modulus K = P (the static pressure).

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (i) requires the isothermal bulk modulus as an intermediate to derive v_T and Z_T.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses K = γP for the isothermal case, swapping the two limits.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate step for both isothermal speed and impedance; load-bearing for sub-question (i).

items.title: Adiabatic bulk modulus
items.description: The response uses the adiabatic relation P ∝ V^{−γ} (i.e., PV^γ = const) to derive the adiabatic bulk modulus K = γP, where γ = C_P/C_V.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (ii) requires the adiabatic bulk modulus as an intermediate to derive v_S and Z_S.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses K = P (no γ factor) for the adiabatic case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate step for both adiabatic speed and impedance; load-bearing for sub-question (ii).

items.title: Isothermal wave speed
items.description: The response gives the isothermal acoustic wave speed as v = (P/ρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (T/m)^{1/2}, where ρ is the volumic mass density and m is the particle mass.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (i) explicitly asks for the wave speed in the isothermal limit; the reference gives v_T = (P/ρ)^{1/2} = (T/m)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the isothermal speed or gives a wrong expression such as (γP/ρ)^{1/2}.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity for sub-question (i); central to the answer.

items.title: Isothermal wave impedance
items.description: The response gives the isothermal wave impedance as Z = (Pρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (mT)^{1/2}n where n = N/V is the particle density.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (i) explicitly asks for the wave impedance in the isothermal limit; all consensus attempts and the reference agree on Z_T = (Pρ)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes only the wave speed and never evaluates the impedance, or gives an inverted formula such as Z = 1/(ρv).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity for sub-question (i); central to the answer.

items.title: Adiabatic wave speed
items.description: The response gives the adiabatic acoustic wave speed as v = (γP/ρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (γT/m)^{1/2}, where γ = C_P/C_V.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (ii) explicitly asks for the wave speed in the adiabatic limit; the reference gives v_S = (γP/ρ)^{1/2} = (γT/m)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that drops the γ factor, writing v_S = (P/ρ)^{1/2} and making it identical to the isothermal case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity for sub-question (ii); central to the answer.

items.title: Adiabatic wave impedance
items.description: The response gives the adiabatic wave impedance as Z = (γPρ)^{1/2}, equivalently (γmT)^{1/2}n.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (ii) explicitly asks for the wave impedance in the adiabatic limit; all consensus attempts and the reference agree on Z_S = (γPρ)^{1/2}.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the adiabatic impedance entirely or drops the γ factor from it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly requested quantity for sub-question (ii); central to the answer.

items.title: Adiabatic index definition
items.description: The response defines γ = C_P/C_V and states that γ > 1 for the ideal classical gas with temperature-independent specific heat.

provenance.evidence_detail: All attempts correctly identified γ = C_P/C_V > 1, and this is load-bearing for the adiabatic results and the comparison between limits.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses γ ≤ 1 or never defines γ, making the comparison between limits unjustified.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required for distinguishing the two limits; underpins the comparison and frequency argument.

items.title: Adiabatic exceeds isothermal
items.description: The response states that the adiabatic wave velocity and impedance are always larger than the isothermal values by a factor of γ^{1/2} (i.e., v_S/v_T = Z_S/Z_T = γ^{1/2}), because γ > 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among attempts and reference that v_S/v_T = Z_S/Z_T = sqrt(γ) > 1; the reference explicitly says adiabatic values are always larger.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the two limits give equal results or that isothermal values are larger.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Delivers the comparative result tying both sub-questions together; high importance for correctness.

items.title: Frequency-regime identification
items.description: The response identifies the adiabatic limit as the one achieved at higher wave frequencies because the oscillation period is too short for heat exchange, while the isothermal process is the low-frequency limit where the period is long enough for temperature to equilibrate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Part (iii) asks which limit is achieved at higher frequencies; the reference states the adiabatic result is realistic at usual sound frequencies.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns the isothermal limit to high frequencies, inverting the thermal-relaxation argument.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the final sub-question; the disputed point of the problem.

items.title: Speed independent of compression
items.description: The response notes that the isothermal wave speed v = (T/m)^{1/2} does not depend on the static compression or ambient pressure of the gas.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states 'v does not depend on the static compression of the gas,' a physical observation no attempt made.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats v_T as depending on ambient pressure or density changes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added physical insight from the reference; not essential for correctness.

items.title: Avoid swapped or gamma-free modulus
items.description: Avoids using K = P (the isothermal bulk modulus) for the adiabatic case, or K = γP for the isothermal case, or writing the adiabatic speed or impedance without the γ factor.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Swapped bulk modulus' (severity high): mixing up which thermodynamic variable is held constant in ∂P/∂V.
provenance.discriminates: A response that interchanges the two limits' bulk moduli, yielding v_T = v_S and Z_T = Z_S with wrong assignments.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed error corrupting both adiabatic results; merges two closely related traps.

items.title: Avoid inverted impedance
items.description: Avoids writing the wave impedance as Z = v/ρ or Z = 1/(ρv) instead of the characteristic acoustic impedance Z = ρv = (Kρ)^{1/2}.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Inverted impedance formula' (severity medium): confusing impedance with admittance in the ρ–v relation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports impedance values with wrong units and wrong density dependence.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Plausible algebraic sign error; specific wrong move named for checkability.

items.title: Avoid skipping impedance
items.description: Avoids computing only the wave speeds v_T and v_S while omitting both wave impedances Z_T and Z_S.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Impedance sub-question skipped' (severity medium): leaving two of four requested quantities unreported.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives speeds but never evaluates impedance in either limit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Incompleteness trap observed in flawed responses; ensures full coverage of request.

items.title: Adiabatic larger than isothermal
items.description: The response states that the adiabatic wave velocity and impedance are larger than the isothermal values by a factor of γ^{1/2}, because γ > 1.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among attempts and reference that v_S/v_T = Z_S/Z_T = sqrt(γ) > 1; the reference explicitly says adiabatic values are always larger.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the two limits give equal results or that isothermal values are larger.

items.title: U(t) form and time-independent H
items.description: The response states the time-evolution operator as U(t) = e^{-iHt/ℏ}, noting that this form holds because the system has a time-independent Hamiltonian (and therefore [H, U(t)] = 0).

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Dropping time-independence of H' pitfall (severity low) warns against using U(t) = e^{-iHt/ℏ} without acknowledging the time-independent Hamiltonian hypothesis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes e^{-iHt/ℏ} as if it holds generally, without connecting it to the given condition of a time-independent Hamiltonian.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational for the entire derivation; without it no subsequent step is justified.

items.title: Evolved state via U(t)
items.description: The response writes the time-evolved state as |ψ(t)⟩ = U(t)|ψ(0)⟩ using the time-evolution operator.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts begin by writing |ψ(t)⟩ = U(t)|ψ(0)⟩ as the first step connecting U(t) to the state at time t.
provenance.discriminates: A response that works directly with the Schrödinger equation and never expresses |ψ(t)⟩ via U(t).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing bridge from U(t) to the probability expression; no derivation possible without it.

items.title: Probability via U(t)
items.description: The response identifies the probability of getting the particular energy eigenvalue E_k as P(E_k, t) = |⟨E_k|ψ(t)⟩|² = |⟨E_k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|² (or the |k⟩ equivalent).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks to use U(t) to derive an expression for P(E_k, t); the target expression is |⟨k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|².
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the final |⟨k|ψ(0)⟩|² without ever exhibiting the intermediate probability expression containing U(t).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the requested expression for probability; central to the question.

items.title: Eigenvalue equation
items.description: The response states the energy eigenvalue equation H|k⟩ = E_k|k⟩ (or H|E_k⟩ = E_k|E_k⟩).

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts invoke H|k⟩ = E_k|k⟩ as the eigenstate property needed to evaluate the action of U(t).
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps to the phase factor e^{-iE_k t/ℏ} without stating the eigenvalue equation that justifies it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate result linking H to its eigenstates; needed for the eigenstate-of-U property.

items.title: Amplitude with phase
items.description: The response derives the probability amplitude ⟨k|ψ(t)⟩ = e^{-iE_k t/ℏ}⟨k|ψ(0)⟩ (or the |E_k⟩ equivalent), isolating the time-dependent phase factor.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts produce ⟨k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩ = e^{-iE_k t/ℏ}⟨k|ψ(0)⟩ as the key intermediate amplitude.
provenance.discriminates: A response that goes straight to the squared modulus without showing the phase factor appearing in the amplitude.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Critical intermediate result connecting the eigenstate property to the final probability.

items.title: Intermediate equality chain
items.description: The response writes the chain |⟨E_k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|² = |e^{-iE_k t/ℏ}|²|⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|² = |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|² (or the |k⟩ equivalent), showing the probability of the particular energy eigenvalue is time-independent.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts present this exact chain of equalities; the reference answer boxes this chain.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives only the first and last terms without showing that the phase factor sits between them and cancels.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects all intermediate results into the time-independent final expression; directly shows independence.

items.title: Final expression boxed
items.description: The response states the final probability expression P(E_k, t) = |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|² (or |⟨k|ψ(0)⟩|²) and presents it in a boxed expression.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) target is the time-independent expression; the reference answer boxes |⟨E_k|ψ(0)⟩|².
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes verbally without writing the explicit final probability formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Matches the reference answer exactly; the boxed final result is the requested deliverable.

items.title: Concludes time-independent
items.description: The response explicitly concludes that the probability expression is independent of time, either by stating dP(E_k,t)/dt = 0 or by declaring that no time-dependent factor survives.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks to show the expression is independent of time; the final conclusion must be stated explicitly.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives |⟨k|ψ(0)⟩|² but never states that this means the probability is time-independent.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the question's final demand; without the conclusion the proof is incomplete.

items.title: General initial state
items.description: The response carries out the derivation for a general initial state |ψ(0)⟩, obtaining an expression for the probability of the particular energy eigenvalue, not only for the special case |ψ(0)⟩ = |k⟩.

provenance.evidence_detail: The eigenstate-only proof pitfall (severity medium) warns against proving the result only for the trivial case |ψ(0)⟩ = |k⟩.
provenance.discriminates: A response that proves P = 1 for |ψ(0)⟩ = |k⟩ and generalizes without showing the derivation for an arbitrary state.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Addresses an implicit constraint of the question; the result must hold generally, not just for eigenstates.

items.title: Avoids amplitude-as-probability
items.description: Avoids stating or implying that the probability is the unsquared amplitude e^{-iE_k t/ℏ}⟨k|ψ(0)⟩ or |e^{-iE_k t/ℏ}⟨k|ψ(0)⟩|, instead taking the modulus squared of the full amplitude.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Amplitude vs probability' pitfall (severity high) identifies the mistake of stopping at the amplitude and treating its phase as residual time dependence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes the amplitude with its time-dependent phase and concludes the probability is time-dependent because the phase survives.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific observed error; real but less central than the modulus-squared computation itself.

items.title: Avoids non-energy basis expansion
items.description: Avoids expanding |ψ(0)⟩ in a non-energy basis that yields a multi-phase sum Σ_n c_n e^{-iE_n t/ℏ}⟨k|n⟩ without reducing it, instead using ⟨k|U(t) = e^{+iE_k t/ℏ}⟨k| to isolate the single phase for the particular energy eigenvalue.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Non-energy basis phases' pitfall (severity medium) warns that a non-energy expansion produces multiple phases that do not obviously cancel.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes a sum over non-energy-basis states and then falsely claims time independence without showing the phases collapse to one.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Targets a specific reasoning dead-end that prevents reaching the clean time-independent result.

items.title: Avoids skipping U(t)
items.description: Avoids proving time-independence solely via the Schrödinger equation d|ψ⟩/dt = -(i/ℏ)H|ψ⟩ without ever writing the probability expression |⟨k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩|² or the relation |ψ(t)⟩ = U(t)|ψ(0)⟩.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Skipping U(t) usage' pitfall (severity medium) warns that the question explicitly requires using the time-evolution operator U(t).
provenance.discriminates: A response that reaches the correct final answer by differentiating the Schrödinger equation directly, never exhibiting U(t) in the probability expression.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The question explicitly demands using U(t); skipping it fails the stated method requirement.

items.title: Spectral decomposition of U(t)
items.description: The response uses the spectral decomposition U(t) = Σ_n e^{-iE_n t/ℏ}|n⟩⟨n| with orthonormality ⟨k|n⟩ = δ_{kn} to evaluate ⟨k|U(t)|ψ(0)⟩, obtaining an expression for the probability of the particular energy eigenvalue.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 3 uses spectral decomposition while rollouts 1 and 2 use the direct bra eigenstate property; both methods are valid.
provenance.discriminates: Does not catch a wrong response; this is an alternative valid method that adds depth.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Alternative valid route to the same result; adds depth but is not required for correctness.

items.title: Hamiltonian statement
items.description: States the classical harmonic oscillator Hamiltonian as H = p²/(2m) + (1/2)mω(T)²q² with a temperature-dependent frequency ω(T).

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure identifies the standard Hamiltonian form assuming a one-dimensional oscillator.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the system as a free particle or anharmonic oscillator.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing starting point for the entire derivation; without it nothing downstream is checkable.

items.title: Partition function Z
items.description: Derives the partition function Z = k_BT/(ℏω(T)) explicitly carrying the temperature-dependent frequency ω(T).

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) requires an explicit expression for Z including the ω(T) dependence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits ω(T) or leaves Z as an unevaluated integral.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core requested quantity; every subsequent result depends on this expression.

items.title: Equipartition holds
items.description: Asserts that the equipartition theorem holds for the phase-space average ⟨H⟩ of the classical harmonic oscillator, giving ⟨H⟩ = k_BT because each quadratic degree of freedom contributes ½k_BT.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states that the equipartition theorem holds despite the temperature dependence.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the equipartition theorem breaks down.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the reference answer; merges the theorem statement with its quantitative result.

items.title: Modified identity
items.description: States the modified statistical mechanics identity -∂lnZ/∂β = ⟨H⟩ + β⟨∂H/∂β⟩, noting that the standard corollary ⟨H⟩ = -∂lnZ/∂β fails when the Hamiltonian has temperature dependence.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Blind -∂lnZ/∂β = ⟨H⟩' pitfall identifies this as a high-severity reflexive error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reflexively equates the derivative to the ensemble average.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Central disputed point of the question; absorbs the corollary-failure statement and its pitfall avoidance.

items.title: Internal energy U
items.description: Derives the thermodynamic internal energy U = k_BT[1 - d ln ω/d ln T] from the partition function considering the temperature-dependent frequency.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus establishes U = k_BT[1 - d ln ω/d ln T] differs from the constant-ω result.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes U = k_BT or has the wrong sign on the correction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key requested quantity with a specific formula; the correction term is the crux of the problem.

items.title: U versus ⟨H⟩ distinction
items.description: States that the thermodynamic internal energy U differs from ⟨H⟩ when dω/dT ≠ 0 due to the temperature dependence of the Hamiltonian, and that stiffening (dω/dT > 0) gives U < k_BT.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Conflating ⟨H⟩ with U' pitfall notes these quantities are distinct when ω = ω(T).
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats ⟨H⟩ and U as identical or interchangeable.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Important interpretive consequence; the stiffening sign check anchors the correction term's physical meaning.

items.title: Chain rule application
items.description: Identifies that differentiating ln Z with respect to beta requires computing the total derivative as the sum of the partial derivative (∂lnZ/∂β)_ω and the chain-rule term ∂lnZ/∂ω · dω/dβ to account for the temperature dependence of omega.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Partial vs total derivative' pitfall shows the total derivative must include ∂ ln Z/∂ω · dω/dβ.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats ω as a constant during differentiation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate step; without the chain rule the correction term cannot appear.

items.title: Detailed energy derivation
items.description: Provides a detailed derivation of the average energy by computing -∂lnZ/∂β along the curve ω(T) rather than treating ω as a constant.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) asks for a detailed derivation of the average energy from the partition function.
provenance.discriminates: A response that asserts the final average energy without performing the differentiation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly requested by the question; ensures the derivation path is shown, not just the result.

items.title: Free energy validity
items.description: States that the relation for Helmholtz free energy F = -k_BT ln Z remains valid without modifications for a temperature-dependent Hamiltonian, and avoids adding ad hoc correction terms to it.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Helmholtz F = -kBT ln Z questioned' pitfall confirms F remains valid.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the free energy definition must be modified.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key thermodynamic relation that stays intact; absorbs the pitfall of spuriously modifying F.

items.title: Integral factorization
items.description: Factorizes the phase-space integral dΓ for the classical harmonic oscillator into separate Gaussian integrals over the momentum p and coordinate q.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus notes Z is derived via factorized Gaussian integrals with ω(T) carried symbolically.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to separate the momentum and position integrals.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Useful intermediate step in the partition function derivation but subordinate to the final expression.

items.title: Coarse-grained interpretation
items.description: Interprets the temperature-dependent Hamiltonian as a coarse-grained description rather than a fully microscopic one, with implications for statistical mechanics relations.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus includes the physical interpretation that a fully microscopic Hamiltonian would be β-independent.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats T-dependent H as fundamental without acknowledging its effective nature.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds conceptual depth about why H can depend on temperature; not required for the calculation.

items.title: Two-parameter partition
items.description: Introduces the partition function as a two-parameter function Z(β, ω) with ω treated as an independent parameter before imposing the temperature dependence ω(T).

provenance.evidence_detail: One rollout introduces Z(β,ω) with ω as independent before imposing ω=ω(T), which reaches identical conclusions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to separate the explicit β from the implicit β dependence through ω.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Clarifies the mathematical structure that enables the partial-versus-total derivative distinction.

items.title: Microscopic implications
items.description: Discusses the implications that a fully microscopic Hamiltonian would be independent of beta, contrasting with the temperature-dependent coarse-grained case.

provenance.evidence_detail: The two-parameter approach highlights this distinction between effective and microscopic theories.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not recognize why a Hamiltonian might depend on temperature.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Conceptual complement to the coarse-grained interpretation; deepens understanding of the framework.

items.title: Avoids equipartition failure claim
items.description: Avoids claiming that the equipartition theorem fails when the Hamiltonian has temperature dependence, since the theorem applies to the phase-space average ⟨H⟩ regardless of ω(T).

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Claiming equipartition fails' pitfall identifies this as a high-severity error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes equipartition must break down for T-dependent H.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly contradicts the reference answer; a common and high-magnitude misconception observed in flawed responses.

items.title: Avoids sign flip
items.description: Avoids flipping the sign of the correction term to +d ln ω/d ln T instead of -d ln ω/d ln T in the thermodynamic internal energy U.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Sign of correction flipped' pitfall identifies this as a medium-severity sign error.
provenance.discriminates: A response with U = k_BT[1 + d ln ω/d ln T].
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific algebraic error that corrupts the final result; observed pitfall in the test set.

items.title: Equal concentrations simplification
items.description: States that because the initial concentrations of the two reactants are equal and stoichiometry is 1:1, [A] = [B] throughout the reaction, so it is treated as a simple second order reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Load-bearing simplification required by the reference answer to reduce the mixed second-order rate law to simple second-order form.
provenance.discriminates: A response that applies the general mixed-order formula without recognizing the equal-concentration edge case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core conceptual step; without this simplification the calculation path is wrong.

items.title: Integrated rate law form
items.description: Writes the integrated rate law as 1/[A] = 1/[A]_0 + kt with the plus sign before kt, using [A]_0 = 0.100 M and t = 100 s.

provenance.evidence_detail: Given time value is required to compute kt = 1.0 L/mol.
provenance.discriminates: A response that substitutes a different time value into the integrated law.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct formula with correct sign is indispensable for the right numerical answer.

items.title: Uses given rate constant
items.description: Uses k = 1.0 × 10^{-2} L mol^{-1} s^{-1} as the second order rate constant in the calculation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Given value of k must appear in the response's calculation to reach the correct answer.
provenance.discriminates: A response that alters the value of k (e.g., treating it as a first-order constant with different units).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Plugging the given k value with correct units is a required intermediate step.

items.title: Reciprocal of initial concentration
items.description: Computes 1/[A]_0 = 1/0.100 = 10.0 L/mol as an intermediate quantity.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference compute 1/[A]_0 = 10.0 L/mol as an intermediate value.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mishandles the reciprocal of 0.100 M.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing intermediate value; errors here propagate to the final answer.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus value among all correct rollouts; reference also yields kt = 1.0 L/mol.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes kt as 0.01, 0.1, or 10.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate; arithmetic mistakes here are common and consequential.

items.title: Sum to 11 L/mol
items.description: Computes 1/[A] = 10.0 + 1.0 = 11 L/mol as the reciprocal of the remaining concentration.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference obtain 1/[A] = 11 L/mol before taking the reciprocal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that sums to a different value (e.g., 9.0, 10.1, 11.0 reported as final answer).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly determines the final answer; any error here is fatal to correctness.

items.title: Final concentration value
items.description: Reports the final concentration of A remaining after 100 s as the reciprocal of 11 L/mol, i.e., [A] = 0.091 M (accepting 0.0909 M or equivalent rounding).

provenance.evidence_detail: This is the required final deliverable: concentration of A remaining after 100 s.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 11 M or 11 L/mol as the concentration, or that gives 0.037 M from a first-order law.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the question; the numeric result is the primary deliverable.

items.title: Units of M
items.description: States the final remaining concentration of A with units of M (mol/L).

provenance.evidence_detail: Question demands the concentration of A remaining, with implied units of M.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits units or reports L/mol as the final concentration unit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct units add completeness but are not the main correctness determinant.

items.title: Avoid sign reversal
items.description: Avoids writing 1/[A] = 1/[A]_0 − kt, which would give 1/[A] = 9.0 L/mol and [A] = 0.111 M.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined high-severity pitfall: 'Sign reversed in rate law'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that subtracts kt from 1/[A]_0 instead of adding it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Sign error produces a plausible but wrong answer; observed pitfall worth flagging.

items.title: Avoid reporting 11 as concentration
items.description: Avoids reporting 11 L/mol (or 11 M) as the remaining concentration of A instead of taking the reciprocal to obtain 0.091 M.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined medium-severity pitfall: 'Zero-conversion answer'.
provenance.discriminates: A response that stops one step early and reports the reciprocal value as the concentration.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Failing to invert at the final step leaves the answer dimensionally and numerically wrong.

items.title: Final concentration inverted
items.description: Reports the final concentration of A as the reciprocal of 11 L/mol, i.e., [A] = 0.091 M (accepting 0.0909 M or equivalent rounding).

provenance.evidence_detail: This is the required final deliverable: concentration of A remaining after 100 s.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports 11 M or 11 L/mol as the concentration, or that gives 0.037 M from a first-order law.

items.title: Correct option and value
items.description: The response selects option (b) and states the solubility of AgCN as 5.0×10⁻¹⁵ M.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks to select the matching multiple-choice value; reference answer yields 5.0×10⁻¹⁵ M which is option (b).
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects (a), (c), or (d).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Final answer; without it the response is simply wrong.

items.title: Correct Ksp value
items.description: The response uses Ksp(AgCN) = 1.0×10⁻¹⁶ in the solubility calculation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree on Ksp = 1.0×10⁻¹⁶; using a different value leads to a different option.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses Ksp = 1.0×10⁻¹⁵ or 2.2×10⁻¹⁶, yielding 5.0×10⁻¹⁴ M or another wrong value.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Load-bearing constant; a wrong Ksp directly yields a wrong answer option.

items.title: Common-ion formula
items.description: The response applies S = Ksp / [CN⁻] and explicitly shows the division 1.0×10⁻¹⁶ / 0.02 yielding 5.0×10⁻¹⁵ M.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer explicitly writes S = Ksp / [CN⁻].
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses S = √Ksp or S = Ksp × [CN⁻].
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core derivation step; distinguishes correct reasoning from distractor approaches.

items.title: CN⁻ concentration source
items.description: The response uses [CN⁻] = 0.02 M from the KCN solution as the sole source of CN⁻, neglecting the CN⁻ contributed by AgCN dissolution.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference use [CN⁻] = 0.02 M.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ignores the common ion and uses pure-water solubility.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate; using the wrong CN⁻ source or value leads to a wrong answer.

items.title: No complex formation
items.description: The response states that, assuming no complex formation, only AgCN(s) ⇌ Ag⁺ + CN⁻ is considered and avoids invoking [Ag(CN)₂]⁻.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference note the 'assuming no complex formation' constraint.
provenance.discriminates: A response that invokes [Ag(CN)₂]⁻ formation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Named assumption; answer changes if complexation is included.

items.title: Ksp expression stated
items.description: The response states or uses the Ksp expression for AgCN as Ksp = [Ag⁺][CN⁻].

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer's formula S = Ksp/[CN⁻] derives directly from Ksp = [Ag⁺][CN⁻].
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses an unrelated solubility expression.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational equation from which the common-ion formula is derived.

items.title: S equals Ag⁺
items.description: The response identifies the solubility S of AgCN with [Ag⁺] under the common-ion approximation.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference formula S = Ksp/[CN⁻] implies S = [Ag⁺] since each dissolved AgCN yields one Ag⁺.
provenance.discriminates: A response that incorrectly equates S with [CN⁻].
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds conceptual depth; not required to reach the numeric answer.

items.title: Avoids pure-water sqrt
items.description: Avoids computing solubility in pure water via S = √(1.0×10⁻¹⁶) = 1.0×10⁻⁸ M, which would select option (a).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Ignoring common ion' leads to 1.0×10⁻⁸ M, option (a).
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses √Ksp instead of the common-ion formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific trap yielding distractor (a); observed in flawed responses.

items.title: Avoids wrong Ksp
items.description: Avoids using a Ksp for AgCN other than 1.0×10⁻¹⁶, such as 1.0×10⁻¹⁵, which yields 5.0×10⁻¹⁴ M and selects option (d).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong Ksp value' shows wrong tabulated values lead to option (d) or no listed option.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses Ksp = 1.0×10⁻¹⁵ and gets 5.0×10⁻¹⁴ M.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific trap yielding distractor (d); observed in flawed responses.
