items.title: LLL projection stated
items.description: The single-particle theory projects electrons into the lowest Landau level, treating them as locked to the lowest quantum state of their circular motion.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for a description of single-particle theory with electrons locked to the lowest quantum state of circular motion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses general Landau levels without specifying lowest-Landau-level projection.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core premise of the question; without it the entire answer is off-track.

items.title: LLL degeneracy and partial filling
items.description: The lowest Landau level degeneracy per unit area is stated as 1/(2π l_0²) or equivalently via ν = 2π l_0² n_e, and partial filling means this degenerate level is not completely filled, leaving residual degrees of freedom.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claims include LLL degeneracy 1/(2π l_0²) and filling factor relation ν = 2π l_0² n_e.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the macroscopic degeneracy, missing why partial filling matters.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Divergent-discriminating result that sets up the partial-filling scenario and key to interactions dominating.

items.title: Guiding center noncommutativity
items.description: The guiding center coordinates are noncommuting with [R_x, R_y] = ±i l_0², stated as a key feature of the single-particle lowest Landau level theory.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim: guiding center coordinates are noncommuting, [R_x, R_y] = ±i l_0²; the sign is convention-dependent.
provenance.discriminates: A response treating guiding centers as ordinary commuting coordinates, missing the LLL algebra.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key structural feature distinguishing LLL physics; divergent-discriminating item.

items.title: Kinetic energy is constant
items.description: After lowest-Landau-level projection the kinetic energy term in the field theory is the constant H_kin = (ℏω_c/2) N_e with each electron at E_0 = ℏ²/(2m l_0²), and the response recognizes that no spatial-gradient or dispersion term such as (∇ψ)² or p²/2m appears.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim: LLL projection freezes cyclotron motion at E_0 = ℏω_c/2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns a continuous or dispersive kinetic energy to LLL electrons.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers how the kinetic energy term appears; absorbed the gradient-term pitfall into the positive statement.

items.title: LLL form factor as regulator
items.description: The projected density operator ρ̄(q) carries the lowest Landau level form factor F_0(q) = e^(−q²l_0²/4), which suppresses modes at q ~ l_0⁻¹ and provides a gauge-invariant regularized cutoff on the scale of l_0.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim uses ρ̄(q) in the interaction Hamiltonian, implying projected density as the EFT variable.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses an unprojected electron field operator rather than the LLL-projected density.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Pitfall-discriminating item; the form factor is the concrete mechanism for consistent regularization.

items.title: Interaction form factor correct
items.description: The projected interaction Hamiltonian in the field theory carries the form factor |F_0(q)|² = e^(−q²l_0²/2), written as H_int = (1/2)∫ d²q/(2π)² V(q) e^(−q²l_0²/2) ρ̄(q)ρ̄(−q).

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim: H_int = (1/2)∫ d²q/(2π)² V(q) e^(−q²l_0²/2) ρ̄(q)ρ̄(−q).
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the single-particle form factor e^(−q²l_0²/4) in the interaction vertex.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Divergent-discriminating; the squared form factor in the interaction vertex is a distinct required result.

items.title: Avoids swapped form factors
items.description: Avoids using the single-particle density form factor e^(−q²l_0²/4) for the interaction matrix element or e^(−q²l_0²/2) for the projected density, correctly assigning each to its respective vertex.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Density vs interaction form factor swapped' (severity medium): using the wrong Gaussian exponent for density or interaction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that conflates the two Gaussian form factors differing by a factor of 2 in the exponent.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific observed swap error; moderate weight for a concrete, checkable pitfall.

items.title: Interactions dominate partial fill
items.description: The response explicitly states that interactions dominate the behavior of the system when the Landau level is not fully filled, because the quenched kinetic energy leaves a macroscopic degeneracy lifted only by electron-electron interactions, so all nontrivial dynamics at scales k ≪ l_0⁻¹ come from interactions.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim: H_kin = (ℏω_c/2) N_e with no spatial gradient/dispersion term; all nontrivial dynamics come from interactions.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns residual single-particle dynamics to the LLL theory at long wavelengths.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Matches the reference answer exactly; merges three overlapping items into the single load-bearing conclusion.

items.title: Coulomb interaction scale
items.description: The characteristic interaction energy scale for the partially filled Landau level is identified as E_C ~ e²/(ε l_0).

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim: Coulomb interaction scale E_C ~ e²/(ε l_0).
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives no energy scale for the interaction or treats it as comparable to the cyclotron gap.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Divergent-discriminating; concrete energy scale anchoring the interaction dominance claim.

items.title: Interaction-driven phases named
items.description: At partial filling the interaction-driven ground state is stated to be a fractional quantum Hall state, composite-fermion state, or Wigner crystal.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim: interactions produce FQH, composite-fermion, or Wigner crystal phases.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the partially filled ν=1 state behaves as the noninteracting integer quantum Hall effect.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Divergent-discriminating; names the physical implications of interactions at partial filling.

items.title: Avoids IQHE topology at partial
items.description: Avoids claiming that a partially filled ν=1 Landau level still exhibits integer quantum Hall topological order or a quantized σ_xy = e²/h from single-particle physics without interactions.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'IQHE topology at partial filling' (severity high): asserting topological Hall conductance e²/h at partial filling.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assumes the IQHE topological response persists when the Landau level is only partially filled.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed conceptual trap: conflating filled-level IQHE topology with the partially filled case.

items.title: Avoids CS term at partial
items.description: Avoids including a Chern-Simons action S_CS = (e²/4πℏ)∫ ε^(μνλ) A_μ ∂_ν A_λ in the effective field theory for a partially filled Landau level, restricting it to the fully filled ν=1 state.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Chern-Simons term at partial filling' (severity medium): including the CS term appropriate to the filled state at partial filling.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reflexively appends the IQHE Chern-Simons topological term to the partially filled theory.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed error of importing a fully-filled-level topological term into the partial-filling theory.

items.title: Cyclotron gap assumption
items.description: The cyclotron gap ℏω_c is assumed large compared to the interaction energy scale, validating the projection of electrons into the lowest Landau level.

provenance.evidence_detail: Pitfall 'Energy scale ordering ignored' (severity medium): the theory assumes ℏω_c is large enough to justify LLL projection.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats inter-Landau-level mixing as necessary or leaves the justification for LLL projection unstated.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Pitfall-discriminating; the large-gap assumption is the load-bearing justification for LLL projection.

items.title: Long-wavelength regime and cutoff
items.description: The field theory is stated to be valid on scales k ≪ l_0⁻¹, with the magnetic length l_0 serving as the microscopic cutoff scale at which the theory is regularized in a consistent way.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) specifies the regime k ≪ l_0⁻¹ for the field theory.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the EFT without acknowledging the long-wavelength restriction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the question's scale and regularization sub-question; merges two near-duplicate items.

items.title: Cyclotron energy frozen
items.description: The response states that the kinetic energy per electron in the lowest Landau level is frozen at E_0 = ℏω_c/2 = ℏ²/(2m l_0²).

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus correct claim: LLL projection freezes cyclotron motion at E_0 = ℏω_c/2.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns a continuous or dispersive kinetic energy to LLL electrons.

items.title: c-ANCA elevated

items.title: Lower respiratory involvement
items.description: The response connects productive cough with hemoptysis and cavitating nodular lesions on chest x-ray to lower respiratory tract involvement of granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

items.title: Pauci-immune GN recognized
items.description: The response identifies kidney impairment with significant hematuria and RBC casts as necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis associated with granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

items.title: Wire-mesh silica trigger
items.description: The response acknowledges that the wire-mesh factory occupational exposure is a known environmental trigger for ANCA-associated vasculitis rather than a stand-alone occupational lung disease.

items.title: Inhibits iodide uptake
items.description: States that thiocyanate inhibits the uptake of iodide into the thyroid gland.

items.title: Names sodium-iodide symporter
items.description: Identifies the sodium-iodide symporter (NIS) as the transporter responsible for bringing iodide ions into thyroid cells.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed with reference that NIS is the named transporter involved in thiocyanate's mechanism.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that omit NIS or name a different transporter (e.g., thyroperoxidase) as the site of action.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Naming the specific transporter is essential to a correct mechanism.

items.title: Competes with iodide at NIS
items.description: States that thiocyanate competes with iodide for transport through the sodium-iodide symporter (NIS).

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus across rollouts and reference that the mechanism is competitive inhibition of iodide transport via NIS.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that say thiocyanate acts non-competitively or competes with a different substrate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The competitive mechanism at NIS is the key mechanistic claim.

items.title: Reduced iodide substrate
items.description: States that competition at NIS reduces the amount of iodide available for hormone synthesis in the thyroid.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly links NIS competition to reduced iodide availability for hormone production.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that stop at 'competes at NIS' without connecting to reduced intracellular iodide substrate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate linking transport competition to downstream hormone effects.

items.title: Iodide as building block
items.description: States that iodide is a critical building block for synthesizing thyroid hormones like T3 and T4.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer explicitly frames iodide as the building block whose availability determines hormone synthesis.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that do not explain why reduced iodide uptake matters for hormone production.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Provides necessary biochemical rationale for why reduced iodide matters.

items.title: Decreased T3/T4 synthesis
items.description: States that reduced iodide uptake leads to decreased synthesis of thyroid hormones T3 and T4.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Stopping one step early' — omitting the downstream consequence of decreased hormone synthesis.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that describe NIS competition but never connect it to reduced thyroid hormone production.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The downstream consequence; ties mechanism to therapeutic outcome.

items.title: Graves' hyperthyroidism link
items.description: States that by limiting iodide supply, thiocyanate addresses the excessive thyroid hormone production characteristic of Graves' disease.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing Graves' relevance' — requiring linkage to the hyperthyroid clinical context.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that give a context-free biochemical mechanism with no mention of hyperthyroidism or Graves' disease relevance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects mechanism back to the clinical indication named in the question.

items.title: Avoids TPO mechanism
items.description: Avoids attributing thiocyanate's mechanism to inhibition of thyroid peroxidase (TPO)-mediated organification of iodide, which is the mechanism of thionamides like methimazole and propylthiouracil.

provenance.evidence_detail: Divergence among rollouts on whether thiocyanate inhibits TPO; reference is silent and scopes only to NIS.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that list dual mechanisms (NIS + TPO) as canonical, exceeding the reference scope.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common confusion between thiocyanate and thionamide mechanisms.

items.title: Avoids receptor competition
items.description: Avoids claiming that thiocyanate competes with T3 or T4 at the hormone receptor level rather than competing with iodide at NIS.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong target site' — high severity, foreseeing competition misattributed to hormones instead of iodide.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that describe thiocyanate as a receptor antagonist or as competing with the end-product hormones.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Identifies a specific wrong-site-of-action error observed in flawed responses.

items.title: Avoids degradation claim
items.description: Avoids claiming that thiocyanate works by promoting hormone degradation or increasing removal of thyroid hormones.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong causal direction' — foreseeing misattribution to hormone destruction rather than uptake blockade.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that frame thiocyanate as clearing or destroying existing thyroid hormones rather than blocking iodide entry.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Names a specific wrong mechanism observed in flawed responses.

items.title: Basolateral membrane site
items.description: States that the sodium-iodide symporter (NIS) is located on the basolateral membrane of thyroid follicular cells through which iodide is transported.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts and pharmacological literature specify the basolateral membrane location of NIS; reference implies the cellular entry point.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds anatomical specificity beyond the core mechanism.

items.title: Monovalent anion similarity
items.description: States that thiocyanate (SCN⁻) is a monovalent anion resembling iodide (I⁻), which enables it to compete for transport through NIS.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus across rollouts that SCN⁻ physicochemically resembles I⁻, explaining the competitive interaction.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that claim the competition is due to covalent binding or an unrelated physicochemical property.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the physicochemical basis for competitive transport.

items.description: States that the F sound relies heavily on the interaction between the upper teeth and the lower lip to create the necessary friction.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollout attempts and the reference agree that F depends on lower-lip-to-maxillary-incisal-edge contact.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains the answer without mentioning the upper-teeth-to-lower-lip contact mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core mechanistic reasoning linking the sound to the affected anatomy; merges friction and interaction items.

items.title: Down disrupts lip-teeth contact
items.description: Explains that positioning the anterior teeth too far down anteriorly disrupts the delicate contact between the upper teeth and the lower lip needed for the F sound.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts and reference: over-lengthened incisal edge displaces lower-lip contact.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects F but does not connect the vertical displacement to disrupted labiodental contact.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects the specific displacement to the articulatory consequence; merges two overlapping items.

items.title: Misalignment alters airflow
items.description: States that misalignment of the anterior teeth alters the airflow required to produce a clear F sound.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states that suboptimal positioning alters the airflow needed to produce a clear F sound.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains the mechanism via contact alone without mentioning altered airflow.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds the aerodynamic dimension of the disruption; distinct from the contact-friction point.

items.title: F is unvoiced fricative
items.description: Identifies F as an unvoiced fricative sound.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer describes F as an 'unvoiced fricative'; rollouts did not use this term.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly picks F but does not specify its phonetic class.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Phonetic classification adds depth but is not required to answer the MCQ.

items.title: S is linguo-alveolar
items.description: States that S is a linguo-alveolar sibilant not governed by incisal edge vertical positioning in the maxilla.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout consensus: S is governed by tongue-to-palate relationship in the AP plane, not by incisal edge vertical length.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies S is affected by vertical incisal edge displacement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes a distractor from the correct answer; supports option exclusion.

items.title: Ch is postalveolar
items.description: Notes that Ch is a postalveolar affricate that does not rely on the lower lip interaction that F relies on.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout consensus: Ch is produced by tongue-to-postalveolar contact, not dependent on maxillary incisal edge vertical position.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies Ch is affected by vertical incisal edge displacement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes another distractor; reinforces why F is specifically affected.

items.title: V retains voicing cue
items.description: States that V retains voicing cues that F lacks because F is an unvoiced sound.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: F is more acoustically sensitive to incisal edge displacement than V because F lacks the voicing cue V retains.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats F and V as equally affected without distinguishing voiced from voiceless.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the F-versus-V distinction; supports correct option over the closest distractor.

items.title: Avoids AP conflation
items.description: Avoids conflating 'down anteriorly' with anteroposterior displacement of the incisors.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: the word 'anteriorly' may be misread as an AP-direction adverb rather than a locational qualifier for the anterior teeth.
provenance.discriminates: A response that interprets 'down anteriorly' as combined vertical and AP displacement, leading to a sibilant answer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific misread observed in flawed responses; guards against a conceptual error.

items.title: Selects option E
items.description: The response selects option E, administering washed blood products, as the intervention that could have prevented this transfusion reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: The single multiple-choice deliverable; reference and all rollouts agree the answer is E.
provenance.discriminates: Any response choosing A, B, C, or D instead of E.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly identifies the correct answer; without it the response fails entirely.

items.title: IgA deficiency link
items.description: The response states that the history of recurrent sinusitis and otitis as a child suggests selective IgA deficiency as the underlying immunological condition.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'IgA deficiency history missed' flags overlooking this clue as a medium-severity error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that dismisses the infection history as incidental to the transfusion reaction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key diagnostic link connecting the clinical history to the transfusion reaction mechanism.

items.title: Anaphylactic reaction
items.description: The response identifies the patient's reaction after transfusion as anaphylaxis, recognizing stridor and shortness of breath as signs of severe airway compromise rather than a mild allergic reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among rollouts and reference that the reaction type is anaphylactic, not a routine mild allergic or febrile reaction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that labels this a mild urticarial or febrile non-hemolytic transfusion reaction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correctly classifying the reaction severity is essential for choosing the right preventive strategy.

items.title: Anti-IgA antibody mechanism
items.description: The response explains that the anaphylactic reaction is mediated by preformed anti-IgA antibodies in the recipient reacting against IgA in donor plasma.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts and reference agree on anti-IgA antibody mechanism as the cause of anaphylaxis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes the reaction to red-cell antigen incompatibility or unknown cause.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core pathophysiological mechanism that justifies why washed products are preventive.

items.title: Washed removes IgA
items.description: The response states that washed blood products remove plasma proteins including IgA, and contrasts this with standard red blood cell units that contain residual plasma capable of triggering an anti-IgA-mediated reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Washed vs whole product' notes the misconception that packed RBCs are plasma-free.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assumes standard packed RBCs are already plasma-free and washing adds no benefit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly explains why option E is correct; ties mechanism to intervention.

items.title: Plasma as allergen source
items.description: The response identifies the donor plasma, rather than the red blood cells, as the source of the inciting allergen IgA in this transfusion reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts agree the allergen source is IgA in donor plasma, not RBC antigens.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes the reaction to red-cell components.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes plasma-derived antigens from red-cell antigens, supporting the correct intervention.

items.title: IVIG contraindicated
items.description: The response notes that IVIG preparations contain IgA and would worsen an anti-IgA-mediated anaphylactic reaction, ruling out option D.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'IVIG direction reversed' identifies D as a high-severity trap.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects D or claims IVIG is protective in IgA deficiency.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific clinical reasoning eliminating a dangerous wrong answer with mechanism.

items.title: Avoids premedication answer
items.description: Avoids selecting pre-transfusion acetaminophen (A) or diphenhydramine (B), and states that premedications do not prevent anaphylactic transfusion reactions in this context.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Premedication vs anaphylaxis' includes acetaminophen as a tempting but incorrect option.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects acetaminophen (A) for an anaphylactic reaction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Eliminates two plausible but incorrect distractors; observed trap collapsed into one item.

items.title: Avoids type-specific answer
items.description: Avoids attributing the reaction to ABO or Rh incompatibility and avoids selecting administering type-specific blood (C), noting that O-negative blood is already ABO and Rh compatible.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Type-specific blood misconception' identifies C as a high-severity trap.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects C or claims the problem is red-cell antigen mismatch.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Eliminates a common misconception; reaction is plasma-protein-mediated, not red-cell-antigen-mediated.

items.title: Reaction timing
items.description: The response notes that the symptoms of itching, shortness of breath, and stridor occurred shortly after the transfusion of O-negative blood, consistent with an acute transfusion reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference frames the reaction as occurring shortly after transfusion, supporting the acute anaphylactic interpretation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ignores the temporal relationship between transfusion and symptom onset.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Supports the temporal link to transfusion; adds depth but is less discriminative.

items.title: Bennett's fracture context

provenance.calibration_rationale: Names the epidemiological concept; adds analytical depth to the distortion claim.

items.title: Avoids severity-underestimated
items.description: Avoids claiming that a blind school survey underestimates the severity of blindness in the community.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Severity direction reversed' pitfall identifies the wrong claim that severity is underestimated rather than overestimated.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assumes missing cases means severity is also undercounted.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific reversal of the correct direction; observed plausible misconception worth penalising.

items.title: Avoids treating as representative
items.description: Avoids treating the blind school survey sample as representative of the general population of blind individuals.

provenance.evidence_detail: The difficulty notes warn against treating an institution-based sample as representative without identifying selection bias.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes the blind school survey results as directly generalisable to the community.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common conceptual error; lower weight since other items already require stating non-representativeness.

items.title: Selects Option D
items.description: The response states that Option D is the correct answer for the definition of maternal mortality.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer and all three independent rollouts identify Option D as correct.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects A, B, or C as the correct option.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Naming the correct option label is indispensable; without it the answer is wrong.

items.title: States 42 days postpartum
items.description: The response specifies the first 42 days after delivery as part of the maternal mortality period.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed the 42-day cutoff is the defining figure supported by the reference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 7, 14, or 28 days as the postpartum cutoff.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The 42-day cutoff is the defining value separating correct from every distractor option.

items.title: Includes pregnancy period
items.description: The response includes pregnancy itself as a covered period within the maternal mortality definition, not merely postpartum days after delivery.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Dropping antepartum window' pitfall notes B and C omit the antepartum period.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects an option excluding deaths during pregnancy.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Including the antepartum period is required by Option D; dropping it is a key distractor trap.

items.title: Includes childbirth
items.description: The response includes childbirth as a covered period within the maternal mortality definition.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly lists childbirth alongside pregnancy and the 42-day postpartum window.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the intrapartum period from the definition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Childbirth is a core component of the definition and part of Option D's scope.

items.title: Defines related causes
items.description: The response states that maternal mortality refers to deaths from causes related to or aggravated by pregnancy and its management.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference opens with this exact definitional phrasing of the cause of death.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes the time period without naming the cause-of-death criterion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Stating the causal framing anchors the full definition beyond just listing time windows.

items.title: Avoids late mortality confusion
items.description: Avoids rejecting the 42 days after delivery period by invoking the one-year late maternal mortality category as the standard cutoff.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Confusing late maternal mortality' pitfall notes the 43–365 day category may overshadow the 42-day definition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that dismisses 42 days as too short because of the late maternal mortality extension.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Confusing late maternal mortality (1 year) with standard maternal mortality (42 days) is a specific trap.

items.title: Pregnancy and 42 days paired
items.description: The response pairs the 42 days after delivery with the full scope of pregnancy and childbirth, matching Option D rather than the postpartum window alone.

provenance.evidence_detail: The '42-day omission from options' pitfall warns of failing to verify that D includes both pregnancy and childbirth with the 42-day figure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that cites 42 days but does not confirm the full antepartum and intrapartum coverage.

items.title: Names analgesia missing
items.description: The response identifies analgesia as the component of general anesthesia not contributed by volatile inhalational anesthetics.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks which component is not contributed by volatiles; the reference answer names analgesia.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names muscle relaxation, amnesia, or autonomic reflex attenuation instead of analgesia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; no discrimination data but directly targets the single correct sub-question.

items.title: Volatiles induce unconsciousness
items.description: The response states that volatile inhalational anesthetics are effective in inducing unconsciousness.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree volatiles provide unconsciousness; this distinguishes the missing component from one that is present.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims volatiles fail to provide unconsciousness, or omits this contrast entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key contrast showing what volatiles do provide; supports the exclusion logic.

items.title: Volatiles provide amnesia
items.description: The response states that volatile inhalational anesthetics contribute some degree of amnesia.

provenance.evidence_detail: The amnesia singled out pitfall: the reference's hedge 'some degree of amnesia' means volatiles contribute amnesia, not that it is absent.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reads the reference's qualifier as insufficiency and answers amnesia instead of analgesia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes volatiles' real contribution; absorbs the avoidance of selecting amnesia as missing.

items.title: Opioids for pain relief
items.description: The response states that additional medications such as opioids are typically used for pain relief during surgery.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree opioids are the adjunct that supplies the missing analgesia component.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims no adjunct is needed, or names a wrong drug class as the analgesic supplement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains how the analgesia gap is filled; key clinical context for the answer.

items.title: Endpoint not drug
items.description: The response names the missing component as a pharmacologic endpoint of general anesthesia (analgesia or pain relief) rather than a drug or device.

provenance.evidence_detail: The partial answer stopped early pitfall: the requested answer is the pharmacologic endpoint (analgesia), not the drug class (opioids).
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers 'opioids' or 'pain medication' instead of 'analgesia' as the missing component.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Prevents naming opioids as the missing component; absorbs the pitfall about mislabeling a drug as a component.

items.title: Halogenated liquids defined
items.description: The response identifies volatile inhalational anesthetics as halogenated volatile liquids such as isoflurane, sevoflurane, or desflurane.

provenance.evidence_detail: The implicit constraints specify volatiles as halogenated liquids excluding nitrous oxide or intravenous adjuncts.
provenance.discriminates: A response that conflates volatile inhalational anesthetics with all inhaled agents including nitrous oxide.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added depth; distinguishes volatiles from gases like nitrous oxide.

items.title: Avoids wrong component
items.description: Avoids selecting muscle relaxation, immobility, or attenuation of autonomic reflexes as the component not contributed by volatile inhalational anesthetics.

provenance.evidence_detail: The immobility vs analgesia confusion pitfall: MAC is defined by volatiles suppressing movement, so immobility is provided by volatiles.
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers muscle relaxation or immobility instead of analgesia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common trap components; volatiles do contribute these, so selecting them is a specific error.

items.title: Avoids N2O confusion
items.description: Avoids citing nitrous oxide as a volatile inhalational anesthetic that provides analgesia, thereby incorrectly concluding volatiles do contribute analgesia.

provenance.evidence_detail: The N2O analgesia extrapolation pitfall: nitrous oxide is a gas, not a volatile liquid, and should not be used to argue volatiles provide analgesia.
provenance.discriminates: A response that includes nitrous oxide under volatiles and uses its analgesic properties to argue volatiles provide pain relief.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Nitrous oxide is not a volatile; conflating it would reverse the correct answer.

items.title: Inactive carrier label
items.description: States the 27-year-old male is likely an "inactive carrier" of hepatitis B, suggested by the incidental discovery of HBsAg positivity combined with a low viral load.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for the named HBV clinical state; the reference answer's primary conclusion is 'inactive carrier.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that labels the condition as immune-tolerant, immune-active, or resolved infection instead of inactive carrier.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core diagnosis; no correct answer exists without it.

items.title: Low viral load stated
items.description: States the DNA-PCR result of 1000 copies/ml represents a low viral load.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference agree that 1000 copies/ml is a low viral load supporting the inactive carrier classification.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to characterize 1000 copies/ml as low, or implies it is a high or moderate viral load.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key reasoning anchoring the specific lab value to the diagnosis.

items.title: HBsAg as chronic infection
items.description: States HBsAg positivity indicates the virus is present as an ongoing chronic infection rather than a past or resolved infection.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Resolved vs. chronic confusion': incorrect interpretation treats low viral load as resolved infection; correct approach notes HBsAg positivity defines ongoing chronic infection.
provenance.discriminates: A response that interprets HBsAg positivity with low DNA as resolved or past hepatitis B rather than ongoing chronic infection.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes active chronic infection from resolved hepatitis B.

items.title: Hedged diagnosis language
items.description: Uses hedging language such as "likely" when stating the inactive carrier diagnosis given the limited data provided.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Staging without ALT/HBeAg': definitive labeling without acknowledging missing data is the mistake; the reference uses 'likely' rather than stating the diagnosis as confirmed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the inactive carrier diagnosis as definitive or confirmed without any hedging language.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Reflects clinical uncertainty appropriate to incidental finding with single values.

items.title: No active replication
items.description: States inactive carriers typically have the virus present without active replication.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states 'Inactive carriers typically have the virus present without active replication or damage to the liver.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the virus is actively replicating in the inactive carrier state, or that active replication is present.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Defines a defining feature of the inactive carrier state.

items.title: No liver damage
items.description: States inactive carriers have no damage to the liver.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states inactive carriers have the virus 'without active replication or damage to the liver.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the inactive carrier state involves liver damage or active hepatitis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Supporting clinical feature of the inactive carrier condition.

items.title: Often asymptomatic
items.description: States inactive carriers often lack symptoms.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states 'they often lack symptoms.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the inactive carrier state is symptomatic or that symptoms are expected.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added clinical context; lower discriminative importance.

items.title: Monitoring recommended
items.description: Recommends regular monitoring by a healthcare provider to ensure the condition remains stable and to check for changes in viral activity or liver health.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states 'Regular monitoring by a healthcare provider is advisable'; none of the rollouts included this management recommendation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ends at the diagnostic label without any mention of ongoing follow-up or monitoring.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Safety-relevant follow-up; clinically required for inactive carriers.

items.title: Copies to IU conversion
items.description: Converts 1000 copies/ml to approximately 200 IU/ml.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts performed the conversion of 1000 copies/ml to approximately 200 IU/ml using ~5 copies/IU; the reference is silent but does not contradict this.
provenance.discriminates: A response that converts 1000 copies/ml to a substantially different IU/ml value or does not attempt any conversion when discussing thresholds.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added depth; not required for the core diagnosis.

items.title: Avoids immune-tolerant phase
items.description: Avoids classifying the 27-year-old as being in the immune-tolerant phase of hepatitis B.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Immune-tolerant phase confusion': young age may tempt classification as immune-tolerant, but 1000 copies/ml is far below the >20,000 IU/ml typical of that phase.
provenance.discriminates: A response that labels the condition as immune-tolerant or immunotolerant chronic HBV infection based on the patient's young age.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific misclassification error observed in flawed responses.

items.title: Avoids resolved hepatitis B
items.description: Avoids labeling the condition as resolved hepatitis B or past infection.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Resolved vs. chronic confusion': a very low viral load can be conflated with clearance, but HBsAg positivity defines ongoing chronic infection.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the patient has resolved hepatitis B, past infection, or immunity rather than chronic inactive carriage.
provenance.calibration_rationale: HBsAg positivity contradicts resolved infection; observed error.

items.title: Avoids wrong DNA threshold
items.description: Avoids citing a wrong HBV DNA threshold such as <20,000 IU/ml when justifying the inactive carrier classification for the DNA-PCR result of 1000 copies/ml.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Threshold value confusion': citing <20,000 IU/ml (the older HBeAg-positive immune-active threshold) instead of the standard <2000 IU/ml for inactive carrier state.
provenance.discriminates: A response that justifies the inactive carrier label using <20,000 IU/ml or another incorrect threshold rather than the correct <2000 IU/ml cutoff.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific threshold error observed; anchors to the given value.

items.title: Diagnosis is bulimia
items.description: Response states the diagnosed condition is bulimia nervosa.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks for pharmacotherapy for the diagnosed condition, and the reference identifies bulimia nervosa as the diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that diagnoses anorexia nervosa or binge eating disorder instead of bulimia nervosa.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core diagnosis; without it the pharmacotherapy selection is ungrounded.

items.title: Names fluoxetine
items.description: Response names fluoxetine as the recommended pharmacotherapy for bulimia nervosa and connects this recommendation to the diagnosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer names fluoxetine as the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for bulimia nervosa.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names a different medication or only gives a generic drug class without specifying fluoxetine.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly answers the single asked quantity; no partial credit without it.

items.title: Identifies SSRI class
items.description: Response identifies fluoxetine as a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer specifies fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).
provenance.discriminates: A response that names fluoxetine but misclassifies its drug class or omits it entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key pharmacologic classification anchoring the choice of agent.

items.title: Only FDA-approved agent
items.description: Response states fluoxetine is the only medication specifically FDA-approved for treating bulimia nervosa.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states fluoxetine is the only medication specifically approved by the FDA for treating this condition.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies other medications are also FDA-approved for bulimia nervosa.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes fluoxetine from off-label alternatives; reference-anchored fact.

items.title: Reduces binge-purge cycles
items.description: Response states fluoxetine is effective in reducing binge-purge cycles.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts and the reference agree that fluoxetine reduces binge-purge frequency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states fluoxetine works through a different mechanism or cannot articulate its clinical benefit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains therapeutic rationale; supports why this drug is chosen.

items.title: Binge eating episodes noted
items.description: Response identifies frequent episodes of binge eating followed by self-induced vomiting as supporting the bulimia nervosa diagnosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure lists binge eating followed by self-induced vomiting as a behavioral symptom driving the diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not connect the binge-purge behavior to the diagnosis of bulimia nervosa.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Links chief clinical feature to the diagnosis; intermediate reasoning step.

items.title: Physical findings noted
items.description: Response links bilateral parotid gland enlargement, knuckle calluses, or eroded dental enamel to the bulimia nervosa diagnosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure lists these physical exam findings as supporting evidence for the diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ignores the physical exam stigmata and gives an unsupported diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds diagnostic depth from physical examination findings.

items.title: 60 mg/day dose
items.description: Response specifies the fluoxetine dose as 60 mg/day for bulimia nervosa.

provenance.evidence_detail: Two of three rollouts specified 60 mg/day; the reference is silent on dose but this is the clinically standard FDA-approved dose.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 20 mg/day, which is the depression dose and subtherapeutic for bulimia nervosa.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Concrete dosing detail beyond the asked quantity; real clinical specificity.

items.title: Russell's sign
items.description: Response identifies the knuckle calluses as Russell's sign, consistent with self-induced vomiting.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure notes knuckle calluses as Russell's sign, a classic physical exam finding in bulimia.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to recognize the clinical significance of knuckle calluses.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Recognises a classic eponymous finding; minor added depth.

items.title: Avoids BED misdiagnosis
items.description: Avoids diagnosing binge eating disorder or recommending lisdexamfetamine instead of fluoxetine.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: wrong eating disorder diagnosis — the compensatory behaviors (vomiting, exercise) distinguish bulimia from binge eating disorder, which lacks compensatory behavior.
provenance.discriminates: A response that conflates bulimia nervosa with binge eating disorder by overlooking the purging and exercise behaviors.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common confusion between bulimia and BED; pits observed in testing.

items.title: Avoids non-pharmacologic answer
items.description: Avoids diagnosing anorexia nervosa, recommending weight restoration alone, or answering cognitive behavioral therapy without naming a medication.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: wrong eating disorder diagnosis — diagnosing anorexia nervosa given the binge-purge behavior and compensatory exercise.
provenance.discriminates: A response that keys on 'daily exercise aimed at weight loss' and lands on anorexia nervosa or states no FDA-approved pharmacotherapy exists.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Question explicitly asks for pharmacotherapy; therapy-only or wrong-diagnosis answers fail.

items.title: Names rheumatic fever
items.description: The response identifies acute rheumatic fever as the most likely underlying cause of the 9-year-old boy's condition, rather than stopping at congestive heart failure or carditis alone.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Syndrome not etiology' warns that the heart-failure findings pull responses toward the hemodynamic syndrome rather than the etiologic mechanism the question demands.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 'congestive heart failure due to myocarditis' or 'carditis' as the final answer without naming the post-GAS immune-mediated illness.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core diagnosis; naming the upstream disease process is the central required answer.

items.title: Links to GAS pharyngitis
items.description: The response links the diagnosis to a preceding group A Streptococcus infection, consistent with the history of sore throat.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts correctly tied the sore throat history to antecedent GAS pharyngitis; the reference explicitly notes the boy's sore throat history aligns with strep throat.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names rheumatic fever but never connects it to the antecedent streptococcal sore throat, missing the etiologic trigger.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Etiologic link is fundamental to the correctness of the rheumatic fever diagnosis.

items.title: Identifies carditis
items.description: The response identifies rheumatic carditis as the complication causing cardiac findings such as the S3 heart sound, jugular venous distension, and enlarged cardiac silhouette on x-ray.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states rheumatic fever can lead to carditis, explaining the cardiac symptoms and enlarged cardiac silhouette.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names rheumatic fever but does not explain the cardiac involvement through carditis, leaving S3, JVD, and cardiomegaly unaccounted for.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Carditis is the key intermediate mechanism explaining the cardiac findings in this case.

items.title: Heart failure signs
items.description: The response explains that bilateral ankle edema and crackles at the lung bases indicate heart involvement secondary to rheumatic carditis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states the presence of bilateral ankle edema and crackles at the lung bases suggest heart involvement, supporting the diagnosis of carditis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not connect the pulmonary and peripheral edema findings to the rheumatic carditis mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects specific physical exam findings to the underlying cardiac pathology.

items.title: Names erythema marginatum
items.description: The response identifies the erythematous ring-shaped macules and patches on the trunk as erythema marginatum.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly names the rash as erythema marginatum and calls it a classic sign of rheumatic fever.
provenance.discriminates: A response that calls the rash 'erythema migrans' or leaves the ring-shaped truncal rash unexplained.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Naming this pathognomonic rash strengthens the rheumatic fever diagnosis.

items.title: Links rash to diagnosis
items.description: The response uses the presence of erythema marginatum as a classic sign supporting the diagnosis of rheumatic fever.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states the erythematous ring-shaped macules are classic signs of rheumatic fever and part of the constellation strongly indicating it.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions the rash but does not tie it to rheumatic fever as a diagnostic clue.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicitly tying the rash to the diagnosis demonstrates diagnostic reasoning.

items.title: Unifies all findings
items.description: The response explains how a single diagnosis of rheumatic fever accounts for the fever, malaise, sore throat history, S3 heart sound, jugular venous distension, bilateral ankle edema, crackles at the lung bases, and enlarged cardiac silhouette on x-ray.

provenance.evidence_detail: The implicit constraints require that a single unifying diagnosis explain the antecedent sore throat, rash, carditis/heart failure signs, and normal urinalysis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the correct diagnosis but leaves several presenting findings unconnected to it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Unifying the constellation of findings under one diagnosis is the core clinical reasoning task.

items.title: Immune-mediated mechanism
items.description: The response describes acute rheumatic fever as a delayed immune-mediated process following group A streptococcal pharyngitis rather than direct bacterial invasion of cardiac tissue.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts correctly identified the immune-mediated pathogenesis via molecular mimicry; the reference supports the immune-mediated post-infectious framing.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies ongoing direct streptococcal infection of the heart rather than a post-infectious immune process.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes post-infectious immune mechanism from active infection; addresses a common misconception.

items.title: Chronic sequela
items.description: The response mentions rheumatic heart disease as the chronic sequela leading from rheumatic fever.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference closes by stating the constellation strongly indicates rheumatic fever as the underlying problem, leading to rheumatic heart disease.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits the chronic-disease label entirely, missing the reference's final linkage.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds depth by naming the long-term consequence; not required for the core diagnosis.

items.title: Avoids PSGN
items.description: The response avoids selecting post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis as the underlying cause, respecting the normal urinalysis that excludes renal pathology.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'PSGN despite normal UA' warns that PSGN is a tempting post-strep differential but cannot explain the rash or carditis and is excluded by the normal urinalysis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is the unifying diagnosis despite the explicitly normal urinalysis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: PSGN is a tempting distractor given the strep throat history; normal urinalysis excludes it.

items.title: Avoids Lyme confusion
items.description: The response avoids interpreting the ring-shaped trunk macules as erythema migrans or attributing the condition to Lyme disease and Borrelia burgdorferi.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Erythema migrans confusion' warns that the ring-shaped rash is easily cross-mapped to Lyme disease despite the absence of tick-bite history.
provenance.discriminates: A response that diagnoses Lyme disease with carditis based on the ring-shaped truncal rash.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Ring-shaped rash is a high-risk confusion point; erythema marginatum vs migrans is a specific trap.

items.title: Avoids viral myocarditis
items.description: The response avoids naming viral myocarditis as the underlying cause, which cannot account for the sore throat history or erythema marginatum.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Viral myocarditis shortcut' warns that viral myocarditis is a bread-and-butter pediatric heart-failure cause that surfaces before the less common rheumatic etiology.
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers 'viral myocarditis' while ignoring the post-streptococcal pattern and ring-shaped truncal rash.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Viral myocarditis is a plausible distractor for carditis but fails to explain the full constellation.

items.title: Final answer and option
items.description: States that the corrected exposure rate X_dot_C equals 121.8 mR/hr and selects option d as the correct answer for the calibrated detector.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks to compute the corrected exposure rate reading; the reference and all three rollouts agree on 121.8 mR/hr.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes a wrong numeric result (e.g., 73.8 from inverted pressure ratio, 135.5 from inverted temperature ratio, or 71.4 from using Celsius values).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core deliverable; without the correct value and option the answer fails.

items.title: Correction formula
items.description: States the correction formula X_dot_C = X_dot(P/P_C)(T_C/T) for the exposure rate read in a 100-mR/hr field.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference explicitly state this formula; it is the load-bearing equation for the entire derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses an inverted or rearranged formula (e.g., X_dot_C = X_dot(P_C/P)(T/T_C)) would produce wrong ratios.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Master equation; all computation derives from it.

items.title: Pressure ratio orientation
items.description: Computes the pressure ratio as 760 torr divided by 591.6 torr with 760 torr in the numerator.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts place 760 over 591.6; the mined pitfall 'Pressure ratio inverted' identifies 591.6/760 as a high-severity error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inverts the pressure ratio (591.6/760) would get approximately 73.8 mR/hr instead of 121.8.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Critical intermediate; inverted ratio yields wrong answer.

items.title: Temperature ratio orientation
items.description: Computes the temperature ratio as 293 K divided by 309 K with 293 K in the numerator.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts place 293 over 309; the mined pitfall 'Temperature ratio inverted' identifies 309/293 as a high-severity error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inverts the temperature ratio (309/293) would get approximately 135.5 mR/hr instead of 121.8.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Critical intermediate; inverted ratio yields wrong answer.

items.title: Full numerical substitution
items.description: Shows the full numerical substitution (100 mR/hr)(760/591.6)(293/309) yielding the corrected exposure rate to be read.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference use X_dot = 100 mR/hr as the starting value in the formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses a different base value or omits it from the computation would get a different result.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Confirms correct values and arrangement are applied together.

items.title: Detector equation and derivation
items.description: States the detector equation I = K multiplied by X_dot multiplied by (P/T) and derives the correction because I = I_C when the detector response is matched.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference derive the correction from I = K·X_dot·(P/T), which is the starting equation of the scenario.
provenance.discriminates: A response that starts from a different relation (e.g., I = K·X_dot·(T/P)) would derive the wrong correction formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Provides theoretical basis; equating currents motivates the formula.

items.title: Temperature conversions
items.description: Converts the calibrated temperature as (273 + 20) = 293 K and the measurement temperature as (273 + 36) = 309 K.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference and all rollouts perform this conversion explicitly; the mined pitfall 'Celsius used instead of Kelvin' identifies using 20 directly as a high-severity error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 20 instead of 293 would compute a wrong temperature ratio (~71.4 mR/hr).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required inputs; wrong conversions propagate to wrong result.

items.title: Calibration pressure identified
items.description: Identifies 591.6 torr as the calibration pressure P_C, distinct from the measurement pressure of 760 torr.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'STP assumed for calibration' identifies substituting 760 torr for P_C as a medium-severity error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assumes calibration at STP (760 torr) would compute approximately 88.3 mR/hr instead of 121.8.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Prevents swapping calibration and measurement pressures in the ratio.

items.title: Context and constant K
items.description: States that K is a constant for a given detector and identifies that measurements were made at sea level with P = 760 torr and T = 309 K.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference explicitly note that K is constant for a given detector, justifying its cancellation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats K as variable between calibration and measurement would not be able to justify the correction formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Supplementary context; adds depth but not required for correctness.

items.title: Inhibition of apoptosis
items.description: States that the cellular change most likely observed as a result of this genetic alteration is inhibition of apoptosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (a) asks for the downstream cellular change caused by t(14;18); the reference answer names inhibition of apoptosis as the cellular change.
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers with BCL2 overexpression or follicular lymphoma but never states inhibition of apoptosis as the cellular change.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct answer to the question; without it correctness collapses entirely.

items.title: BCL2 overexpression
items.description: Identifies overexpression of the BCL2 gene as the molecular result of the translocation between chromosomes 14 and 18.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference agree that t(14;18) causes BCL2 overexpression.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions apoptosis inhibition but does not identify BCL2 overexpression as the causal molecular event.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core mechanistic link connecting the translocation to the observed cellular change.

items.title: Follicular lymphoma
items.description: Associates the translocation between chromosomes 14 and 18 with follicular lymphoma.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference identify t(14;18) as the hallmark of follicular lymphoma.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses BCL2 and apoptosis but does not name follicular lymphoma as the associated diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key diagnostic context that anchors the molecular mechanism to the clinical presentation.

items.title: BCL2 regulates apoptosis
items.description: States that BCL2 plays a role in regulating apoptosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly states BCL2 plays a crucial role in regulating apoptosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names BCL2 overexpression and inhibition of apoptosis but does not connect BCL2 to apoptosis regulation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate explaining why BCL2 overexpression produces the observed cellular change.

items.title: Overexpression prevents death
items.description: States that BCL2 overexpression leads to prevention of programmed cell death, so lymphocytes do not undergo cell death as they normally would.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states that lymphocytes 'do not undergo cell death as they normally would.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions apoptosis inhibition but does not frame it as a failure of the normal cell death process.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects the molecular result to the functional consequence in lymphocytes.

items.title: BCL2 on chromosome 18
items.description: Identifies BCL2 as the gene located on chromosome 18 involved in the translocation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agree that BCL2 is the gene on chromosome 18 involved in the translocation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses the translocation but does not specify that BCL2 resides on chromosome 18.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specifies which chromosome contributes BCL2, a required intermediate detail.

items.title: IgH enhancer locus
items.description: States that chromosome 14 provides the IgH enhancer locus in this translocation.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agree that chromosome 14 carries the IgH locus/enhancer in this translocation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the translocation partners but does not identify chromosome 14 as carrying the IgH enhancer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specifies the partner locus on chromosome 14 that drives overexpression.

items.title: Juxtaposition drives overexpression
items.description: States that juxtaposition of BCL2 with the IgH enhancer leads to overexpression of BCL2.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agree BCL2 overexpression results from juxtaposition with the IgH enhancer.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states BCL2 is overexpressed but does not explain the enhancer juxtaposition mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the mechanistic basis for how the translocation causes BCL2 overexpression.

items.title: Accumulation and enlargement
items.description: States that lymphocytes accumulate due to failure to undergo cell death, contributing to the painless enlargement of lymph nodes.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly ties inhibited apoptosis to the painless enlargement of lymph nodes observed in the patient; rollouts did not make this clinical linkage.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains BCL2 and apoptosis but does not connect the mechanism to the patient's painless lymph node enlargement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Links the cellular change back to the clinical presentation; real but secondary depth.

items.title: Programmed cell death term
items.description: Uses the term programmed cell death to describe apoptosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer uses 'programmed cell death' as a synonym for apoptosis to clarify the mechanism.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions apoptosis but从不 uses the descriptive phrase programmed cell death.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Minor terminological clarity; adds little beyond the apoptosis criterion above.

items.title: Avoids proliferation claim
items.description: Avoids claiming the cellular change is increased proliferation or uncontrolled cell division.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Proliferation not survival' (high severity): responses may wrongly attribute the effect to increased mitotic rate rather than decreased cell death.
provenance.discriminates: A response that correctly identifies BCL2 but states the cellular change is increased proliferation instead of inhibited apoptosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common trap substituting proliferation for apoptosis inhibition; directly tests the key distinction.

items.title: Avoids reversed BCL2 effect
items.description: Avoids stating that BCL2 overexpression promotes or stimulates apoptosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Reversed apoptosis direction' (high severity): responses may invert BCL2 from anti-apoptotic to pro-apoptotic.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names BCL2 and apoptosis but claims BCL2 overexpression promotes apoptosis rather than inhibiting it.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Reversing BCL2 function is a specific mechanistic error observed in flawed responses.

items.title: Avoids wrong attribution
items.description: Avoids attributing the translocation to MYC or cyclin D1 overexpression, or stating the cellular change is follicular lymphoma without describing the mechanism.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Names disease not mechanism' (high severity): responses may answer with the diagnosis instead of the downstream cellular change.
provenance.discriminates: A response that answers 'follicular lymphoma' as the cellular change rather than inhibition of apoptosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Names the specific wrong genes and disease-as-answer trap observed in flawed responses.

items.title: IgA vasculitis diagnosis
items.description: States the diagnosis as IgA vasculitis or Henoch-Schönlein purpura (HSP) based on the clinical picture of non-blanching rashes, knee joint swelling, hematuria, and proteinuria.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks to identify the specific biopsy finding, which requires recognizing the underlying diagnosis from the clinical tetrad.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that fail to identify the clinical picture as IgA vasculitis and instead name a different disease.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core diagnosis driving the entire answer; without it the biopsy finding is unexplained.

items.title: Clinical picture linkage
items.description: Connects the clinical picture of non-blanching rashes over the shin, knee joint swelling, and hematuria with proteinuria to the diagnosis of IgA vasculitis.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly links the constellation of non-blanching rashes, joint swelling, and hematuria with proteinuria to HSP.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that state the correct finding without connecting it to the clinical presentation, indicating pattern-matching rather than reasoning.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Reasoning bridge from presentation to diagnosis; key intermediate step for correctness.

items.title: Mesangial IgA deposition
items.description: States mesangial deposition of IgA as the specific finding observed on microscopic analysis of the renal biopsy specimen.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong immunoglobulin' identifies that responses may default to IgG instead of IgA.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that name IgG, IgM, or C3 as the primary deposited immunoglobulin.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Direct answer to the question; the single most important fact with highest discriminative value.

items.title: Immunofluorescence modality
items.description: Mentions immunofluorescence as the method demonstrating mesangial IgA deposition on the renal biopsy specimen.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus among all rollouts specified immunofluorescence as the modality, though the reference uses the broader term 'microscopic analysis.'
provenance.discriminates: Responses that attribute IgA deposition to light microscopy alone rather than specifying immunofluorescence.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds technical depth on how the deposition is visualized; not required for the core answer.

items.title: EM electron-dense deposits
items.description: States that electron microscopy of the renal biopsy shows mesangial electron-dense deposits consistent with IgA vasculitis.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts included electron microscopy findings as consensus correct content, though the reference does not mention EM.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that describe only immunofluorescence findings without acknowledging the corresponding EM correlate.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Supplementary ultrastructural detail; reinforces correctness but not the Question's focus.

items.title: Palpable purpura recognition
items.description: Recognizes the non-blanching rashes over the shin as palpable purpura characteristic of HSP.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference interprets non-blanching rashes as part of the HSP clinical picture, specifically noting the palpable purpura component.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that treat the rash as nonspecific rather than identifying it as the palpable purpura of IgA vasculitis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Nice clinical clue but peripheral to the renal biopsy finding being asked.

items.title: Renal involvement recognition
items.description: Recognizes hematuria with proteinuria as renal involvement in IgA vasculitis prompting the renal biopsy.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly notes hematuria with proteinuria as part of the clinical picture suggestive of HSP with renal involvement.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that do not connect the hematuria and proteinuria to renal involvement in HSP.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains why biopsy is performed; relevant context but not the finding itself.

items.title: Avoids non-IgA biopsy emphasis
items.description: Avoids presenting mesangial hypercellularity, focal proliferative glomerulonephritis, or co-deposits such as IgG, IgM, or C3 as the defining finding rather than mesangial IgA deposition itself.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Light microscopy only' (severity high): responses may give the nonspecific light microscopy finding instead of the diagnostic immunofluorescence finding.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that answer 'mesangial hypercellularity' or 'focal proliferative glomerulonephritis' as the specific finding rather than mesangial IgA deposition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common trap of overemphasizing light microscopy or co-deposits; directly observed pitfall.

items.title: Avoids wrong-disease biopsy findings
items.description: Avoids answering leukocytoclastic vasculitis, subepithelial electron-dense humps of PSGN, or pauci-immune glomerulonephritis as the specific finding on the renal biopsy specimen.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Skin biopsy finding' (severity high): responses may confuse the skin biopsy finding with the renal biopsy finding given the prominence of the rash.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that answer 'leukocytoclastic vasculitis' or 'neutrophilic infiltrate with fibrinoid necrosis' instead of mesangial IgA deposition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Confuses renal biopsy with skin biopsy or a different glomerulonephritis; observed trap.
