items.title: Hyper-IgM diagnosis
items.description: Identifies the condition as hyper-IgM syndrome based on decreased CD40L cells.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks for the immunoglobulin profile expected with decreased CD40L, which is hyper-IgM syndrome per the reference answer.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to name hyper-IgM syndrome or misidentifies the condition.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core diagnosis; without it the entire immunoglobulin profile is unexplained.

items.title: IgM elevated or normal
items.description: States that IgM levels are elevated or normal in this patient.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states elevated or normal levels of IgM as a key part of the profile.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IgM as decreased, as in pan-hypogammaglobulinemia or Bruton's.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Defining lab finding of hyper-IgM; directly answers the immunoglobulin profile asked.

items.title: IgG low
items.description: States that IgG levels are low in this patient.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer lists low levels of IgG as part of the expected profile.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IgG as normal or elevated.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Defining lab finding; failure of class-switch recombination produces low IgG.
provenance.merged_mirror_text: States that IgA levels are low in this patient.

items.title: X-linked form
items.description: Identifies the X-linked form of hyper-IgM syndrome as associated with CD40L deficiency.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus across all rollouts and the reference answer that the X-linked form is due to CD40L defect.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes the CD40L deficiency to an autosomal inheritance pattern.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key distinction; CD40L mutation specifically causes the X-linked form.

items.title: Class-switch recombination impaired
items.description: States that the CD40L defect causes impaired class-switch recombination in B-cells due to disrupted communication between T-cells and B-cells.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus across rollouts and the reference answer that the inability to switch from IgM underlies the profile.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not explain why IgM remains elevated while other classes are low.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Central mechanism linking the CD40L deficiency to the observed immunoglobulin profile.

items.title: CD40L on T-cells
items.description: States that CD40L is expressed on activated T-cells.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Reversed CD40/CD40L cell' identifies the common error of misattributing the defect to B-cell CD40 rather than T-cell CD40L.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states or implies the defect is in B-cell CD40 rather than T-cell CD40L.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds mechanistic depth about where CD40L is located in the immune interaction.

items.title: CD40L-CD40 receptor pair
items.description: States that CD40L on T-cells interacts with CD40 on B-cells to signal class-switch recombination.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Reversed CD40/CD40L cell' notes that CD40 and CD40L are a receptor-ligand pair whose names are easily swapped.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes the signaling pair incorrectly or omits the receptor-ligand relationship.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specifies the receptor-ligand pair mediating the T-cell to B-cell signaling defect.

items.title: B-cell count normal
items.description: States that the number of B-cells is normal in this hyper-IgM syndrome profile.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Confusing with Bruton's' notes that B-cell count is normal in CD40L deficiency, unlike Bruton's where B-cells are absent.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports B-cells as absent or low, confusing CD40L deficiency with Bruton's agammaglobulinemia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes hyper-IgM from B-cell aplasia; B-cells are present but non-functional.

items.title: B-cell machinery intact
items.description: States that the class-switch recombination machinery within B-cells is intrinsically intact but unstimulated due to CD40L deficiency.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Reversed CD40/CD40L cell' specifies that the B-cell machinery for class switching is intrinsically intact but unstimulated.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes the B-cell machinery as intrinsically defective.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Clarifies that the defect is extrinsic to B-cells, located in T-cell signaling.

items.title: Somatic hypermutation impaired
items.description: States that somatic hypermutation is also impaired due to lack of CD40-CD40L signaling, compounding the class-switch recombination defect.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure's implicit constraints note that somatic hypermutation is impaired due to lack of CD40-CD40L signaling.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only mentions class-switch recombination and omits somatic hypermutation impairment.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added depth; CD40-CD40L signaling also drives somatic hypermutation.

items.title: T-cell-independent intact
items.description: States that responses of B-cells that are independent of T-cells remain intact despite the CD40L deficiency.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question structure's implicit constraints note that T-cell-independent responses remain intact while T-cell-dependent responses are defective.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies all B-cell function is globally impaired.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Useful nuance; T-cell-independent B-cell responses do not require CD40L signaling.

items.title: Elevated IgM reflects intact production
items.description: States that elevated or normal IgM reflects intact IgM production while class-switch recombination to other immunoglobulin classes fails.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus across rollouts that IgM production is intact while class switching fails, explaining why IgM remains normal or elevated.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports elevated IgM without explaining the mechanistic basis of intact IgM production alongside failed class switching.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the mechanistic basis for the paradoxically high IgM alongside low IgG and IgA.

items.title: Avoids physiologic nadir
items.description: Avoids attributing the low IgG solely to the 3-month-old physiologic nadir of maternal IgG, instead linking it to failed class-switch recombination.

provenance.evidence_detail: The mined pitfall 'Physiologic nadir confound' identifies the error of dismissing low IgG as transient hypogammaglobulinemia of infancy rather than a pathological class-switch defect.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports IgG as 'normal for age' or dismisses it as physiologic nadir without recognizing the class-switch defect.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific trap for this age; 3-month-olds normally have low maternal IgG but here the cause is pathological.

items.title: Names latex agglutination test
items.description: The response names the Latex Agglutination Test as the test commonly utilized for the rapid detection of microbial antigens.

provenance.evidence_detail: The sole sub-question asks for the name of the diagnostic test; the reference answer is the Latex Agglutination Test.
provenance.discriminates: Any response that names a different test or fails to name one at all.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; all flawed responses naming a wrong test fail here.

items.title: Sensitized inert particles
items.description: The response states that the latex agglutination test uses sensitized inert particles.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question's given mechanism is 'sensitized inert particles,' which the reference answer echoes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names latex agglutination but does not connect it to the sensitized inert particles descriptor from the question.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key distinguishing feature from biological-particle methods; high discriminative value.

items.title: Five minutes or less
items.description: The response states that the latex agglutination test provides results in five minutes or less, characterizing it as a rapid test.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question's given turnaround time is 'five minutes or less,' a defining characteristic the reference includes.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the correct test but omits or contradicts the ≤5-minute turnaround requirement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explicit time constraint from the question; distinguishes from slower methods like ELISA.

items.title: Microbial antigen target
items.description: The response specifies that the latex agglutination test is used for the detection of microbial antigens.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question's detection_target is 'microbial antigens,' which the reference answer restates.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names latex agglutination but for a non-microbial application such as rheumatoid factor.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Defines the correct application scope; catches responses misattributing the test's purpose.

items.title: Antibody-coated latex particles
items.description: The response describes latex particles coated with antibodies as the mechanism of the test.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer specifies 'latex particles coated with antibodies' as a key mechanistic detail.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the correct test but gives a vague or incorrect mechanistic description.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains how sensitized particles work; distinguishes from passive agglutination methods.

items.title: Agglutination or clumping
items.description: The response states that latex particles agglutinate or clump together when specific antigens are present in the sample.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer states that particles 'agglutinate, or clump together, when specific antigens are present.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the test but does not describe the visible agglutination endpoint.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Describes the observable readout mechanism; central to explaining the test's principle.

items.title: Diagnostic tool for infections
items.description: The response characterizes the latex agglutination test as a diagnostic tool for identifying various infections.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer frames the test as 'a quick and straightforward diagnostic tool for identifying various infections.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the test but frames it only as a lab technique without connecting it to infection diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added context from reference; nice-to-have clinical framing but not essential to the answer.

items.title: Avoids wrong test names
items.description: Avoids naming coagglutination, hemagglutination, immunochromatography, ELISA, or precipitation reaction as the test, since these do not use sensitized inert particles providing results in five minutes or less.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined high-severity pitfall: coagglutination confused for latex agglutination because both produce visible agglutination rapidly.
provenance.discriminates: A response that substitutes coagglutination for latex agglutination, overlooking the 'inert particles' criterion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common confusions from mined pitfalls; rewards selecting the correct test specifically.

items.title: Avoids wrong application
items.description: Avoids attributing the latex agglutination test solely to rheumatoid factor or pregnancy testing instead of microbial antigen detection.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined low-severity pitfall: wrong test application named, such as rheumatoid factor, because that is a common teaching context.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names latex agglutination but associates it only with rheumatoid factor rather than microbial antigens.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Targets responses that name the right test but misattribute its primary diagnostic use.

items.title: CRS diagnosis stated
items.description: The response states that the most likely diagnosis for the neonate is Congenital Rubella Syndrome (CRS).

provenance.evidence_detail: The single required deliverable is naming the diagnosis; the reference answer and all rollouts agree on CRS.
provenance.discriminates: Any response naming CMV, toxoplasmosis, syphilis, or a generic TORCH differential instead of CRS.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; without CRS diagnosis the response fails entirely.

items.title: Classic triad of CRS
items.description: The response identifies cataracts, patent ductus arteriosus (PDA), and CNS or auditory involvement as the classic indicators of CRS.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'PDA + cataracts overlooked' — the combination is highly specific for rubella but may be undervalued when many nonspecific findings are present.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists CRS but treats cataracts and PDA as generic findings without recognizing their specific rubella association.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key reasoning linking specific findings to CRS; discriminates from generic TORCH answers.

items.title: Maternal rash as rubella
items.description: The response identifies the mother's mild maculopapular rash during mid-pregnancy as the rubella exanthem in an unimmunized teenager.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing maternal rash clue' — failing to integrate the maternal maculopapular rash as the rubella exanthem.
provenance.discriminates: A response that arrives at CRS purely from neonatal findings without ever connecting the maternal rash to rubella.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects maternal history to diagnosis; critical intermediate reasoning step.

items.title: First trimester teratogenic risk
items.description: The response states that rubella infections in pregnancy, particularly during the first trimester, can lead to significant congenital defects.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference_only finding: the reference specifically notes first trimester as the highest-risk period, which all rollouts omitted.
provenance.discriminates: A response that discusses CRS risk without specifying the first trimester as the period of greatest teratogenic risk.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains pathogenesis timing; adds depth to diagnostic reasoning.

items.title: Transplacental transmission
items.description: The response states that maternal rubella infection transmits transplacentally to the fetus.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus item: all correct rollouts noted transplacental transmission as the mechanism connecting maternal rash to neonatal CRS.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names CRS but does not explain how maternal infection reaches the fetus.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Mechanistic detail supporting CRS; moderate importance to answer.

items.title: Purpura consistent with CRS
items.description: The response recognizes that thrombocytopenia with purpura is consistent with CRS rather than exclusively diagnostic of CMV.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Blueberry muffin = CMV only' — the blueberry muffin rash occurs in CRS as well as CMV and is not discriminating between them.
provenance.discriminates: A response that either excludes CRS because purpura is present or incorrectly selects CMV based on purpura alone.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Prevents CMV misattribution; real added depth in differential reasoning.

items.title: Meningoencephalitis in CRS
items.description: The response recognizes meningoencephalitis as CNS involvement consistent with CRS without requiring sensorineural hearing loss to be present.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Seeking hearing loss specifically' — the textbook triad includes SNHL, but meningoencephalitis represents CNS involvement and SNHL may not be detectable at birth.
provenance.discriminates: A response that hesitates to commit to CRS or selects another diagnosis because sensorineural hearing loss is not mentioned.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Prevents exclusion of CRS when SNHL is absent; adds diagnostic specificity.

items.title: Bone lucency as CRS feature
items.description: The response identifies bone lucency as a finding consistent with CRS rather than attributing it to syphilis or another condition.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus item: correct rollouts listed bone lucency among the clinical features supporting CRS; radiolucency of long bones is a recognized rubella manifestation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes bone lucency to syphilis or another diagnosis instead of CRS.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes radiographic finding from syphilis; specific clinical depth.

items.title: Teenager immunization gap
items.description: The response notes that the teenager mother without prenatal care likely lacked rubella immunization verification, increasing susceptibility to rubella infection.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Missing maternal rash clue' context — the maternal demographic of a teenager without prenatal care implies no immunization surveillance, supporting susceptibility to rubella.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ignores the maternal demographic context that makes rubella susceptibility plausible.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Links maternal risk factors to susceptibility; contextual depth.

items.title: SGA and hepatosplenomegaly in CRS
items.description: The response identifies the neonate being small for gestational age and having hepatosplenomegaly as findings consistent with CRS.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus item: correct rollouts listed SGA among the clinical features supporting CRS as intrauterine growth restriction.
provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to acknowledge SGA as part of the CRS clinical picture.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Supportive but non-discriminative findings; low incremental value.

items.title: Avoids alternative TORCH misdiagnosis
items.description: Avoids diagnosing congenital CMV, toxoplasmosis, or syphilis as the most likely diagnosis instead of CRS, despite overlapping features such as hepatosplenomegaly, meningoencephalitis, and bone findings.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Confusing with CMV' — CMV shares SGA, hepatosplenomegaly, and purpura but does not classically cause cataracts, PDA, or bone lucency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects CMV based on overlapping findings while ignoring the specific cataract-PDA-bone lucency combination.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Major observed trap; multiple flawed responses chose these alternatives.

items.title: Avoids timing exclusion
items.description: Avoids rejecting CRS solely because the maternal maculopapular rash occurred in mid-pregnancy rather than the first trimester.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Timing excludes rubella' — first trimester carries highest risk, but infection later in pregnancy can still transmit and cause congenital defects.
provenance.discriminates: A response that dismisses CRS because the rash was in mid-pregnancy and selects another diagnosis on that basis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific trap where mid-pregnancy timing could wrongly exclude CRS.

items.title: Avoids broad TORCH hedge
items.description: Avoids presenting a broad TORCH differential without committing to CRS as the most likely diagnosis for this neonate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'PDA + cataracts overlooked' — the temptation to evaluate each finding in isolation and offer a generic TORCH list rather than the specific diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists multiple TORCH infections as possibilities without selecting CRS as the single most likely diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Observed flaw where responses listed TORCH infections without concluding CRS.

items.title: VP two components
items.description: The ventral posterior nucleus of the thalamus is stated to be primarily composed of two components, the ventral posterolateral nucleus (VPL) and the ventral posteromedial nucleus (VPM).

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks to identify the components; the reference answer names VPL and VPM as the two principal components.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists only one component, lists three or more, or names incorrect nuclei.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer to the question; all correct responses must name both VPL and VPM.

items.title: VPL processes body
items.description: States that the VPL processes sensory information from the body, including the arms, legs, and torso, rather than attributing body input to the VPM.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'VPL/VPM function swap' pitfall (severity high) foresees assigning body somatosensory input to VPM.
provenance.discriminates: A response that transposes VPL and VPM, assigning body sensation to VPM.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key functional distinction; absorbs the VPM-body swap pitfall into the positive claim.

items.title: VPM handles face
items.description: States that the VPM handles sensory data from the face, rather than attributing face input to the VPL.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'VPL/VPM function swap' pitfall (severity high) foresees assigning face/trigeminal input to VPL.
provenance.discriminates: A response that transposes VPL and VPM, assigning face sensation to VPL.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key functional distinction; absorbs the VPL-face swap pitfall into the positive claim.

items.title: VPM handles head
items.description: States that the VPM handles sensory data from the head.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly includes head alongside face as VPM's sensory domain, which attempts omitted.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions only face and omits head as a region handled by VPM.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Complementary to face input; verifies the full VPM sensory domain.

items.title: VP relay role
items.description: States that the ventral posterior nucleus plays a role in relaying sensory information.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer describes the VP nucleus and its components as playing a crucial role in relaying sensory information.
provenance.discriminates: A response that lists components but does not describe their functional role in sensory relay.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Defines the functional purpose of the VP nucleus itself.

items.title: Relay to cortex
items.description: States that both the VPL and VPM relay sensory information to the primary somatosensory cortex.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Missing cortical target' pitfall identifies that respondents may list only subnuclei and omit the cortical relay destination.
provenance.discriminates: A response that identifies VPL and VPM but never mentions the primary somatosensory cortex as their projection target.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific cortical target is a key anatomical fact; discriminates from vague relay claims.

items.title: Further processing
items.description: States that sensory information relayed to the primary somatosensory cortex is further processed in the brain.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer concludes that these nuclei relay sensory information to the cortex where it is further processed.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the cortex but does not indicate that processing continues there.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Minor contextual detail from the reference answer; adds little discriminative value.

items.title: Avoids including VPI
items.description: Avoids listing the ventral posterior inferior nucleus (VPI) as a core component of the ventral posterior nucleus.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts included VPI as a component, but the reference defines the VP nucleus as primarily composed of two components (VPL and VPM) with no mention of VPI.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents three components (VPL, VPM, VPI) instead of the two principal ones.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common error surfaced from collective mistakes; VPI is not a standard core component here.

items.title: Avoids VL/VA confusion
items.description: Avoids confusing the ventral posterior (VP) nucleus with the ventral lateral (VL) or ventral anterior (VA) nucleus by listing motor relay nuclei instead of somatosensory components.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Wrong thalamic nucleus' pitfall (severity high) foresees cross-contamination with VL or VA nuclei.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names VL or VA components or describes motor relay to motor cortex instead of somatosensory relay.
provenance.calibration_rationale: High-likelihood confusion between adjacent thalamic groups; naming motor nuclei is a substantive error.

items.title: Avoids tract mispairing
items.description: Avoids pairing the spinothalamic tract or medial lemniscus with the VPM for face sensory input, or the trigeminothalamic tract with the VPL for body input.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Spinothalamic vs trigeminal mismatch' pitfall (severity medium) foresees crossing the pathway-nucleus pairings.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states face input reaches VPM via spinothalamic tract or body input reaches VPL via trigeminal tract.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific tract-nucleus mispairing is a known pitfall; corrects a common crossed association.

items.title: VPL medial lemniscus
items.description: States that the VPL receives body sensory input via the medial lemniscus and/or spinothalamic tract.

provenance.evidence_detail: Attempts agreed that VPL receives body input via medial lemniscus and spinothalamic tract; the reference does not name specific tracts.
provenance.discriminates: A response that either omits afferent pathways or assigns the wrong tract to VPL.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added anatomical depth beyond the reference answer; verifiable and correct.

items.title: VPM trigeminothalamic
items.description: States that the VPM receives face sensory input via the trigeminal or trigeminothalamic tract.

provenance.evidence_detail: Attempts agreed that VPM receives face input via the trigeminothalamic tract; the reference does not name specific tracts.
provenance.discriminates: A response that either omits afferent pathways or assigns the wrong tract to VPM.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Added anatomical depth beyond the reference answer; verifiable and correct.

items.title: VPM taste input
items.description: States that the VPM receives gustatory or taste fibers from the solitary nucleus.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 3 specified taste fibers from the solitary nucleus via central tegmental tract; rollouts 1 and 2 mentioned taste without naming the tract; the reference is silent on taste.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns taste to VPL or does not mention the taste pathway at all.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Additional VPM input source; correct but tangential to the core question.

items.title: VPM gustatory relay
items.description: States that the VPM relays gustatory information to the primary somatosensory cortex.

provenance.evidence_detail: The consensus identified that VPM relays both face sensory input and taste; connecting taste to the cortical relay target adds functional depth beyond the reference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions taste input to VPM but does not connect it to cortical relay, or that omits the taste modality entirely.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Extension of VPM function; correct but not required for the core answer.

items.title: Selects option B
items.description: The response identifies B. Varicella zoster infection as the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks to select one of four options; the reference answer is B.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects A, C, or D instead of B.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Selecting the correct option is indispensable; without it the answer is wrong regardless of reasoning.

items.title: Post-infectious cerebellar ataxia
items.description: The response states that the patient's symptoms represent post-infectious cerebellar ataxia following varicella infection.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts agreed on this mechanism; the reference answer explicitly names post-infectious cerebellar ataxia after chickenpox.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects B but attributes it to direct viral CNS invasion rather than a post-infectious immune mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Names the specific mechanism linking varicella to ataxia; central to explaining the diagnosis.

items.title: Localizes to cerebellum
items.description: The response attributes the broad-based staggering gait, difficulty touching the nose (dysmetria), and inability to perform rapidly-alternating palm movements (dysdiadochokinesia) to cerebellar dysfunction.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed on cerebellar localization based on dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, and broad-based gait.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attributes these findings to a peripheral nerve or cortical process.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Cerebellar localization is the key intermediate step; distinguishes central ataxia from peripheral weakness.

items.title: Acute onset favors post-infectious
items.description: The response uses the 2-day symptom duration in a previously healthy 5-year-old child to favor an acute post-infectious process over chronic causes such as nutritional deficiency or neoplasm.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts emphasized previously healthy status combined with acute onset as favoring post-infectious cerebellitis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ignores the previously healthy baseline when justifying a chronic or progressive diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Timeline is the primary discriminator among the differential; directly narrows the diagnosis.

items.title: Unvaccinated status as clue
items.description: The response connects the patient's lack of routine childhood vaccinations to increased susceptibility to varicella infection and its post-infectious complications.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Unvaccinated underweighted' warns against treating the vaccination history as background noise.
provenance.discriminates: A response that mentions unvaccinated status but does not link it to varicella risk.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Unvaccinated status is a deliberate case clue pointing toward VZV; important supporting evidence.

items.title: Excludes B1 deficiency
items.description: The response explains that Vitamin B1 deficiency is unlikely because the patient lacks encephalopathy or ophthalmoplegia, and notes that the vegetarian diet is a distractor rather than evidence of thiamine deficiency.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Vegetarian diet → B1' warns against selecting A based on dietary distractor.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects A because of the vegetarian diet without recognizing thiamine deficiency requires chronic malnutrition and Wernicke features.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Vegetarian diet is the main distractor; excluding B1 with specific findings prevents the common wrong answer.

items.title: Excludes posterior fossa malignancy
items.description: The response excludes posterior fossa malignancy based on the acute 2-day onset and the absence of headache, vomiting, or papilledema suggesting increased intracranial pressure.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed that no signs of increased ICP and acute onset exclude a posterior fossa mass.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects C based on hyperpigmented macules or without addressing the acute timeline.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Posterior fossa malignancy is a plausible alternative; acute onset and absence of ICP signs distinguish it.

items.title: Excludes peripheral nerve demyelination
items.description: The response excludes peripheral nerve demyelination because strength is 5/5 in the upper and lower extremities and deep tendon reflexes, though 1+ bilaterally, are present rather than absent.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed that intact strength and present reflexes exclude peripheral neuropathy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects D despite 5/5 strength and present reflexes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: 1+ reflexes are a designed trap; citing intact strength and present reflexes blocks the GBS misdiagnosis.

items.title: Macules not café-au-lait
items.description: Avoids interpreting the faint hyperpigmented macules on the chest as café-au-lait spots of NF1 to justify posterior fossa malignancy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Macules → NF1 → tumor' warns against misidentifying skin lesions to select option C.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects C by conflating hyperpigmented macules with café-au-lait spots and NF1-associated CNS tumors.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Faint macules are a deliberate NF1 distractor; avoiding this misread prevents selecting option C.

items.title: No rash does not exclude VZV
items.description: Avoids discarding varicella zoster infection as the cause solely because no preceding chickenpox rash is documented in the history.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'No rash → exclude VZV' warns against eliminating B for lack of rash history.
provenance.discriminates: A response that eliminates B because no rash is described, leading to A, C, or D.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Absence of documented rash is expected; discarding VZV for this reason would eliminate the correct answer.

items.title: Subclinical varicella possible
items.description: The response states that the preceding varicella infection may have been subclinical or unrecognized by the family.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer notes the varicella infection may not have been recognized by the family as chickenpox; no rollout mentioned this.
provenance.discriminates: A response that requires a documented chickenpox rash before considering varicella as the cause.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains why no rash history is present; adds depth to the VZV explanation without being essential.

items.title: Alert mental status excludes Wernicke
items.description: The response notes that the patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time, which argues against Wernicke encephalopathy from Vitamin B1 deficiency.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts noted absence of encephalopathy or ophthalmoplegia as exclusion criteria for thiamine deficiency.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects A without recognizing that altered mental status is expected in Wernicke encephalopathy.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Mental status is a specific differentiator for Wernicke; supports excluding B1 deficiency.

items.title: Acute onset not chronic
items.description: Avoids applying chronic disease timelines such as nutritional deficiency or neoplasm to the 2-day symptom duration without recognizing that acute cerebellar ataxia in a child is most often post-infectious.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Acute onset ignored' identifies this as a high-severity trap.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects B1 deficiency or posterior fossa malignancy despite the 2-day acute timeline.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Reinforces that 2-day onset rules out chronic etiologies; lower weight as it overlaps with item 4.

items.title: Schwartz formula structure
items.description: The response states the Schwartz formula as GFR = (k × height in cm) / serum creatinine in mg/dl, with the product of k and height in the numerator and serum creatinine in the denominator.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree on the formula structure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inverts the ratio or rearranges terms incorrectly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core formula structure; inverting numerator and denominator is a common error.

items.title: Constant k = 0.55
items.description: The response uses the constant k = 0.55 for this 2-year-old child in the Schwartz formula.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree on k = 0.55 for a 2-year-old in the original Schwartz formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response using k = 0.413 (bedside Schwartz) or k = 0.45 (infant constant) instead of 0.55.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct k value is essential; wrong constants yield wrong GFR.

items.title: Height 85 cm used
items.description: The response substitutes the child's height of 85 cm (not 0.85 m) into the numerator of the formula.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Height in meters' identifies the 0.85 m substitution error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports GFR = (0.55 × 0.85) / 2 = 0.234 ml/min/1.73 m².
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific input value; using meters instead of cm changes the result 100-fold.

items.title: Creatinine 2 mg/dl used
items.description: The response substitutes serum creatinine of 2 mg/dl as the denominator without converting to µmol/L.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Creatinine unit mix-up' identifies the µmol/L conversion error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports GFR = (0.55 × 85) / 176.8 = 0.264 ml/min/1.73 m².
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct input and unit; conversion to µmol/L would break the formula.

items.title: Numerator 46.75
items.description: The response shows the calculation (0.55 × 85) / 2 and computes the numerator as 46.75 before dividing.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states 0.55 × 85 = 46.75 as an intermediate step.
provenance.discriminates: A response that miscalculates the product or uses different operands.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate result; verifies the arithmetic path to the final GFR.

items.title: Final GFR 23.375
items.description: The response reports a final GFR of 23.375 ml/min/1.73 m² (or approximately 23.38 / 23.4).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference gives GFR = 23.375 ml/min/1.73 m², rounded to 23.38.
provenance.discriminates: A response reporting ~17.55, ~19.1, ~62, or any other value derived from a wrong constant or formula.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The single requested quantity; correctness collapses without it.

items.title: Units ml/min/1.73 m²
items.description: The response states the GFR units as ml/min/1.73 m².

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly gives units of ml/min/1.73 m².
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits units, uses ml/min alone, or uses incorrect units.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct units are required for a complete clinical answer.

items.title: Only height and creatinine
items.description: The response relies on the child's height and serum creatinine as the only variables in the formula, avoiding incorporation of weight (11 kg) or serum urea (49 mg/dl).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Distractor variables used' identifies weight 11 kg as a distractor not part of the canonical formula.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses 11 kg in a Cockcroft-Gault-style or otherwise modified calculation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distractor exclusion; weight and urea are not in the Schwartz formula.

items.title: Avoids wrong k constants
items.description: Avoids using k = 0.413 (updated bedside constant) or k = 0.45 (infant constant) instead of 0.55 for this 2-year-old child.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong k constant' identifies k = 0.413 as the wrong choice for the original formula context.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports GFR = (0.413 × 85) / 2 = 17.55 ml/min/1.73 m².
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific competing constants observed in flawed responses.

items.title: Avoids inverted ratio
items.description: Avoids placing serum creatinine of 2 mg/dl in the numerator and height of 85 cm in the denominator.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Inverted creatinine ratio' identifies the reversed formula structure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports GFR = (0.55 × 2) / 85 = 0.013 ml/min/1.73 m².
provenance.calibration_rationale: Inversion is a specific arithmetic trap producing a nonsensical value.

items.title: Clinical context note
items.description: The response notes that interpretations of the GFR should be made in the context of clinical evaluations and standards.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference includes this clinical caveat.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents the number without any statement that interpretation requires clinical context.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added clinical depth but not required for the calculation itself.

items.title: Names SIgAD
items.description: The response identifies the underlying immunological condition as Selective IgA Deficiency rather than stopping at anaphylaxis or Type I hypersensitivity alone.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Stops at anaphylaxis' (severity medium): the question asks for the underlying condition, not the reaction type.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that treat the acute reaction itself as the final answer rather than the predisposing immunodeficiency.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core diagnosis; absorbing the avoidance of stopping at anaphylaxis keeps one fact scored once.

items.title: Classifies anaphylaxis
items.description: The response classifies the transfusion reaction as anaphylaxis or anaphylaxis-like.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed the reaction type is anaphylactic (type I hypersensitivity); the reference uses the phrase 'anaphylaxis-like symptoms.'
provenance.discriminates: Responses that describe the reaction as hemolytic, febrile, or allergic without recognizing the anaphylactic nature.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Correct reaction classification frames the entire mechanism; high clinical importance.

items.title: Donor IgA trigger
items.description: The response identifies IgA present in the transfused blood products as the trigger antigen for the reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts identified donor IgA in blood products as the trigger; the reference states patients can have severe allergic reactions to blood products containing IgA.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that attribute the reaction to ABO antigens, drugs, or latex instead of donor IgA.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Names the specific antigen linking transfusion to SIgAD pathophysiology; key intermediate.

items.title: Anti-IgA antibodies
items.description: The response states that individuals with Selective IgA Deficiency develop anti-IgA antibodies that mediate the transfusion reaction.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts included anti-IgA antibodies as the mechanism; the reference says the immune system may not recognize IgA as self and can launch an attack.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that explain the reaction through a generic allergy mechanism without specifying anti-IgA antibodies.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Mechanism connecting diagnosis to reaction; central to explaining the case.

items.title: IgA not self
items.description: The response explains that the immune system in Selective IgA Deficiency does not recognize IgA as self, leading to antibody formation.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states 'Their immune system may not recognize IgA as self and can launch an attack'; no rollout included this specific mechanism.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that describe anti-IgA antibodies without explaining the loss of self-tolerance underlying their formation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains why anti-IgA antibodies arise; adds mechanistic depth.

items.title: Childhood infections
items.description: The response explains the history of mild recurrent infections during childhood as resulting from reduced IgA levels.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts linked the mild recurrent infections to IgA deficiency; the reference states people with this deficiency can experience recurrent infections.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that name Selective IgA Deficiency but do not connect it to the childhood infection history.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects the clinical history clue to the diagnosis; required intermediate reasoning.

items.title: Mucosal immunity role
items.description: The response states that IgA antibodies are crucial for mucosal immunity, protecting against infections of the respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states IgA antibodies are crucial for mucosal immunity; rollouts mentioned sinopulmonary/GI infections but did not state the mucosal immunity role.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that name IgA deficiency without explaining its functional role in mucosal defense.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains why low IgA causes sinopulmonary and GI infections; merged specific sites.

items.title: O negative excludes ABO
items.description: The response notes that transfusion with O negative packed red blood cells makes ABO or Rh incompatibility unlikely as the cause.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts agreed that O negative blood makes hemolytic reaction unlikely and symptoms are anaphylactic not hemolytic.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that attribute the reaction to ABO or Rh mismatch despite the use of O negative packed red blood cells.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Useful differential reasoning but not required to reach the diagnosis.

items.title: Avoids hemolytic error
items.description: Avoids classifying the transfusion reaction as a hemolytic transfusion reaction or acute hemolysis.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Hemolytic reaction misidentified' (severity high): the symptoms of pruritus, wheezing, and wheals are anaphylactic, not hemolytic.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that diagnose acute hemolytic transfusion reaction, missing the anaphylactic nature and the immunodeficiency.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common misclassification in transfusion contexts; observed pitfall requiring explicit avoidance.

items.title: Avoids wrong immunodeficiency
items.description: Avoids diagnosing CVID, Hyper-IgM syndrome, or SCID as the underlying immunological condition.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong immunodeficiency chosen' (severity high): several immunodeficiencies feature recurrent infections but only Selective IgA Deficiency classically causes anti-IgA anaphylaxis to blood products.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that select CVID or Hyper-IgM syndrome, which do not classically cause anti-IgA anaphylaxis to transfusions.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Plausible alternative immunodeficiencies that are incorrect for this presentation.

items.title: Screen with Test C
items.description: The response names Test C as the initial campus-wide screening test for the entire student body.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer specifies initial screening with Test C.
provenance.discriminates: A response that screens with Test A or Test B instead of Test C.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer component; selecting the correct screening test is essential to the scheme.

items.title: Confirm with Test A
items.description: The response names Test A as the secondary confirmation test for students with initial positive results.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer specifies confirmation with Test A.
provenance.discriminates: A response that confirms with Test B or Test C instead of Test A.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer component; selecting the correct confirmation test is essential to the scheme.

items.title: C highest sensitivity 0.98
items.description: The response states that Test C is chosen for initial screening because it has the highest sensitivity of 0.98.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and reference agree Test C screens due to highest sensitivity 0.98.
provenance.discriminates: A response that picks Test C without tying it to sensitivity 0.98.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key reasoning justifying Test C; ties the numeric value to the screening rationale.

items.title: A highest specificity 0.99
items.description: The response states that Test A is chosen for confirmation because it has the highest specificity of 0.99.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and reference agree Test A confirms due to highest specificity 0.99.
provenance.discriminates: A response that picks Test A without tying it to specificity 0.99.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key reasoning justifying Test A; ties the numeric value to the confirmation rationale.

items.title: Screen prioritizes sensitivity
items.description: The response explains that the initial screening step should prioritize maximizing sensitivity to catch potential positives.

provenance.evidence_detail: Implicit constraint: screening test should prioritize high sensitivity.
provenance.discriminates: A response that justifies screening with specificity rather than sensitivity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Underlying principle for the two-step approach; distinguishes screen from confirm.

items.title: Confirm prioritizes specificity
items.description: The response explains that the secondary confirmation step should prioritize minimizing false positives by using the test with the highest specificity.

provenance.evidence_detail: Implicit constraint: confirmatory test should prioritize high specificity.
provenance.discriminates: A response that justifies confirmation with sensitivity rather than specificity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Complementary principle for the confirmation step; central to the question's goal.

items.title: C lower specificity acceptable
items.description: The response acknowledges that Test C has a lower specificity of 0.93 but states this is acceptable for the initial screening because catching all potential positives is crucial.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference explicitly defends Test C's lower specificity as acceptable for initial screen; rollouts missed this nuance.
provenance.discriminates: A response that avoids mentioning the specificity tradeoff of Test C.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Addresses the trade-off in Test C; adds depth to the screening justification.

items.title: A sensitivity 0.92
items.description: The response reports Test A sensitivity as 0.92 when discussing the confirmation test.

provenance.evidence_detail: Given value for Test A sensitivity.
provenance.discriminates: A response that misstates Test A sensitivity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Supplementary numeric detail about Test A; not central to the scheme choice.

items.title: B sensitivity 0.95
items.description: The response reports Test B sensitivity as 0.95 when evaluating the three available tests.

provenance.evidence_detail: Given value for Test B sensitivity.
provenance.discriminates: A response that misstates Test B sensitivity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Minor numeric detail for a test not used in the final scheme.

items.title: B specificity 0.96
items.description: The response reports Test B specificity as 0.96 when evaluating the three available tests.

provenance.evidence_detail: Given value for Test B specificity.
provenance.discriminates: A response that misstates Test B specificity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Minor numeric detail for a test not used in the final scheme.

items.title: Both tests required for positive
items.description: The response states that a student is classified as HIV positive only if both the Test C screen and the Test A confirmation are positive.

provenance.evidence_detail: Implicit constraint: final positive classification requires positive on both tests (series interpretation).
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies only one test is needed for a final positive.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Clarifies the series logic; adds rigor to the two-step scheme description.

items.title: Avoids reversed logic
items.description: Avoids selecting Test A with specificity 0.99 for initial screening and Test C with sensitivity 0.98 for confirmation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: reversed screen/confirm logic, severity high.
provenance.discriminates: A response that screens with Test A and confirms with Test C.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly inverts the correct scheme; high-impact error observed in flawed responses.

items.title: Avoids Test B compromise
items.description: Avoids selecting Test B for either screening or confirmation on the basis that its sensitivity of 0.95 and specificity of 0.96 are balanced.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: compromise test selection, severity medium.
provenance.discriminates: A response that chooses Test B because it is the middle option.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common distractor reasoning; Test B is suboptimal for both roles in this scheme.

items.title: Avoids prevalence paralysis
items.description: Avoids declaring the question unsolvable or refusing to recommend a testing scheme because HIV prevalence on campus is not supplied.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall: prevalence paralysis, severity low.
provenance.discriminates: A response that refuses to answer due to missing prevalence.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Spurious refusal; prevalence is not needed to compare the three-test scheme.

items.title: Names Yersinia pestis
items.description: The response names Yersinia pestis as the most likely pathogen causing this patient's condition.

provenance.evidence_detail: The sole sub-question asks for the causative microorganism; the reference answer is Yersinia pestis.
provenance.discriminates: Any response that names a different or no pathogen.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; without naming the correct pathogen, the response fails entirely.

items.title: Identifies bubonic plague
items.description: The response identifies the clinical syndrome as bubonic plague and identifies the enlarged inguinal lymph nodes as a bubo.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and reference agree the syndrome is bubonic plague; naming the syndrome is load-bearing for the diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names Yersinia pestis without connecting it to bubonic plague, or one that names plague without the organism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Naming the syndrome links pathogen to presentation; key diagnostic reasoning step.

items.title: Southwestern US endemicity
items.description: The response links the southwestern United States travel history to plague endemicity and states that plague persists in wild rodent populations there.

provenance.evidence_detail: One rollout named specific SW states (New Mexico, Arizona, Colorado); this is extra depth not required by the reference.
provenance.discriminates: A response that provides only a vague geographic reference versus one that pins down specific endemic states.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Geographic context is central to the diagnosis; merges overlapping items into one.

items.title: Flea-vector transmission
items.description: The response attributes transmission of Yersinia pestis to fleas associated with rodents.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference identify flea-vector transmission from rodents as the relevant route.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the correct pathogen but invokes inhalation or direct-contact transmission instead of flea bite.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains mechanism of acquisition; required intermediate reasoning for this case.

items.title: Mouse droppings exposure
items.description: The response connects mouse droppings in the motel room to rodent exposure as the source of Yersinia pestis infection.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference link mouse droppings to the rodent reservoir for plague.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names the correct pathogen but does not tie the mouse droppings exposure to the diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Ties the key exposure clue from the stem to the rodent reservoir.

items.title: Absence of erythema and warmth
items.description: The response states that the absence of erythema and warmth over the swollen inguinal area supports plague over pyogenic cellulitis, and avoids diagnosing Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, inguinal hernia, or non-infectious lymphadenopathy on that basis.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Cellulitis/lymphadenitis error' notes that inguinal swelling with fever and rash commonly triggers a cellulitis diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that defaults to bacterial cellulitis or staphylococcal lymphadenitis despite the absence of erythema/warmth.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Differentiates plague from cellulitis and non-infectious mimics using exam findings.

items.title: Rash as flea-bite site
items.description: The response interprets the localized rash on the ipsilateral inner thigh as a flea-bite inoculation site draining to the inguinal lymph nodes, and avoids identifying it as an eschar pointing to tularemia or Rickettsia akari.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Rash misread as inoculation ulcer' notes the temptation to interpret the rash as an eschar and steer toward rickettsialpox or tularemia.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reclassifies the rash as an eschar and selects a rickettsial or tularemia diagnosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects the rash to the route of spread; integrates a pitfall avoidance into one item.

items.title: No animal contact still plausible
items.description: The response states that the absence of direct animal contact does not exclude flea-borne Yersinia pestis transmission.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Direct-contact assumption' notes the trap of excluding plague because no animal contact was reported.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reasons that no animal contact rules out plague and defaults to hantavirus or inhalational anthrax.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Addresses a specific trap in the stem; reinforces correct reasoning despite negative cue.

items.title: Fever and inguinal pain
items.description: The response states that fever and severe inguinal pain with swelling are consistent with bubonic plague.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference notes that symptoms including severe inguinal pain, swelling, and fever are consistent with bubonic plague.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names Yersinia pestis but does not connect the specific symptoms to the bubonic plague presentation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Confirms symptom fit; moderate discriminative value as supporting reasoning.

items.title: Avoids hantavirus
items.description: Avoids naming hantavirus or Sin Nombre virus as the causative pathogen and avoids defaulting to an inhalation-acquired rodent pathogen such as hantavirus or Bacillus anthracis based on the absence of direct animal contact.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Hantavirus trap' is the highest-severity distractor; mouse droppings in SW US is the classic hantavirus scenario.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects hantavirus because of the mouse droppings clue while ignoring the bubo and flea-bite rash.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Major trap anchored on mouse droppings in the southwestern United States; observed distractor.

items.title: Avoids tularemia
items.description: Avoids naming Francisella tularensis as the causative pathogen, which would misidentify the rodent exposure and lymphadenopathy as ulceroglandular tularemia rather than bubonic plague.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Tularemia misidentification' is a high-severity trap due to overlapping features of rodent exposure, rash, and lymphadenopathy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects tularemia due to the rash-lymphadenopathy combination without weighing the SW US plague context.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Plausible differential trap; observed distractor in flawed responses.

items.title: Avoids cellulitis misdiagnosis
items.description: Avoids diagnosing pyogenic cellulitis from Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes, or an inguinal hernia or non-infectious reactive lymphadenopathy, on the basis that the swollen inguinal area lacks erythema and warmth.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Cellulitis/lymphadenitis error' notes that inguinal swelling with fever and rash commonly triggers a cellulitis diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that defaults to bacterial cellulitis or staphylococcal lymphadenitis despite the absence of erythema/warmth.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Addresses misreading the exam findings; blends two related pitfalls into one item.

items.title: Selects option A
items.description: The response selects option A, CT cervical spine, as the next best step in management of this trauma patient.

provenance.evidence_detail: The single multiple-choice deliverable asks for the correct next step; reference answer states option A.
provenance.discriminates: A response that picks B, C, or D instead of A.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Directly names the correct management choice; essential to the answer.

items.title: Tenderness mandates imaging
items.description: The response states that the patient's exquisite cervical spine tenderness on palpation requires radiographic imaging before any clearance.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree that midline tenderness is the key finding driving the need for CT imaging.
provenance.discriminates: A response that identifies option A but fails to cite tenderness as the reason, making it indistinguishable from a lucky guess.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core clinical reasoning anchoring the answer; high discriminative value.

items.title: Mechanism supports imaging
items.description: The response cites the motor vehicle accident mechanism, including collision with a drunk driver traveling approximately 45 mph, as supporting cervical spine imaging.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference says 'given the mechanism of the trauma and her symptoms'; consensus_correct includes mechanism as supporting reasoning.
provenance.discriminates: A response that picks A based solely on tenderness without acknowledging the trauma mechanism.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Relevant trauma mechanism detail; supports imaging decision.

items.title: Collar remains in place
items.description: The response states that the cervical collar should remain in place until cervical spine injury is excluded by CT imaging.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct: 'Collar should remain in place until cervical spine injury is excluded.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects A but also implies the collar can be removed before imaging results.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Safety-critical; absence of collar removal is a key discriminative point.

items.title: Normal labs not clearance
items.description: The response states that the normal FAST exam and hemoglobin within normal limits do not exclude cervical spine injury and that CT imaging is still required.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Stable vitals → discharge' warns that normal FAST/Hb can be misread as overall clearance.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the normal FAST and hemoglobin as sufficient grounds to defer or skip cervical spine imaging.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Addresses a common flawed-response pattern; solid discriminative signal.

items.title: CT identifies fractures
items.description: The response states that CT cervical spine is performed to identify or rule out significant injuries such as fractures or instability.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer: 'allowing clinicians to identify or rule out any significant injuries, such as fractures or instability.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects A but does not explain what injuries CT is meant to detect.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains purpose of CT; aligns with reference answer reasoning.

items.title: GCS 15 no airway issue
items.description: The response notes that the patient has no airway compromise, citing GCS of 15, alert and oriented status, and speaking in complete sentences.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct includes 'GCS 15, stable vitals' as a key clinical descriptor supporting continued non-invasive management.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not incorporate the patient's neurological status, which is needed to rule out option D.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Anchors why intubation is not indicated; catches flawed RSI responses.

items.title: Stable vitals not exclusion
items.description: The response indicates that the patient's stable vitals and GCS of 15 do not exclude cervical spine injury and do not replace the need for CT imaging.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct and implicit constraints both note stability addresses hemorrhagic workup, not c-spine clearance.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses stable vitals as grounds to minimize or defer cervical spine imaging.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Prevents discharge-based-on-stability error; moderate discrimination.

items.title: CT preferred over plain films
items.description: The response states that CT cervical spine is the preferred first-line imaging modality over plain radiographs for cervical spine evaluation in adult blunt trauma.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus_correct: 'CT cervical spine preferred over plain radiographs.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects A but does not distinguish CT as the preferred modality over other imaging.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real added depth on imaging choice; modest discrimination expected.

items.title: Catastrophic outcome if missed
items.description: The response states that removing the collar or discharging the patient without imaging could lead to potentially catastrophic outcomes if a cervical spine injury is present.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference answer: 'Removing the cervical collar or discharging the patient without this crucial imaging could potentially lead to catastrophic outcomes if an injury is present.'
provenance.discriminates: A response that justifies option A without acknowledging the harm of premature collar removal or discharge.
provenance.calibration_rationale: References safety rationale from the reference answer; adds depth.

items.title: Avoids RSI in stable patient
items.description: Avoids selecting or recommending rapid sequence intubation given the patient is speaking in complete sentences with GCS of 15 and stable vitals.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Intubate stable airway' warns that ATLS airway-first thinking can trigger RSI despite no airway compromise.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects option D or suggests intubation is needed because this is a trauma activation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Targets wrong option D; catches intubation-in-stable-patient error.

items.title: Avoids discharge on stability
items.description: Avoids selecting discharge home and physical therapy on the basis of stable vitals, normal FAST exam, and normal hemoglobin alone.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Stable vitals → discharge' describes conflating hemodynamic stability with overall clearance.
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes the patient can be discharged because all listed positive findings are reassuring.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Targets wrong option C; catches premature discharge error.

items.title: Avoids self-extrication clearance
items.description: Avoids using the patient's ability to extricate herself from the crushed car and sit on the ground as evidence that cervical spine imaging is unnecessary.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Overweight self-extrication' describes treating self-rescue as clinical clearance, leading to option B or C.
provenance.discriminates: A response that argues the patient's self-extrication means the c-spine is likely uninjured, justifying collar removal or discharge.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Targets a specific reasoning trap from the clinical vignette.

items.title: Lobectomy as ideal treatment
items.description: The response states that lobectomy is the ideal treatment for this 40-year-old male with papillary thyroid cancer confined to one lobe.

provenance.evidence_detail: The sub-question asks for the ideal treatment; the reference answer identifies lobectomy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that recommends total thyroidectomy or gives only a generic 'surgery' answer.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core answer; lobectomy is the correct intervention and the question's central ask.

items.title: 4 cm size threshold
items.description: The response identifies 4 cm as the American Thyroid Association size threshold and notes that the 3x3 cm tumor, with a maximum diameter of 3 cm, falls below it.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts and the reference agree the tumor at 3 cm is below the 4 cm ATA threshold for total thyroidectomy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the tumor exceeds the threshold size for lobectomy eligibility.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key discriminative threshold; the 3 cm vs 4 cm comparison is central to the reasoning.

items.title: Confined to one lobe
items.description: The response acknowledges that the papillary thyroid cancer is confined to one lobe as a criterion supporting lobectomy.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree that intrathyroidal disease confined to one lobe is a key criterion for lobectomy eligibility.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ignores the single-lobe confinement and treats the tumor as multifocal or bilateral.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Removes ambiguity about extent; supports the lobectomy recommendation.

items.title: No regional metastasis
items.description: The response identifies the absence of regional metastasis or clinically node-negative status with no palpable lymph nodes as a factor supporting lobectomy.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference agree that cN0 status (no palpable lymph nodes) is a key criterion for lobectomy eligibility.
provenance.discriminates: A response that ignores nodal status or assumes nodal involvement requiring more extensive surgery.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Node-negative status is a required criterion for lobectomy eligibility.

items.title: Low-risk categorization
items.description: The response classifies this papillary thyroid cancer case as low-risk based on tumor size below 4 cm, intrathyroidal extent, and no palpable lymph nodes.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer describes the case as low-risk per ATA criteria for tumors smaller than 4 cm confined to one lobe with no regional metastasis.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats this as intermediate or high-risk and therefore recommends more aggressive surgery.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Frames the clinical reasoning linking the case features to the treatment choice.

items.title: Cites ATA guidelines
items.description: The response references American Thyroid Association guidelines as the basis for recommending lobectomy in this case.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer cites American Thyroid Association guidelines for the low-risk criteria supporting lobectomy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that gives the correct answer without anchoring it to any guideline body.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Grounds the recommendation in the authoritative source cited by the reference answer.

items.title: Hormone replacement rationale
items.description: The response states that lobectomy minimizes the need for lifelong thyroid hormone replacement compared to total thyroidectomy.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer explicitly cites minimization of lifelong thyroid hormone replacement as a rationale for choosing lobectomy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that recommends lobectomy without explaining the hormone replacement advantage over total thyroidectomy.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the clinical advantage of lobectomy; taken directly from the reference answer.

items.title: Avoids total thyroidectomy
items.description: Avoids recommending total thyroidectomy as the required or ideal treatment, avoids using the unqualified term thyroidectomy without specifying lobectomy, and avoids claiming that smaller intrathyroidal tumors require total thyroidectomy while larger ones permit lobectomy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Wrong size cutoff (2 cm)' and 'Reversed surgery-size logic' both lead to erroneously recommending total thyroidectomy.
provenance.discriminates: A response that claims total thyroidectomy is necessary because the tumor exceeds a misremembered 2 cm threshold.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Names the primary wrong move; merged three variants of the same size-logic error.

items.title: Avoids routine RAI
items.description: Avoids adding radioactive iodine ablation to the treatment plan for this low-risk papillary thyroid cancer measuring 3x3 cm with no palpable lymph nodes.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Adding unnecessary RAI' warns against reflexively appending radioactive iodine to low-risk intrathyroidal PTC <4 cm.
provenance.discriminates: A response that recommends lobectomy plus adjuvant radioactive iodine for this low-risk case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific overtreatment trap for low-risk papillary thyroid cancer.

items.title: Avoids prophylactic CND
items.description: Avoids including prophylactic central neck dissection as a routine component of the ideal treatment for this papillary thyroid cancer with no palpable lymph nodes.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Ipsilateral prophylactic CND' warns against adding prophylactic central neck dissection to low-risk cN0 intrathyroidal PTC.
provenance.discriminates: A response that recommends lobectomy plus prophylactic central neck dissection for this cN0 case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific overtreatment trap when lymph nodes are not palpable.

items.title: Total thyroidectomy as alternative
items.description: The response notes that total thyroidectomy is an acceptable alternative but is not required for this 3x3 cm papillary thyroid cancer confined to one lobe.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts noted total thyroidectomy is an alternative but not mandated; the reference focuses on lobectomy as ideal.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents total thyroidectomy as contraindicated rather than as an acceptable but non-required alternative.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds nuance without being essential; reflects ATA framing of both options.

items.title: Patient age incorporated
items.description: The response incorporates the 40-year-old age of the patient into its treatment reasoning for papillary thyroid cancer.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question specifies age 40 as a given clinical parameter; the reference uses it to classify the case as low-risk.
provenance.discriminates: A response that omits age from consideration entirely.

items.title: States conditions are distinct

items.title: References infancy presentation

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer notes that overlapping symptoms are seen especially during infancy.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Minor contextual accuracy from the reference answer; low discrimination.

items.title: Avoids wrong syndrome

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Naming Lightwood syndrome' identifies this as a foreseen error where the respondent names a synonym for IIH instead of the distinct Williams syndrome.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names Lightwood syndrome instead of Williams syndrome, confusing the condition itself for the resembling syndrome.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Common confusion traps specific to this question; observed pitfalls merged into one.
