items.title: Transference named and defined
items.description: The response identifies the phenomenon as transference, specifying that it involves the patient unconsciously projecting feelings and attitudes from early relationships with significant figures such as parents or caregivers onto the therapist, directed from patient to therapist.

provenance.evidence_detail: The question asks to describe the clinical phenomenon; the reference names transference as the primary concept.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes the situation in lay terms without ever naming transference.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core concept of the question; transference is the primary phenomenon being asked about.

items.title: Idealization as mechanism
items.description: The response identifies idealization as a mechanism alongside transference, describing the patient viewing the therapist as exceptionally understanding and perceiving the therapist as empathetic in a way that affirms their sense of being uniquely understood.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly links the perceived deep empathy to the patient's sense of being uniquely understood and the subsequent affectionate feelings.
provenance.discriminates: A response that names transference and idealization but does not connect the perceived empathy to the patient's sense of being uniquely understood.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Second key mechanism in the reference answer; adds necessary depth beyond transference alone.

items.title: Perception is distortion
items.description: The response characterizes the patient's belief that the therapist deeply understands their emotions as an idealized distortion rather than an accurate reading of therapeutic rapport.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Genuine rapport framing' pitfall is high severity; the reference explicitly frames the perception as mistaken and a distortion.
provenance.discriminates: A response that frames the patient's perception as accurate empathy or healthy therapeutic rapport.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Central to the question's premise that the patient mistakenly feels understood; without this the answer misframes the scenario.

items.title: Distinguishes from countertransference
items.description: The response explicitly identifies the phenomenon as transference and not countertransference, recognising that countertransference would refer to the therapist's feelings toward the patient, not the patient's feelings toward the therapist.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Countertransference mislabel' pitfall is high severity and foreseen; reversing the direction is a common error.
provenance.discriminates: A response that calls the phenomenon countertransference instead of transference.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Critical distinction; mislabeling as countertransference reverses the direction of the dynamic entirely.

items.title: Misreads professional empathy
items.description: The response states that the patient misinterprets the therapist's structured and empathetic attributes as signs of a personal emotional connection.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Omitting professional-behavior misread' pitfall (medium severity) and reference_only finding both note that the therapist's professional behavior is the trigger being misread.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains the distortion as pure internal projection without specifying what external stimulus is being misinterpreted.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the mechanism of the distortion; answers why affectionate feelings develop from a therapeutic context.

items.title: EUPD vacillation cycle
items.description: The response notes that patients with emotionally unstable personality disorder vacillate between idealizing and devaluing important figures including therapists.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states EUPD patients vacillate between idealizing and devaluing; no rollout mentioned this cycle.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents a static, one-way idealization without the characteristic EUPD devaluation cycle.
provenance.calibration_rationale: EUPD-specific pattern that contextualizes idealization within the diagnostic features of the disorder.

items.title: Craving for validation
items.description: The response identifies a deep craving for validation and support in EUPD patients as a contributing driver of the transference and idealization.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly names the craving for validation as the motivational engine; no rollout mentioned it.
provenance.discriminates: A response that explains the transference mechanism without identifying the validation-seeking motivation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Adds explanatory depth for why the patient develops these feelings; drawn from the reference answer.

items.title: EUPD magnifies intensity
items.description: The response acknowledges that the emotional intensity and instability characteristic of emotionally unstable personality disorder magnify the effects of transference.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states the intensity and instability of emotions in EUPD magnify transference effects, making the therapeutic process more complex.
provenance.discriminates: A response that describes transference generically without linking it specifically to EUPD's emotional intensity.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Supplementary link between the diagnosis and transference intensity; nice-to-have context.

items.title: Maintain therapeutic boundaries
items.description: The response states that the therapist maintains boundaries while helping the patient explore these affectionate feelings in a healthy and constructive way.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference discusses boundary maintenance as part of clinical management; no rollout addressed management implications.
provenance.discriminates: A purely descriptive response that names the phenomenon but is silent on boundary maintenance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Practical implication for the therapist; real added depth in the clinical context.

items.title: Therapeutic exploration utility
items.description: The response states that recognizing these feelings within the therapeutic context allows for deeper exploration of the patient's relational patterns and emotional processing.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference notes that recognizing transference allows deeper exploration of relational patterns; no rollout discussed this utility.
provenance.discriminates: A response that identifies the phenomenon but does not connect it to therapeutic utility for exploring relational patterns.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Explains the clinical value of recognizing transference; rounds out the therapeutic relevance.

items.title: Avoids eroticized overlabel
items.description: Avoids upgrading the affectionate feelings described in the question to eroticized transference, which would imply sexual or romantic content the question does not describe.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Eroticized transference overlabel' pitfall is medium severity and was observed in rollout 1; the reference does not use the term eroticized.
provenance.discriminates: A response that labels the phenomenon as eroticized transference rather than positive/idealizing transference with affectionate feelings.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific over-labeling trap; affectionate does not equal eroticized, and inflating the label is a diagnostic error.

items.title: Feelings positive or negative
items.description: The response notes that transference can involve positive or negative feelings projected onto the therapist, with the affectionate feelings in this case representing the positive pole.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference describes transference feelings as positive or negative, providing the affective context for the affectionate presentation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that implies transference is exclusively positive or exclusively negative.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Contextualizes the affectionate feelings within the broader spectrum of transference phenomena.

items.title: Combination of mechanisms
items.description: The response describes the situation as a combination of transference and idealization operating together rather than attributing it to a single isolated mechanism.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly frames the situation as a combination of transference and idealization, a framing no single rollout fully captured.
provenance.discriminates: A response that presents only one mechanism without acknowledging the combination.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Captures the reference answer's framing of both phenomena working in combination; ties the answer together.

provenance.discriminates: A response that fails to connect the low HCO3- of 12 mmol/L to metabolic acidosis.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Concrete lab value anchoring one half of the mixed disorder.

items.title: pCO2 18 respiratory alkalosis
items.description: Identifies the pCO2 of 18 mmHg as below normal, indicating respiratory alkalosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts and the reference identify the low pCO2 of 18 mmHg as respiratory alkalosis.

items.title: Winter's formula comparison
items.description: Calculates the expected pCO2 using Winter's formula as 1.5 × 12 + 8 ± 2 = 26 ± 2 mmHg and states that the actual pCO2 of 18 mmHg is below this expected compensatory range, confirming an additional respiratory alkalosis.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts correctly computed expected pCO2 = 1.5 × 12 + 8 ± 2 = 26 ± 2 mmHg, range 24–28 mmHg.
provenance.discriminates: A response that skips Winter's formula or computes an incorrect expected pCO2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key intermediate reasoning distinguishing mixed disorder from simple compensation.

items.title: Link to salicylic acid
items.description: Links the mixed acid-base disorder to salicylic acid poisoning.

items.title: Metabolic acidosis primary
items.description: Identifies metabolic acidosis as the dominant primary process because the pH of 7.1 is acidemic.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Critical distinction: acidemia makes metabolic acidosis the primary, not respiratory.

items.title: Avoids single-disorder label

items.title: Avoids reversing primary

provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes 'primary respiratory alkalosis with metabolic compensation' rather than metabolic acidosis as the dominant process.

items.title: CO2 exhalation mechanism

provenance.calibration_rationale: Merges avoidance and positive note; prevents overstating AG without data.

items.title: 15 million/ml borderline
items.description: States that the sperm count of 15 million/ml is at the lower threshold or borderline of the normal range, referencing the WHO lower reference limit of 15 million/ml for sperm concentration.

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollouts disagreed on whether to apply the WHO 2010 cutoff of 15 million/ml or the older 20 million/ml cutoff; the reference frames 15 million/ml as the lower threshold.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that use an incorrect cutoff (e.g., 20 million/ml) and therefore miscalculate the degree of abnormality.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key reasoning linking the borderline count to the diagnosis; central to correctness.

items.title: Borderline count explains infertility
items.description: States that the borderline sperm count of 15 million/ml contributes to the 25-year-old patient's fertility challenges despite normal findings in other semen analysis parameters.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states: 'Despite the normal findings in other aspects of the analysis, the slightly lower sperm concentration may impact overall fertility, which aligns with a diagnosis of mild oligospermia.'
provenance.discriminates: Responses that do not link the borderline count to the patient's infertility or that attribute infertility to other unproven causes.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Connects the lab finding to the clinical presentation; important reasoning step.

items.title: 60% motility is normal
items.description: States that the motility of 60% motile sperms is within the normal range.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Asthenozoospermia mislabel' notes that 60% motility exceeds WHO 2010 (≥40%) and older WHO (≥50%) thresholds; classifying it as abnormal is an error.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that misread 60% motility as abnormal and diagnose asthenozoospermia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Distinguishes the single abnormal parameter from preserved motility; guards against overcalling.

items.title: 60% morphology is normal
items.description: States that the morphology showing 60% normal sperms is within the normal range.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Teratozoospermia mislabel' notes that 60% normal morphology is well above all commonly used thresholds (≥4% strict; ≥30% older); classifying it as abnormal is an error.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that apply an incorrect high morphology cutoff and diagnose teratozoospermia.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Confirms morphology is not contributing; prevents misdiagnosis of teratospermia.

items.title: Volume and pH normal
items.description: States that the semen volume of 2 ml and the pH of 7.5 are within the normal range.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Obstructive diagnosis overcall' notes that volume 2 ml is within normal limits and should not trigger an obstructive diagnosis.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that treat 2 ml as low and infer an obstructive component such as CBAVD or ejaculatory duct obstruction.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Rules out volume or pH abnormalities; narrows the diagnosis to count alone.

items.title: Total sperm number below WHO limit
items.description: Computes the total sperm number per ejaculate as 30 million by multiplying the sperm count of 15 million/ml by the volume of 2 ml, and states that this is below the WHO lower reference limit of 39 million per ejaculate.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Total sperm number omission' notes that 30 million is below the WHO lower limit of 39 million, making it the more definitively abnormal parameter.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that conclude the count is only borderline without recognizing the total sperm number is clearly below the WHO limit.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate calculation that strengthens the oligospermia diagnosis.

items.title: No agglutination, not immunologic
items.description: States that the absence of agglutination in the semen analysis findings argues against an immunologic or anti-sperm antibody cause of infertility.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Immunologic cause overcall': ignoring absent agglutination and nonetheless invoking anti-sperm antibody infertility.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that add immunologic infertility or anti-sperm antibody as a contributing diagnosis despite negative agglutination.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Uses a stated finding to exclude a specific alternative diagnosis; discriminator.

items.title: Normal volume and pH exclude obstruction
items.description: States that the normal volume of 2 ml and pH of 7.5 argue against obstructive causes such as CBAVD or ejaculatory duct obstruction.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Obstructive diagnosis overcall': interpreting volume 2 ml as low and adding an obstructive component.
provenance.discriminates: Responses that add obstructive azoospermia or CBAVD to the diagnosis despite normal volume and pH.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Excludes obstructive etiologies using two normal parameters; prevents overcall.

items.title: Suggests specialist consultation

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference answer includes a suggestion to consider further evaluation or consultation with a fertility specialist, which no rollout addressed.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific overcall risk for this borderline count; naming the wrong severity is a grading error.

items.title: Earth launch speed
items.description: The response derives the initial speed on Earth as v₀ = √(gL) = √1200 ≈ 34.6 m/s from the Earth range of 120 m at 45°, using v₀²sin(2θ)/g with sin(90°) = 1, and avoids computing the launch speed as √(2gL) or other misapplications of the range formula.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Launch speed formula misuse' pitfall (medium severity) notes the temptation to include the factor of 2 or mishandle sin(2θ).
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives v₀ ≈ 49 m/s or another incorrect value, propagating a ~40% error through all subsequent calculations.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary intermediate; gold=FAIL but load-bearing. Absorbs pitfall 15.

validation.gold_why: Uses correct √(gL) implicitly; no misuse.

items.title: Velocity components at 45°
items.description: The response states that the radial and tangential components of the ball's velocity relative to the batter are each v₀/√2 ≈ 24.5 m/s for the 45° launch in the habitat.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts agree on u = v₀/√2 = 10√6 ≈ 24.49 m/s for each component at 45°.
provenance.discriminates: A response that assigns different values to the components or fails to decompose the velocity at 45°.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=FAIL but required intermediate for both prograde and retrograde cases.

validation.gold_why: Does not state v₀/√2 ≈ 24.5 m/s numerically.

items.title: Habitat tangential speed
items.description: The response computes the habitat's tangential speed at radius R = 10000 m as V = √(gR) ≈ 316 m/s and the angular velocity as ω = √(g/R) ≈ 0.0316 rad/s from the apparent gravity condition ω²R = g.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts compute V = ωR = √(gR) ≈ 316.23 m/s and ω = √(g/R) ≈ 0.03162 rad/s.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses R = 10 (in km) directly, yielding V = √(10×10) = 10 m/s, or omits the unit conversion of R from 10 km to 10000 m.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=FAIL but essential intermediate; anchors the unit consistency.

validation.gold_why: Uses √(gR) symbolically but does not compute ≈ 316 m/s.

items.title: Inertial straight-line trajectory
items.description: The response models the ball as traveling in a straight line at constant velocity in the inertial frame after leaving the surface of the habitat, with no real gravitational force acting on it, and avoids applying the flat-Earth projectile range formula v²sin(2θ)/g with the habitat's apparent gravity g to obtain 120 m.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'Flat projectile approximation' pitfall (high severity) notes that reusing the Earth range formula gives 120 m, ignoring curvature and Coriolis effects.
provenance.discriminates: A response that simply reports 120 m, reasoning that the same v₀, θ, and g produce the same range.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass; core physical insight. Absorbs pitfall 11 which caught 0/1.

validation.gold_why: Uses inertial-frame geometry, not flat projectile formula.

items.title: Inertial speed composition
items.description: The response composes the inertial tangential velocity as V + v_t for the prograde hit and V − v_t for the retrograde hit, where v_t ≈ 24.5 m/s is the tangential component relative to the batter.

provenance.evidence_detail: All correct rollouts add the tangential component to V for prograde and subtract for retrograde; the reference gives u_± = √(v_y² + (V ± v_x)²).
provenance.discriminates: A response that swaps the signs, assigning the larger inertial speed to the retrograde direction or vice versa.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass; key reasoning step splitting the two cases.

validation.gold_why: Uses u_+ with (V + v_x) and u_- with (V - v_x).

items.title: Prograde distance value

provenance.discriminates: A response that reports a prograde distance of 132 m due to a sign error, or never computes the prograde case.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass; one of the two requested numerical answers.

validation.gold_why: Reports L_+ ≈ 108 m.

provenance.discriminates: A response that gives 133.1 m from premature rounding, or gives only the prograde value of 108 m.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Gold=pass, caught 1/1 negatives; discrimination=1.00, the furthest distance answer.

items.title: Position completeness insertion
items.description: Explicitly inserts the position completeness relation ∫dx'|x'⟩⟨x'| when evaluating ⟨p'|x|alpha⟩ in part (i).

provenance.evidence_detail: Part a(i) requires proving ⟨p'|x|α⟩ = iħ∂⟨p'|α⟩/∂p'; the reference derivation begins by inserting ∫dx'|x'⟩⟨x'|.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the result without derivational steps, or uses hand-waving Fourier analogy instead of the completeness insertion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core first step of the proof; 0 discrimination but load-bearing structural step.

validation.gold_why: Inserts ∫dx'|x'⟩⟨x'| in the proof of part (i).

items.title: Position eigenvalue extraction
items.description: Evaluates x on the position eigenstate |x'⟩ to produce the eigenvalue x', giving the integrand x'⟨p'|x'⟩⟨x'|alpha⟩ in part (i).

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Misapplying x operator': the correct approach has x act on |x'⟩ giving eigenvalue x', not on |α⟩.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inserts completeness but lets x act on the wrong factor, never reaching the momentum-space derivative.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate step; 0 discrimination but essential for converting operator to value.

validation.gold_why: Uses x|x'⟩=x'|x'⟩, integrand has x'⟨p'|x'⟩⟨x'|α⟩.

items.title: Derivative identity step
items.description: Uses the identity x'·exp(-ip'x'/hbar) = i hbar ∂/∂p' exp(-ip'x'/hbar) to convert the position eigenvalue into a momentum derivative in part (i).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly writes x' = iħ ∂_{p'} acting on the exponential as a load-bearing algebraic step.
provenance.discriminates: A response that inserts completeness and pulls out x' but cannot show how x' converts to iħ∂/∂p', leaving a logical gap.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Key algebraic move enabling the result; 0 discrimination but structurally essential.

validation.gold_why: Recognizes x'exp(-ip'x'/ℏ)=iℏ∂/∂p' exp(-ip'x'/ℏ).

items.title: Plane-wave overlap used
items.description: Uses the plane-wave overlap ⟨p'|x'⟩ = A exp(-ip'x'/hbar), with A a normalization constant, in the derivation of part (i).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference writes ⟨p'|x'⟩ = A e^{-ip'x'/ħ} with A left generic; all rollouts instead used the explicit (2πħ)^{-1/2} convention.
provenance.discriminates: A response that does not exhibit the plane-wave overlap at all, leaving the step from completeness insertion to the derivative unconnected.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Real intermediate detail; 0 discrimination, low importance to final correctness.

validation.gold_why: Uses ⟨p'|x'⟩=A exp(-ip'x'/ℏ).

items.title: Correct +iħ result (i)
items.description: Arrives at the final result ⟨p'|x|alpha⟩ = i hbar ∂/∂p' ⟨p'|alpha⟩ with the +i hbar sign in part (i).

provenance.evidence_detail: Equation (1.45) in the reference is the target of part a(i).
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives -iħ∂/∂p' instead of +iħ∂/∂p' due to mishandling the exponential derivative.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The statement being proved; correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: Arrives at ⟨p'|x|α⟩=iℏ∂/∂p'⟨p'|α⟩ with +iℏ.

items.title: Momentum completeness insertion
items.description: Inserts momentum completeness ∫dp'|p'⟩⟨p'| and applies the result from part (i) to evaluate ⟨beta|x|alpha⟩ in part (ii).

provenance.evidence_detail: Equation (1.46) in the reference begins by inserting ∫dp'⟨β|p'⟩⟨p'|x|α⟩ and substituting part (i).
provenance.discriminates: A response that attempts part (ii) without using the result of part (i) or without inserting momentum completeness.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core structural step linking parts (i) and (ii); 0 discrimination but load-bearing.

validation.gold_why: Inserts ∫dp'|p'⟩⟨p'| and applies part (i).

items.title: Correct integral result (ii)
items.description: Arrives at ⟨beta|x|alpha⟩ = ∫dp' phi*_beta(p') i hbar ∂/∂p' phi_alpha(p') in part (ii).

provenance.evidence_detail: Equation (1.46) is the target of part a(ii).
provenance.discriminates: A response that produces a different integral form, e.g., with the derivative acting on phi*_beta or with a minus sign.
provenance.calibration_rationale: The statement being proved; correctness collapses without it.

validation.gold_why: Arrives at the correct integral result with +iℏ.

items.title: Wave function identification
items.description: Identifies ⟨beta|p'⟩ = phi*_beta(p') and ⟨p'|alpha⟩ = phi_alpha(p') as the momentum-space wave functions in part (ii).

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference explicitly states ⟨β|p'⟩ = φ*_β(p') and ⟨p'|α⟩ = φ_α(p') to connect the abstract matrix element to the wave-function notation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes the integral but does not connect it to the defined wave functions phi_alpha and phi_beta.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required identification connecting abstract states to wave functions; 0 discrimination.

validation.gold_why: Identifies ⟨β|p'⟩=φ*_β(p') and ⟨p'|α⟩=φ_α(p').

items.title: Derivative scope on phi_alpha
items.description: Avoids letting ∂/∂p' act on the full product phi*_beta(p') phi_alpha(p'); the derivative i hbar ∂/∂p' acts only on phi_alpha(p') in the integrand.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Inclusion-boundary term dropped': the derivative must act only on phi_alpha, not on the product or on phi*_beta.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ∫dp' iħ ∂/∂p'(phi*_beta · phi_alpha) or integrates by parts incorrectly.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Specific trap in part (ii); 0 discrimination but names a real product-rule error.

validation.gold_why: Derivative acts only on φ_α(p'), not on the product.

items.title: Momentum translation significance
items.description: States that exp(i x Ξ / hbar) is the momentum translation operator that shifts momentum eigenstates by Ξ.

provenance.discriminates: A response that identifies the operator as a position-translation operator or fails to state the physical significance.

items.title: Commutator [p,U]=ΞU computed
items.description: Computes the commutator [p, exp(i Ξ x / hbar)] = Ξ · exp(i Ξ x / hbar) using the canonical commutator [x, p] = i hbar.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference derives this via series expansion (equation 1.47) as the key step in the justification.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states the significance of exp(iΞx/ħ) without computing the commutator that justifies it.

items.title: Eigenvalue equation on |p'⟩
items.description: Acts the commutator [p, exp(i Ξ x / hbar)] on the eigenstate |p'⟩ and rearranges to obtain p(exp(i Ξ x / hbar)|p'⟩) = (p' + Ξ)(exp(i Ξ x / hbar)|p'⟩).

provenance.evidence_detail: Equation (1.48) in the reference explicitly performs this rearrangement to extract the shifted eigenvalue.
provenance.discriminates: A response that computes [p,U]=ΞU but does not act on |p'⟩ to show the eigenvalue shift.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate derivation step; 0 discrimination but structurally necessary.

items.title: Avoids conjugation sign error
items.description: Avoids writing UpU^{-1} = p + Ξ for U = exp(i Ξ x / hbar); the correct relation is U^{-1}pU = p + Ξ (or equivalently UpU^{-1} = p - Ξ).

provenance.evidence_detail: Rollout 1 wrote UpU^{-1}=p+Ξ (wrong) while Rollouts 2,3 wrote U^{-1}pU=p+Ξ (correct); the reference derives pU=U(p+Ξ) which implies UpU^{-1}=p-Ξ.

validation.gold_why: Avoids UpU⁻¹=p+Ξ; uses commutator approach instead.

items.title: Normalization constant A noted
items.description: Includes a normalization constant A in the relation exp(i Ξ x / hbar)|p'⟩ ≡ A|p' + Ξ⟩ and notes that A can be taken to 1 by normalization.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Added rigor; discrimination 1.00 but properly optional and discounted as pitfall-adjacent.

items.title: Conclusion |p'+Ξ⟩ proportional
items.description: Concludes that exp(i Ξ x / hbar)|p'⟩ is proportional to |p' + Ξ⟩, thus establishing that momentum shifts up by Ξ.

provenance.evidence_detail: Equation (1.49) gives exp(iΞx/ħ)|p'⟩ ≡ A|p'+Ξ⟩; this is the final justified result of part (b).
provenance.discriminates: A response that concludes the shift is |p'-Ξ⟩ (downward) due to a sign error in the commutator or eigenvalue read-off.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Final mathematical conclusion of part (b); the justification endpoint.

validation.gold_why: Concludes exp(iΞx/ℏ)|p'⟩≡A|p'+Ξ⟩.

items.title: Pressure stoichiometry P0+x
items.description: States or uses the relation that the total pressure after decomposition equals P0 + x, where x is the pressure drop of CH3CHO, consistent with 1 mole of reactant producing 2 moles of gaseous products (CH4 and CO).

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference derives P_total = P0 + x from the stoichiometry CH3CHO → CH4 + CO.
provenance.discriminates: A response that misidentifies the pressure relation (e.g., P_total = P0 + 2x or P_total = P0 − x) obtains wrong x values and propagates errors through the entire solution.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; load-bearing for all downstream pressure calculations.

validation.gold_why: Uses P0+x relation explicitly.

items.title: x1 = 100 mmHg
items.description: Computes the pressure drop x1 = 100 mmHg for the experiment with initial pressure 400 mmHg and total pressure 500 mmHg after 100 sec.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: when P0 = 400, after 100 sec, x = 100 (P0 + x = 500).
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses P_total = P0 + 2x would obtain x1 = 50 instead of 100, corrupting all downstream calculations.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; required intermediate for rate and order calculations.

validation.gold_why: x=100 for P0=400 stated.

items.title: x2 = 26 mmHg
items.description: Computes the pressure drop x2 = 26 mmHg for the experiment with initial pressure 200 mmHg and total pressure 226 mmHg after 100 sec.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: when P0 = 200, after 100 sec, x = 26 (P0 + x = 226).
provenance.discriminates: A response that misapplies stoichiometry would obtain x2 = 13 or 52 instead of 26.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; required intermediate for rate and order calculations.

validation.gold_why: x=26 for P0=200 stated.

items.title: Rate r1 = 1.0
items.description: Computes the rate r1 = 1.0 mmHg/sec as x1 divided by the time of 100 sec (i.e., 100/100), using dx/dt.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: r1 = (300 − 400)/100 = 1, equivalently r1 = x1/t = 100/100 = 1.0.
provenance.discriminates: A response that uses the wrong time interval or miscalculates the rate would produce a different r1, affecting the order determination.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; simple but essential input to the order formula.

validation.gold_why: r1=1 computed as 100/100.

items.title: Rate r2 = 0.26
items.description: Computes the rate r2 = 0.26 mmHg/sec as x2 divided by the time of 100 sec (i.e., 26/100), using dx/dt.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: r2 = 0.26, obtained from x2 = 26 over t = 100 sec.
provenance.discriminates: A response pairing the rate with incorrect x or time values would obtain a different r2, shifting the computed order.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; simple but essential input to the order formula.

validation.gold_why: r2=0.26 computed as 26/100.

items.title: Order formula ln ratio
items.description: Applies the differential order formula n = ln(r1/r2) / ln(a1/a2) using the initial pressures a1 = 400 and a2 = 200 as the concentration terms.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: n = ln(r1/r2) / ln(a1/a2) with a1 = 400 and a2 = 200.
provenance.discriminates: A response using remaining pressures (300 and 174) instead of initial pressures (400 and 200) as concentration terms would get n ≈ 2.5 instead of ≈ 2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; key reasoning step linking rates to reaction order.

validation.gold_why: Applies n=ln(r1/r2)/ln(a1/a2).

items.title: Order n approximately 2
items.description: Reports the reaction order n as approximately 2 (near 1.94 or 1.943) with respect to CH3CHO.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: n = ln(1/0.26)/ln(400/200) ≈ 1.94, rounded to 2.
provenance.discriminates: A response with incorrect intermediate values would produce a different order (e.g., 1.5 or 2.5).
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; directly answers the first requested quantity.

validation.gold_why: Reports n≈1.94, rounds to 2.

items.title: Second-order rate law
items.description: Applies the second-order integrated rate law k = (1/t) · x / [a(a − x)] for calculating the rate constant from both experimental data sets, where a is the initial pressure and (a − x) is the remaining pressure.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference uses k = (1/t) · x / [a(a−x)], the second-order integrated rate law in pressure units.
provenance.discriminates: A response using the first-order law k = (1/t)·ln[a/(a−x)] or zero-order k = x/t would produce k values off by orders of magnitude with wrong units.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; the correct rate law determines the entire k calculation.

validation.gold_why: Uses k=(1/t)·x/[a(a−x)].

items.title: k1 = 8.33e-6
items.description: Computes k from experiment 1 (P0 = 400, x = 100, remaining = 300) as 8.33 × 10⁻⁶ mmHg⁻¹·sec⁻¹ using t = 100 sec.

provenance.discriminates: A response using the wrong rate law or wrong x would obtain a different k1 value or different units.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; one of two required rate constant values.

validation.gold_why: k1=8.33e-6 from experiment 1.

items.title: k2 = 7.47e-6
items.description: Computes k from experiment 2 (P0 = 200, x = 26, remaining = 174) as 7.47 × 10⁻⁶ mmHg⁻¹·sec⁻¹ using t = 100 sec.

provenance.discriminates: A response computing k from only one experiment or using wrong values would miss this second rate constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; second rate constant value needed for averaging.

validation.gold_why: k2=7.47e-6 from experiment 2.

items.title: Average k = 7.9e-6
items.description: Reports the average rate constant k at 500°C as 7.9 × 10⁻⁶ mmHg⁻¹·sec⁻¹, obtained by averaging the k values from both experiments.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference: k_av = 7.9 × 10⁻⁶ mm⁻¹·sec⁻¹.
provenance.discriminates: A response that reports only one k value or an incorrect average would not match this final rate constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; final value for the rate constant sub-question.

validation.gold_why: Average k=7.9e-6 reported.

items.title: Arrhenius T1 and Ea
items.description: Converts the temperature 500°C to 773 K for use as T1 and the activation energy of 180 kJ to 180000 J for consistency with R = 8.314 J·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹ in the Arrhenius equation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Consensus: T1 = 773 K (or 773.15 K) used in Arrhenius calculation.
provenance.discriminates: A response plugging 500 directly into the Arrhenius equation would obtain a nonsensical T2 ≈ 503 K.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; incorrect T1 or Ea units derail the final answer.

validation.gold_why: Uses 773 K as T1.

items.title: R = 8.314 used
items.description: Uses the gas constant R = 8.314 J·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹ in the Arrhenius equation.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference and all rollouts use R = 8.314.
provenance.discriminates: A response using a different R value (e.g., 0.0831 in L·bar units) would produce an incorrect T2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives but basic setup step already implied by item 12.

validation.gold_why: R=8.314 used in Arrhenius.

items.title: ln 2 as k ratio
items.description: Uses ln 2 as the ratio k2/k1 in the two-point Arrhenius equation, since the rate constant is to be twice its value at 500°C.

provenance.discriminates: A response using a different ratio (e.g., ln 1 = 0, or 2 instead of ln 2) would solve for a different T2.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; sets up the equation that yields the final temperature.

validation.gold_why: ln 2 used as k ratio.

items.title: T2 approximately 793 K
items.description: Reports the final temperature T2 as approximately 793 K (≈ 520°C) at which the rate constant will be twice its value at 500°C.

provenance.discriminates: A response with a sign error in the Arrhenius equation would obtain T2 < 773 K, and one using Celsius or unconverted Ea would obtain entirely different values.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; directly answers the third requested quantity.

validation.gold_why: T2≈793 K (520°C) reported.

items.title: Avoids wrong k units
items.description: Avoids reporting the rate constant k in concentration-based units (e.g., M⁻¹·s⁻¹) or first-order units (s⁻¹) instead of the pressure-based mmHg⁻¹·sec⁻¹ required by this pressure data.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Rate-constant units mismatch': solvers may report k in s⁻¹ (first-order) or mol⁻¹·L·s⁻¹ instead of mmHg⁻¹·s⁻¹.
provenance.discriminates: A response reporting k in s⁻¹ or mol⁻¹·L·s⁻¹ units would be dimensionally inconsistent with the second-order pressure-based derivation.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 1/1 negatives; common unit error when pressure data drives a second-order rate law.

validation.gold_why: k units given as mm⁻¹·sec⁻¹.

items.description: The response selects choice (b) as the correct answer for how to build a car to reduce the likelihood of injury in a head-on collision.

items.title: Work-energy identity
items.description: The response frames the problem using work-energy, stating that the integral of force over distance (∫F dx) equals the kinetic energy mv₀²/2 that must be dissipated.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts used impulse-momentum (maximize Δt) as the primary framework; the reference uses work-energy (∫F dx = mv₀²/2) and explicitly calls the momentum approach trickier.
provenance.discriminates: A response that only uses F_avg = Δp/Δt and never mentions spreading force over distance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; core framework without which the answer is unjustified.

validation.gold_why: Frames problem via ∫F dx equaling kinetic energy mv₀²/2.

items.title: Integral is collision-invariant
items.description: The response states that the integral ∫F dx is fixed at the magnitude mv₀²/2 because the occupant ends at rest, independent of the specifics of the collision.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference states this integral takes on the given value mv₀²/2 in magnitude, independent of collision specifics; no rollout mentioned this.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats the total energy or force integral as variable depending on design.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the invariance is the key constraint enabling the design principle.

validation.gold_why: States ∫F dx fixed at mv₀²/2, independent of collision specifics.

items.title: Spread force over distance
items.description: The response states that to reduce injury, the force should be spread out evenly over the largest possible crumpling distance rather than spiked over a small interval.

provenance.evidence_detail: All rollouts maximized collision time; the reference argues the goal is to spread F over the largest possible range of x.
provenance.discriminates: A response that says the goal is only to maximize collision duration without mentioning spreading force over distance.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; the central design principle that directly motivates choice (b).

validation.gold_why: States force should spread evenly over largest possible x range.

items.title: (b) yields constant force
items.description: The response explains that option (b) spreads the force evenly across the crumpling distance because the front crumples when large forces are applied, maintaining a roughly constant decelerating force.

provenance.evidence_detail: The 'stopping one step early' pitfall: rollouts selected (b) but justified it only with extended collision time, not with the even force-profile argument.
provenance.discriminates: A response that selects (b) but justifies it only with 'extends time' rather than explaining the spread-out force profile.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; connects the physics principle to the specific correct choice.

validation.gold_why: States (b) spreads force evenly over largest distance.

items.title: Option (a) bumper too short
items.description: The response explains that option (a) involves only the front bumper, which is a small fraction of the total possible crumpling distance, making it hardly different from a completely rigid car.

provenance.evidence_detail: The reference distinguishes (a) from (d) by noting the bumper is only a small fraction of crumpling distance; all rollouts lumped (a) and (d) together.
provenance.discriminates: A response that treats (a) and (d) as identical rigid designs.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; required rejection of a plausible-but-wrong sub-option.

validation.gold_why: Explains (a) involves only bumper, small fraction of crumpling distance.

items.title: Option (c) spikes at end
items.description: The response explains that option (c) leads to a force spike at the end of the collision because the front crumples too easily under small forces, providing little deceleration early on.

provenance.discriminates: A response that justifies rejecting (c) only with structural integrity or normal-driving concerns.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; absorbs pitfall items 12 and 15 which restated this point.

validation.gold_why: States (c) leads to spike at end of collision.

items.title: Option (d) spikes at beginning

items.title: Avoids conflating (a) and (d)

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; deep insight about why the momentum framework is trickier.

provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; explains why energy, not impulse, is the preferred approach.

items.title: Constant F(t) is ideal

provenance.discriminates: A response that claims the ideal force profile has any shape other than constant.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; elegant tie-back to why spreading force evenly is optimal.

validation.gold_why: Identifies constant F(t) as ideal to minimize maximum force.

items.title: Final ⟨U⟩ formula
items.description: States the mean internal energy expression ⟨U⟩ = ∂(βF)/∂β in terms of the free energy F, including both the additive F term and the β ∂F/∂β term that arise from the product rule.

provenance.evidence_detail: Mined pitfall 'Sign of mean energy' (high severity, foreseen): the chain of two minus signs tempts an incorrect overall negative sign.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ⟨U⟩ = -∂(βF)/∂β anywhere in the derivation, even if the final answer is later corrected.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core reference result; absorbed pitfall items 16,17 covering observed sign and drop-F errors.

validation.gold_why: Uses positive sign, not negative.

items.title: Final ⟨S⟩ formula
items.description: States the entropy expression ⟨S⟩ = β² ∂F/∂β in terms of the free energy F, retaining both powers of β and including no explicit k_B factor multiplying this formula.

provenance.evidence_detail: All three rollouts included an explicit Boltzmann constant (k_B or k) in ⟨S⟩ = k_B β² ∂F/∂β, but the reference gives ⟨S⟩ = β² ∂F/∂β with k absorbed into β.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ⟨S⟩ = k_B β² ∂F/∂β or ⟨S⟩ = k β² ∂F/∂β, which every rollout did.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Core result; caught 3/3 negatives — highest measured discrimination, essential for correctness.

validation.gold_why: States ⟨S⟩ = β² ∂F/∂β with no k_B factor.

items.title: ln Z_N = −βF relation
items.description: States or uses the relation ln Z_N = −βF (equivalently F = −(1/β) ln Z_N) connecting the canonical partition function to the free energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires derivation from Z_N = e^{-βF}; all rollouts used this relation and consensus_correct confirms it.
provenance.discriminates: A response that attempts the derivation without ever invoking the link between Z_N and F.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Foundational linking relation; gold=FAIL but structurally necessary for the derivation chain.

validation.gold_why: Relation ln Z_N = -βF not mentioned.

items.title: Derivative of Z_N to ⟨U⟩
items.description: Shows the intermediate derivative ∂Z_N/∂β = −Σ_φ E[φ] e^{−βE[φ]} and the resulting form ⟨U⟩ = −∂ ln Z_N/∂β, connecting the canonical partition function to the mean internal energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires showing steps; all rollouts performed this differentiation as the first step of the derivation.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps straight to the final formula without showing how differentiating Z_N produces the energy-weighted sum.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Merged intermediate steps; 0/3 discrimination but load-bearing for the derivation.

validation.gold_why: Intermediate derivative of Z_N not shown.

items.title: Product rule expansion
items.description: Expands ∂(βF)/∂β using the product rule to obtain F + β ∂F/∂β as the expression for the mean internal energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires showing steps; the product rule expansion is the link from -∂ ln Z_N/∂β to ∂(βF)/∂β.
provenance.discriminates: A response that writes ∂(βF)/∂β as the final answer but never shows the F + β ∂F/∂β expansion.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Required intermediate linking free energy to internal energy; gold=FAIL, moderate weight.

validation.gold_why: Product rule expansion not shown.

items.title: Thermodynamic identity for S
items.description: Uses the thermodynamic relation F = ⟨U⟩ − T⟨S⟩ (i.e., ⟨S⟩ = (⟨U⟩ − F)/T) as the starting point for deriving the entropy expression.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (b) requires deriving ⟨S⟩ from F = U - TS; consensus_correct confirms all rollouts used this structure.
provenance.discriminates: A response that derives ⟨S⟩ from a different starting point or simply states the entropy formula without using F = ⟨U⟩ - T⟨S⟩.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Necessary starting identity for the entropy derivation; 0/3 discrimination but structurally required.

validation.gold_why: Thermodynamic identity for S not used.

items.title: Intermediate ⟨S⟩ form
items.description: Shows the intermediate expression ⟨S⟩ = β(⟨U⟩ − F) before arriving at the final β² ∂F/∂β form, where ⟨U⟩ is the mean internal energy and F is the free energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires showing steps; the intermediate ⟨S⟩ = β(⟨U⟩ - F) bridges the thermodynamic identity to the statistical expression.
provenance.discriminates: A response that jumps from F = ⟨U⟩ - T⟨S⟩ directly to ⟨S⟩ = β² ∂F/∂β without showing the intermediate rearrangement.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; critical intermediate bridging thermodynamics to final entropy formula.

validation.gold_why: Intermediate ⟨S⟩ form not shown.

items.title: Substitution into ⟨S⟩
items.description: Shows the explicit substitution of ⟨U⟩ − F = β ∂F/∂β into ⟨S⟩ = β(⟨U⟩ − F) to obtain ⟨S⟩ = β² ∂F/∂β, where F is the free energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Sub-question (c) requires showing steps; this substitution is the final algebraic step linking ⟨U⟩ and ⟨S⟩ derivations.
provenance.discriminates: A response that states both ⟨S⟩ = β(⟨U⟩ - F) and ⟨S⟩ = β² ∂F/∂β but never shows how one transforms into the other.
provenance.calibration_rationale: Caught 3/3 negatives; substitution completing the entropy derivation with high discriminative value.

validation.gold_why: Substitution step not shown.

items.title: Step 1 energy reasoning
items.description: The response identifies that half the atoms of X lose one electron (costing IP per atom) while the remaining half gain one electron (releasing EA per atom), giving a net cost of IP − EA per transfer pair.

items.description: The response writes the step 1 energy balance as (N/2)×(IP − EA) = 409 kJ, with EA subtracted because electron attachment releases energy.

provenance.evidence_detail: Reference and correct rollouts use IP − EA for step 1; pitfall EA-sign-in-step-1 addresses the wrong move of adding EA.
